Plan-owned packaged acceptance: [launch-environment live check](2026-10-13-opencode-launch-environment_livetest.md),
sharing the original owner's two open UI steps; record one live run there and link its evidence back.
Deferred-check record: the exact procedure is recorded inline in
[Deferred packaged acceptance](#lt-704-deferred-packaged-acceptance) below so any checkout of
this branch can follow it; the untracked root-checkout
[startup remediation live test](2026-10-13-opencode-startup-remediation_livetest.md) (active
`_livetest.md`, never committed) is the identical campaign/evidence copy.

### Observed behaviour

After James rebuilt and restarted Harness, provider-default thinking still failed for session
`ix0iunga7` in `~/work/12steps`, OpenCode `xiaomi-token-plan-ams/mimo-v2.6-pro`, explicitly routed
to local Amsterdam account ComTechSpare (`comtechspare-f7a6`). Packaged-app High thinking was not tested.
The installed archive contains the prior effort-only variant repair, including the `Map` projection;
this is a distinct reproduced failure after that repair, not evidence that its projection regressed.

`app.log` lines 27455, 27457 and 27458–27459 record startup at 17:38:06.816 UTC, fallback to
another OpenCode install of major 2 at 17:38:08.011 UTC, and initialization failure at
17:38:09.553 UTC. The retained-session error has `textChars: 92` and
`textHash: 7d9b0dca8f11b1bd`, which identifies the static
`Unable to confirm the selected model for its configured generation budget; refusing startup.`
message in `acp-generation-budget-selection.ts`, not the native-config probe error.
Per-check timestamps and installed-build provenance remain in the owning live test.

### Root cause

The actual factory supplies caller environment overrides, not a complete inherited environment,
to `listOpenCodeCommandCandidates`. That function passes the overrides-only object straight into
`buildCliSpawnOptions` for `which -a opencode`. Without inherited `HOME`/`PATH`, discovery misses
the working NVM OpenCode 1.19.0 and sees the stale Homebrew install plus desktop OpenCode 2.
The later native probe/spawn merges `getSafeEnvForTrustedProcess()` with caller overrides, so
discovery and execution use different environment semantics.

The factory then selects desktop OpenCode 2. Its native model options include the region's
`xiaomi-token-plan-ams` models, but not the requested derived
`aio-mimo-comtechspare-f7a6/mimo-v2.6-pro` account model. The post-session generation-budget
guard correctly refuses startup rather than allowing an unconfirmed account/model.

The implementing agent reproduced this through the actual factory with an overrides-only
environment. Supplying inherited `HOME` selected the NVM CLI, confirmed the exact routed
ComTechSpare model and reached adapter ready. These experiments sent no model prompt and
do not count as a packaged-app reply or High-thinking acceptance pass.

Reproducer: `_scratch/opencode-real-startup.ts`. The before-fix options-only run exited 1;
`--inherit-home` reached ready without a prompt and exited 0. After the source merge repair,
both normal `--prompt` and `--high --prompt` source-runtime runs exited 0 and confirmed the
exact routed account/model and requested effort (`modelConfirmed: true`, `effortConfirmed: true`,
`responseIsOK: true`). Safe retained outputs: `_scratch/opencode-launch-runtime-default.log`
and `_scratch/opencode-launch-runtime-high.log`. Packaged-app High thinking remains unrun;
the installed/restarted packaged checks remain open.

Focused verification passed eight spec files / 181 tests (`_scratch/test-run.opencode-launch-focused.log`).
Temporarily removing only the source fix made the new regressions fail, exit 1
(`_scratch/opencode-launch-regression-red.log`); the implementing agent restored the repaired source.
Typecheck, spec typecheck, lint, length ratchet, main build and renderer build exited 0
(`_scratch/opencode-launch-{types,spec-types,lint,length,main,renderer}.log`). The guard is unchanged.
The actual compiled JavaScript factory also passed both real default and High-thinking prompts,
exit 0 (`_scratch/opencode-launch-compiled-default.log`, `_scratch/opencode-launch-compiled-high.log`).
Both safe results record `compiled: true`, `modelConfirmed: true`, `effortConfirmed: true`,
and `responseIsOK: true`; the second records `high: true`. The implementation coordinator's
pinned no-cache full suite passed, and independent fresh review returned PASS with no
actionable findings. Code remediation is verified; this item stays open for packaged acceptance.
Both installed/restarted packaged acceptance checks remain pending.

The initial full-suite run exited 1 with exactly two SEA build-repeatability spec failures:
the shell used Homebrew Node 26.3, whose binary lacked the SEA fuse, rather than `.nvmrc`'s
pinned Node 24.15.0. Both affected SEA specs passed under the installed pinned version, without

(`_scratch/opencode-launch-pinned-{types,spec-types,lint,length,main,renderer}.log`).
The implementation coordinator's pinned no-cache full suite exited 0: 2,420 files,
31,276 tests passed, six skipped (`_scratch/opencode-launch-full-pinned.log`; raw
`_scratch/test-run.opencode-launch-full-pinned.log`).

Independent report `_scratch/opencode-launch-fresh-gate.md`: **VERDICT: PASS**, no actionable
findings. The fresh reviewer independently reran all six canonical non-test gates, eight focused
spec files / 181 tests, compiled default/High actual replies, and the full no-cache suite under

This verdict covers the scoped launcher code repair on the shared dirty checkout; no

The committed implementation was re-verified in queue worktree

### Required behaviour

Candidate discovery uses the same trusted inherited environment plus caller overrides as native
probe/spawn. Inherited `HOME` and `PATH` allow the normal NVM CLI to be discovered; explicit
caller overrides retain precedence. The launched adapter confirms the exact derived routed
account/model before starting a budgeted turn. Keep the guard fail-closed: a native region model
is not confirmation of the requested account model, and no silent account fallback is permitted.

### Acceptance

- A focused regression proves inherited `HOME`/`PATH` reach the candidate-discovery subprocess
  when the caller supplies only overrides, and proves explicit caller overrides still win.

### Deferred packaged acceptance (branch-recorded procedure)

## LT-705 — OpenCode 1 cannot open a folder whose shared database OpenCode 2 changed, and the OpenCode 2 fallback cannot honour per-session settings

**Status: machine repair applied and verified 2026-10-13; code change implemented, canonical gates and full suite pass, independent reviews PASS with advisory notes addressed; queue re-verified 2026-10-14; install/restart prerequisite satisfied 2026-10-14; the communitytech packaged smoke remains unrun and deferred — not confirmed fixed live.**
Origin: the LT-704 packaged provider-default check, run by James on 2026-10-13 at 20:22 UTC
(21:22 BST) in `~/work/communitytech` ([launch-environment live check](2026-10-13-opencode-launch-environment_livetest.md)).
Implementation status: [active startup remediation plan](2026-10-13-opencode-startup-remediation_plan.md)
(untracked root-checkout working document; lands as `2026-10-13-opencode-startup-remediation_plan_completed.md` at close).
Deferred-check record: the exact procedure is recorded inline in
[Deferred packaged acceptance](#lt-705-deferred-packaged-acceptance) below so any checkout of
this branch can follow it; the untracked root-checkout
[startup remediation live test](2026-10-13-opencode-startup-remediation_livetest.md) (active
`_livetest.md`, never committed) is the identical campaign/evidence copy.

### Observed behaviour

The installed archive was built at 20:17 UTC and contains the LT-704 discovery repair. Session
`icott8xxw` (`~/work/communitytech`, OpenCode `xiaomi-token-plan-ams/mimo-v2.6-pro`, routed by
default to ComTechSpare `comtechspare-f7a6`) logged `OpenCodeCliLaunch` "OpenCode CLI could not
read its database; using another install" `{major: 2}` at 20:22:27 UTC, then failed at 20:22:28
with `textChars: 92`, `textHash: 7d9b0dca8f11b1bd`: the same selected-model confirmation refusal
as LT-704. James's screenshot shows the 13:35 BST message timestamp and the native-config probe
error (`textChars: 89`, `textHash: 1f2fc4ca0fb107ff`, logged for `i1sevv0tp` at 12:35 UTC), so the
restored session appears to display its earlier error. That UI detail was not separately verified.

### Root cause

Each step was reproduced without sending a model prompt and without printing native values.

1. **OpenCode 1 cannot open this folder.** NVM OpenCode 1.19.0, the newest 1.x on npm, exits 1
   with `no such column: project_id` in `~/work/communitytech` (`debug config`, `models`), but
   works in `/`, `~`, ai-orchestrator and 12steps. Desktop OpenCode 2.0.18 shares
   `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` and has rebuilt `workspace` as
   `(id, provider, binding, created_at, last_used_at)`; OpenCode 1's schema has
   `workspace.project_id`. On an APFS clone of the database, adding a nullable
   `workspace.project_id` alone made OpenCode 1 start in communitytech. Clearing the project's
   `sandboxes` or deleting its duplicate project row did not. LT-704's discovery repair therefore
   found the right CLI, which then failed in this folder, and selection fell back to OpenCode 2.
2. **OpenCode 2 sessions ignore the per-spawn overlay.** OpenCode 2's `acp` command takes no
   options (`--standalone` and `--server` are rejected) and attaches to the shared background
   service (`opencode-cli serve --service`). A probe overlay that defined a provider with a
   placeholder key was visible to an OpenCode 1 ACP session and invisible to an OpenCode 2 one.
   The running service's `GET /api/config` held an inline document with `agents`, `permissions`
   and an `aio-mimo-comtechspare-f7a6` provider: a frozen copy from whichever process started the
   service. The pre-spawn probe (`api --standalone GET /api/config`) reads a private server that
   does see the overlay, so the permission and generation-budget assertions passed against
   settings the session never used. This affects every OpenCode 2 session, not only routed accounts.
3. **OpenCode 2 has no key for the second account.** OpenCode 2 keeps credentials in the
   database `credential` table, which held only `xiaomi-token-plan-ams` (row created 2026-09-26).
   OpenCode 1's `auth.json` holds both accounts. Harness's account sign-in command runs
   `opencode auth login -p …`, which is OpenCode 1 syntax. The OpenCode 2 ACP session listed only
   the eight `xiaomi-token-plan-ams` models, and `session/set_config_option` answered
   `-32602 model not found: aio-mimo-comtechspare-f7a6/mimo-v2.6-pro`. The guard correctly refused.

Reproducers: `_scratch/mimo-second-account/repro.ts` (routed handshake per CLI),
`overlay-test.ts` (overlay visibility), `app-path.ts` (actual factory startup, no prompt) and
`refusal.ts` (selection against the real OpenCode 2 install).

### Repair

- **Machine, 2026-10-13 about 20:40 UTC:** `ALTER TABLE workspace ADD COLUMN project_id text` on the
  shared OpenCode database, after an APFS clone backup at
  `~/.local/share/opencode-backups/2026-10-13-before-workspace-column`. Undo with
  `ALTER TABLE workspace DROP COLUMN project_id`. Verified on a clean clone first: OpenCode 1
  `debug config`, and OpenCode 2 `api --standalone GET /api/config`, `/api/session`,
  `/api/project` and `session list`, all exit 0. On the live database, OpenCode 1 opens
  communitytech, 12steps, binsout, one-more-floor and ai-orchestrator, and the live OpenCode 2
  service still lists sessions and projects. The actual factory then started ComTechSpare in
  communitytech on OpenCode 1 and confirmed `aio-mimo-comtechspare-f7a6/mimo-v2.6-pro`. A future
  OpenCode 2 migration that rebuilds `workspace` would undo this repair.
- **Code (James approved "both" follow-ups):** `selectOpenCodeLaunch` reads `--version` first,
  which does not open the database, skips any install newer than `MAX_SUPPORTED_OPENCODE_MAJOR`
  (1), and refuses startup before any ACP spawn with a plain message when no OpenCode 1 install
  can print its config. The OpenCode 2 branches in the adapter factory remain but are inactive.

### Implementation status update — 2026-10-14 (Plan Queue worker)

Queue worktree `queue/2026-10-13-opencode-startup-re-bf56b9` re-verified the committed code with
no changes (19 OpenCode spec files / 325 tests, six canonical gates, builds, generators —
receipts `_scratch/opencode-startup-remediation-queue-worker-20261014-bf56b9/`). The machine
repair still holds: OpenCode 1 `debug config` exits 0 in `~/work/communitytech` and
`~/work/12steps` (output discarded). The installed archive (2026-10-14 13:00:28 UTC) contains
both repairs with a compiled launcher byte-identical to the worktree build, and the production
app booted 13:08:32 UTC after that install, so the install/restart prerequisite is satisfied.
The communitytech packaged smoke needs session creation in the packaged app UI (no
agent-reachable surface; desktop control hard-denied) and its deferred procedure (exact steps)
is recorded inline in
[Deferred packaged acceptance](#lt-705-deferred-packaged-acceptance) below and mirrored in the
untracked root-checkout
[startup remediation live test](2026-10-13-opencode-startup-remediation_livetest.md).
No packaged live pass is claimed.

### Required behaviour

Harness never starts an OpenCode session on a version whose session ignores the per-spawn overlay.
When no supported install works, it refuses before spawning, naming the cause without native
output, paths or credentials. Routed-account model confirmation stays fail-closed.

### Acceptance

- Focused regressions: OpenCode 2 is never selected and its `debug config` never runs; a lone
  OpenCode 2 install, a broken OpenCode 1 install and no install each give the right plain
  message; LT-704's inherited-environment discovery tests still pass.
- The actual factory starts ComTechSpare in `~/work/communitytech` on OpenCode 1 and confirms the
  exact account model without a prompt.
- Canonical gates and an independent completion review pass.
- Packaged: after installing and restarting a build containing this change, a ComTechSpare
  session in `~/work/communitytech` starts and replies. This shares the LT-704 packaged checks.

## LT-706 — a MiMo step that exhausts the combined cap on reasoning ends the session silently

**Status: fixed and regression-tested 2026-10-14; live-verified 2026-11-11 with real MiMo generation (both checks in the live-test document passed).**
Origin: James's live session `ivx7upc8u` (installed app, OpenCode 1.19.0,
`aio-mimo-comtechspare-f7a6/mimo-v2.6-pro`), 2026-10-14 20:39–21:41 BST.
Plan: [2026-10-14-mimo-reasoning-cap-cutoff_plan_completed.md](2026-10-14-mimo-reasoning-cap-cutoff_plan_completed.md).

### Observed behaviour

- OpenCode session `ses_ec4126b42ffemKuqDOJBnet17O` records three consecutive assistant steps
  with `finish: "length"`: output 0 + reasoning 16388 (21:21:59 BST), output 1 + reasoning 16383
  (21:29:16 BST), and output 0 + reasoning 16386 (21:41:26 BST, after James's manual
  "continue"). Earlier tool-call steps used up to about 12.7k reasoning tokens each.
- `app.log`: all three `ACP turn completed` lines report `stopReason: "end_turn"`,
  `classifierReason: "completed"`, `generationBudget.combinedOutputTokens: 16384`. The shared
  `ProviderTurnEnding` line reclassified the first as `dangling_tool_result` (one automatic
  continuation); the other two stayed `completed`. No notice, no further continuation; the
  session went idle each time, so the manual "continue" also appeared to do nothing.

### Root cause

`outputBudgetSaturated` (`src/main/cli/turn-ending-classifier.ts`, added for LT-690) returned false
for empty text and otherwise required the whole-turn text to end unfinished. ACP usage covers only
the final provider step, so a step cut off while reasoning after earlier finished narration, or
with no text at all, read as a normal completion. `AdapterTurnEndingObservation` reclassifies
without `combinedOutputTokenCap`, and its `dangling_tool_result` overrides the adapter ending.

### Required behaviour

A non-error completion with no open tool call whose final-step output + reasoning reaches the
injected cap (within tolerance) is `max_output / budget_saturated` when the final step's visible
output is within tolerance or the turn text is empty or unfinished. The cap is also read from the
adapter's `generationBudget` metadata so both classification layers agree, and saturation takes
precedence over an unanswered tool result. Failure and transient-error signals keep
saturation out, so a failed turn is never auto-continued.

### Acceptance

- Regression tests for the zero-text, earlier-narration, metadata-cap/dangling, metadata-usage,
  runtime observation and `acp-turn-completion` cases fail on the previous classifier and pass; negative cases (finished answer,
  open tool, error, empty under cap) stay out of saturation.
- Live: [MiMo reasoning-cap live checks](2026-10-14-mimo-reasoning-cap-cutoff_livetest.md). Met 2026-11-11 ("Evidence run — 2026-11-11"): a real ordinary turn completed with cap 32000 and no continuation; three real `finish: length` steps were classified `max_output / budget_saturated`, with exactly two automatic continuations and the visible notices.

## LT-707 — benchmark runner loses a scored run when workspace cleanup flakes

Scope note: this defect is in the experiment harness (`benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/`), not app
code. It was reproduced while running deferred check A6 of
[2026-10-14-local-model-plan-execute-ab_plan_livetest.md](2026-10-14-local-model-plan-execute-ab_plan_livetest.md)
and is tracked/remediated in the active plan
[2026-10-14-local-model-plan-execute-ab_plan.md](2026-10-14-local-model-plan-execute-ab_plan.md)
(same pattern as LT-704/LT-705 being tracked in their active plan). It is registered here
because the operating rule requires every reproduced defect to be indexed before it is fixed.

### Observed behavior

2026-10-24, `runner.ts run --local-only --phase pilot --session pilot-2026-10-15 --arms C1
--tasks AIO-03,...,12ST-04`: the AIO-05 coder run completed and the runner had captured its
patch, applied hidden tests and scored it, then aborted with `run failed: ENOTEMPTY, Directory
not empty: '<workRoot>/AIO-05-C1-1'` before `appendRunRecord`. The scored run left no
`runs.jsonl` record (the batch matrix lost the cell and the batch exits 1), and the leftover
workspace directory makes the re-run fail with `workspace already exists`.

### Root cause

`runArm` (`benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/runner.ts`) runs `cleanupWorkspace(workspace.dir)`
between scoring and building/writing the RunRecord. `cleanupWorkspace`
(`benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/task-export.ts`) is a bare `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true,
force: true })`; Node's recursive removal can fail transiently with ENOTEMPTY/EBUSY (removal
races — files appearing during rm, e.g. `.DS_Store` on macOS). Because cleanup runs before the
record write, any such flake discards a fully completed run and misreports it as "failed before
scoring".

### Required behavior

1. A run that reached scoring always persists its RunRecord (and patch), whatever happens to its
   throwaway workspace afterwards.
2. Workspace cleanup tolerates transient removal races (bounded retries) and never turns a
   completed run into a batch failure; a persistent leftover is reported as a warning/note.
3. A leftover workspace from a crashed/killed run still refuses silent reuse (existing
   behaviour) but the error identifies the stale directory for manual clearing.

### Acceptance

- Regression tests pin: (a) the run record is appended even when cleanup throws; (b)
  `cleanupWorkspace` retries through a transient ENOTEMPTY and then succeeds; (c) a cleanup
  failure that persists is surfaced as a note/warning without dropping the record.
- The AIO-05 C1 cell is re-run and recorded normally after the fix; the benchmark suite and the
  canonical static gates stay green.

## LT-782 — refreshing during MiMo renewal cooldown hides an unresolved expired-login warning

Numbering note (2026-10-27): the original MiMo LT-708 assignment conflicted with the benchmark reservation. The initial root and queue plan-directory scan at approximately 04:23 UTC confirmed LT-782 was unallocated; this MiMo record uses that number. A later review found a separate LT-790 reservation without an LT-782 conflict. Its earlier evidence retains the original timestamps; no other defect is renumbered.

Status: fixed and verified live 2026-10-27; canonical gates and fresh independent completion review PASS. No unresolved acceptance item. Implementation status: [active follow-up plan](2026-10-27-mimo-stale-session-warning_plan.md). The older 2026-07-19 plan remains closed; new work is recorded in this follow-up under the completed-document rule.

### Observed behaviour

In the isolated rebuilt dev app, omitted outgoing console cookies produce real MiMo 401 responses. Omitting outgoing account cookies for the failed-renewal case reaches the real Xiaomi sign-in page, and the quota retry still receives 401. At 02:49:54 UTC, cached token bars remain and the chip shows OC 94% plus a warning; one quota-reauth notification records desktop delivery. A second real Refresh at 02:50:14 UTC again receives 401, but the renewer is on cooldown: the cached snapshot changes needsReauth from true to false and the warning disappears. No successful quota response intervenes. Evidence: rejected-refresh-one.json, rejected-refresh-two.json and rejected-network-two.json in 2026-09-25-mimo-session-resilience_evidence/2026-10-27-round2/.

### Root cause

MimoTokenPlanProbe returns a windowless transient failure when renewal is unavailable (including cooldown). ProviderQuotaService.retainLastKnownQuotaWindows defaults its absent needsReauth flag to false and drops the prior sign-in instruction. The IPC listener consequently resets its one-shot transition tracking despite no evidence that authentication recovered.

### Required behaviour

A windowless failure with no authentication verdict preserves the previous warning, original instruction, cached bars and original takenAt. An authoritative successful snapshot, explicit false verdict, configuration exclusion or source invalidation can replace that state. Repeated refreshes of the same unresolved expiry issue only one quota-reauth notification.

### Acceptance

- Live rejection plus repeated Refresh retains two cached token bars, their age and warning; exactly one quota-reauth notification is delivered.
- A real saved-SSO walk followed by successful native quota responses clears the warning, advances takenAt and writes the renewal-success log. The 04:26 UTC correction run excludes the original service token from every renewal-phase request: SSO-returned authentication alone gets 200; identity-only negative controls get 401; a persisted-session reread gets 200 again. See the owning live-test report and its `2026-10-27-review-fixes` receipts. Natural expiry was not induced.
- Service regressions cover preserved state, successful and explicit-false replacement, and account isolation; existing healthy-cache and source-invalidation tests remain green. Canonical gates and fresh independent review pass.

## LT-1008 — session account dropdown initially selects a different account from its chip

_Renumbered from LT-710 on 2026-11-08 during the merge with main, which already uses LT-710 for another defect. The 2026-10-27 receipts keep the original number._

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27, live worktree dev app, focus emulation enabled and `document.hidden === false`.
A real OpenCode/MiMo session was explicitly created on `comtechspare-f7a6` (label MiMo Test B).
After both chips finished loading their two options, the header and composer each displayed
MiMo Test B. Their component inputs, `currentProfileId()` and `selectedValue()` all held
`comtechspare-f7a6`, but each actual `HTMLSelectElement.value` was `legacy` and its first
option (MiMo Test A) had `selected === true`. A second read confirmed the mismatch.
After the subsequent real automatic switch to legacy, the selects agreed with that new value.
Evidence: owning live-test document's 2026-10-27 run; `select-session.js.result.json` in its evidence
receipts. This is a rendered control-state defect; the actual backend account was B.

### Root cause

`src/renderer/app/shared/components/provider-account-chip.component.ts` binds the select's
`[value]` before the asynchronous account-list response creates its `@for` options. The
selected value is computed only from the session input and does not change when the options
arrive, so Angular does not write it again and the browser selects the first new option.
The live component signal/DOM mismatch confirms this execution path in both placements.

### Required behaviour

After accounts load or change order, the actual select must select the current account in
both header and composer. The visible label, keyboard selection and submitted account must
agree; merely assigning the DOM value in a live-test script is not a repair.

### Acceptance

- A meaningful delayed-account-list component regression starts on a non-first account and
  checks the native select's `value` and selected option after options appear.
- Live recreation of the MiMo session on its second account shows both selects on that account.
- Existing explicit switching, ownership confirmation/cancellation, draft and continuation
  selection behaviours remain intact, with the usual project gates and fresh independent review.

Implementation status, verifier follow-up 2026-10-27: option-level selected binding repairs
delayed creation in draft, session and continuation modes. The added delayed-list regressions
fail on the original implementation. Actual header/composer selected values now match B
([DOM receipt](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-10-27-queue-61bedf-r2/chips-ready.json)).
Independent review and the overall live-test campaign remain open.
The closed 2026-07-19 remediation plan remains untouched; new work is tracked in
`2026-10-27-mimo-account-state-remediation_plan.md` in the root checkout.

## LT-780 — documented Copilot account CLI reads double-wrap the authenticated request

**Status:** reproduced and repair implemented 2026-10-27; independent review pending.
The rebuilt CLI calls the real authenticated running parent successfully for all four methods.
The new spawned-CLI transport regression fails against the original source and passes with
the repair. Evidence: `2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/review2/cli-live.receipt.json`
and `transport-red-final` / `transport-green` receipts. Active implementation record:
[review corrections](2026-10-27-human-external-review2_plan.md#lt-780--lt-781-implementation-status).
Renumbered from the colliding campaign-local LT-710 to LT-780 after scanning every registered
checkout on 2026-10-27. The other campaigns' LT-710/LT-711 records are unrelated and preserved.

**Observed behaviour.** The injected, installed `AIO_MCP` executable's documented
`copilot-account list --json`, `rules --json`, and `doctor --json` all exit 1 with
`Unrecognized key: "payload"`. `route <current-worktree> --origin=automation --json`
also reports missing top-level `workingDirectory`. A second list call reproduces the failure.
No account mutation or login was attempted. The same authenticated parent transport, called
through the built repository client with the expected empty payload, succeeds and returns two
authenticated profiles. This distinguishes a malformed CLI request from missing authentication,
an unavailable parent, or absent Copilot profiles.

**Executing source path / root cause.** `src/main/mcp/copilot-account-cli.ts:133` calls
`client.call(method, { payload })`. `orchestrator-tools-rpc-client.ts:60` already wraps that
argument as `params.payload`. `orchestrator-tools-rpc-server.ts:377` passes it unchanged to
`dispatchCopilotAccountCliRpc`, whose strict empty/route schemas reject the extra wrapper
(`orchestrator-tools-rpc-copilot-account.ts:34`, `:43`). Existing CLI tests mock the transport
instead of joining it to dispatch, and even pin the nested wrapper in the route assertion
(`copilot-account-cli.spec.ts:44`); the focused suite remains green on the defective source.
The observed installed failure and the successful correct-shape control agree with this path;
this run does not claim the installed binary is byte-identical to the checkout.

**Required behaviour.** All four read verbs must pass the business payload once through the
existing authenticated client. Preserve strict request/response validation and the operator-only
boundary on account mutations. Do not relax a schema or add a compatibility adapter to accept
the malformed internal shape.

**Acceptance.** A real-client/dispatcher regression must exercise all four verbs, including route
origin, alongside unknown-key and response-leak refusals. After rebuild, the injected installed
CLI must return valid read-only results for list/rules/doctor/route against the running parent.
Recheck RES-020 and RES-021 account prerequisites without claiming their provider campaigns pass.

**Evidence.** Durable [campaign receipts](2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/REPORT.md),
`2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/run1/`:
`copilot-account.receipt.json`, `copilot-cli-repro.receipt.json`,
`copilot-direct-read.receipt.json`, `focused-tests.receipt.json`, `source-seal.json`.
The source hashes and authenticated replies are retained without transport capabilities,
socket values, profile homes or credentials. The root-owned residual document is the live owner.
The review retry reproduces all four malformed reads again; see
`review-round1/copilot-cli-recheck.receipt.json` in the same durable evidence directory.

`2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/review2/cli-live.receipt.json` and transport receipts.
Active implementation record:
[review corrections](2026-10-27-human-external-review2_plan.md#lt-780--lt-781-implementation-status).

**Observed behaviour.** Twice, the injected installed `aio-mcp settings list --json`, captured
through a pipe by `subprocess.run`, exits 0 with exactly 65,536 bytes and no stderr. Parsing fails
with `Unterminated string starting at: line 1868 column 11 (char 65493)`. No raw settings list is
retained. A regular-file stdout control returns valid JSON: 115,377 bytes, 224 settings. Running
the same compiled `runSettingsCli` with natural Node shutdown through a pipe also returns all
115,377 bytes; the two complete outputs have the same SHA-256. Small individual setting reads
continue to work. These controls rule out a truncated parent response or a JSON formatting error.

**Source-supported cause.** `src/main/mcp/settings-cli.ts:32` writes stdout without awaiting its
callback; the list path writes the complete serialization at `:45`. The outer dispatcher calls
`process.exit(code)` immediately after the async command returns
(`src/main/mcp/aio-mcp-dispatcher.ts:109`), without draining a piped stdout stream. The observed
pipe/file/natural-exit difference identifies premature exit as the repair target. This run does
not patch the dispatcher or claim other large-output command families have been live-tested.

**Required behaviour.** Successful CLI completion must preserve every stdout byte before exiting,
for pipes as well as regular files, while retaining nonzero error exits and clean MCP streams.
Keep secret-tier values redacted. Do not hide the defect by silently truncating results or
requiring callers to redirect to a file.

**Acceptance.** A spawned CLI/dispatcher test must write a harmless JSON result larger than the
pipe buffer, pipe it to a slow reader, parse the full result and assert exit status. Include
failure output/exit handling. After rebuild, the installed `settings list --json` must parse
through a pipe and match a regular-file capture; retain only hashes, lengths and setting counts.

**Evidence.** Durable [campaign receipts](2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/REPORT.md),
`2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/run1/`:
`settings-list-integrity.receipt.json`, `settings-stdout-controls.receipt.json`, `source-seal.json`.
Only redacted metadata, sizes, parse results and hashes are retained; temporary raw output was
closed and deleted immediately after the controls.
The review retry reproduces the same lengths and matching complete-output hashes; see
`review-round1/settings-pipe-recheck.receipt.json` in the same durable evidence directory.

## LT-890 — fresh-profile RLM initialization can leave the app without a window

**Status:** observed live on 27 October 2026; not fixed. The immediately subsequent launch with the same profile succeeded, as did this review's new fresh-profile first launch. Investigation has not identified the lock owner or established a repair. Active implementation status: [startup remediation plan](2026-10-27-residuals-startup-remediation_plan.md#lt-890-implementation-status). That untracked document lives in the root checkout for the coordinator.

### Observed behaviour

At 04:19:30.067 UTC, the rebuilt assigned checkout, launched with its isolated empty profile and debug port 9554, reports critical `Work controls` initialization failure: `SqliteError: database is locked`. The stack reaches `RLMDatabase.initializeDatabase` through `initializeGlobalPauseRuntime`. The process remains alive and its debug endpoint returns an empty target list; readiness of that endpoint alone was insufficient. The context worker also starts during this interval. After stopping the owned process and renderer and restarting against the same profile, the app initializes and exposes its real Angular renderer at 04:21:29–04:21:46 UTC. Focus-emulated DOM and animation-frame checks pass. No database or product source was patched for recovery.

### Root cause and uncertainty

The observed failing operation is `db.pragma('journal_mode = WAL')` at `src/main/persistence/rlm-database.ts:140`; the explicit busy timeout is installed later at line 144. Both main and the context worker initialize the same isolated database (`context-worker-main.ts:157–160`; `context-worker-client.ts:107–114`). Concurrent initial WAL/schema setup is a candidate cause, not a proven lock-owner attribution. No lock-owner trace or deterministic race reproduction was collected, so timeout ordering alone is not claimed as the complete cause.

**Review correction, 27 October.** `defaultDriverFactory` constructs better-sqlite3 without a
timeout override (`src/main/db/better-sqlite3-driver.ts:72`). Its JavaScript constructor defaults
to 5,000 ms (`node_modules/better-sqlite3/lib/database.js:34`), and the native constructor applies
`sqlite3_busy_timeout` before returning (`src/objects/database.cpp:172` in that installed package).
The connection therefore already has this timeout before RLM's pragmas. Moving the later pragma
alone is not an evidenced repair. The new fresh-profile first launch succeeded; the earlier
failure remains open with no identified lock owner or product-source change.
The compiled driver was also exercised in Electron Node mode against an in-memory database:
the initial busy timeout reads 5,000 ms and `SELECT 1` succeeds before any RLM configuration
pragma. See the [native control receipt](2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/review2/native-electron-control.receipt.json).

### Required behaviour

A new profile must initialize database ownership and critical Work controls safely with the context worker enabled. Contention must either settle within a bounded startup policy or produce a visible, actionable startup failure; the process must not remain running without an app window and only an unhandled rejection. Do not hide the error or change production data during remediation.

### Acceptance

1. Identify the actual competing connection and reproduce contention under ordinary startup without a stress generator.
2. Exercise compiled main/context-worker startup against fresh and existing isolated databases; verify the window and real IPC become ready.
3. Exercise bounded persistent contention and require an actionable visible error plus clean process teardown.
4. Preserve database contents and run focused database/worker regressions and canonical code gates for the eventual fix.

### Evidence

Retained under `2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/resume2/`: `startup-first/electron.log.txt`, startup/stop/build receipts, the successful second runtime receipts, and `ui-ready.receipt.json`. `id-reallocation.receipt.json` records the clear all-checkout search for LT-890. The initial proposed LT-790 was clear when scanned, then concurrently claimed by the MiMo campaign; its original allocation receipt and pre-cleanup seal remain historical, with this correction recorded in the current report. LT-782 was already owned by MiMo and was never allocated here. Other campaigns' records are untouched.

## LT-991 — persistence sentinel ignores the extension's serialized evaluate result

**Status:** reproduced live 27 October 2026; repair implemented in the queue checkout,
focused regressions pass. Packaged-coordinator live retest passed 11 November 2026 on an owned
Windows fixture: clean state `signalState:ok`; with the banner, `browser.type` refused
`browser_target_session_stale`, journal and `assert_persisted` (`persisted:false`) carry
`your session has expired` (evidence run in
[the livetest](2026-10-27-human-external-review2_livetest.md)). Not live-exercised: the
pre-dispatch refusal after an extension channel disconnect (source integration tests only).
Independent review pending.
Active implementation status: [review corrections](2026-10-27-human-external-review2_plan.md#lt-991-implementation-status).

**Observed behaviour.** An owned Windows-loopback session serves a save-on-type form. Only its
save socket is deliberately interrupted; no machine network or business tab is changed.
The page visibly reports `Your session has expired` in a `role=alert` region. After restoring
the fixture connection while retaining that banner, `browser.type` still returns `succeeded`
(audit `5fc3e94e-52c1-4340-86db-f4e4652b71eb`). Its journal records successful/unverified
writes, and `browser.assert_persisted` reports `persisted:true`, `confidence:verified`,
`signalState:unknown` (audit `3e23fdcb-6aae-4da9-810c-82aa1152d2cb`). A subsequent snapshot
still contains the expiry banner. No CAPTCHA, credential, real customer data or global network
change was involved. The owned tab, server, script and helper session were cleaned up.

**Executing path / root cause.** `resources/browser-extension/background.js:evaluateInTab`
returns `{type, json}` where `json` serializes the expression's value. This exact shape was
also captured from the real extension. `BrowserTargetPersistenceSentinel.scan` submits that
evaluate command, but `normalizeScanResult` only recognized a bare `{s,m}` or `{result:{s,m}}`.
It therefore returned unknown for both healthy and stale real-extension responses. The
existing mutation guards and persistence assertion consume that unknown state. The repair
decodes the existing wire format before classifying it, retaining unknown for malformed or
truncated results. No extension deployment or new browser capability is required.

**Required behaviour.** Real extension scan results must identify stale-session and failed-save
banners. A post-write scan must report the failed persistence verdict and journal entry;
the first post-disconnect write must be refused when the required pre-write scan is stale.
`browser.assert_persisted` must not report true when the alert scan identifies either failure.

**Acceptance.** Exercise actual serialized extension envelopes for ok/save_failed/session_stale,
including malformed/truncated data; drive mutation guard, journal and persistence-assertion
paths with that wire shape; rerun the owned live form against a rebuilt coordinator. Preserve
normal healthy writes and keep original human/credential escalation boundaries unchanged.

**Evidence.** `2026-10-27-human-external-residuals_evidence/review2/spa-stale-session.receipt.json`
contains the before/after snapshots, restored connection response, write journal and failing
assertion. `sentinel-baseline`, `sentinel-red`, `sentinel-green` and worker cleanup receipts
record the baseline, reproduced missing classification, repair checks and owned cleanup.

## LT-1013 — a completed Harness turn is replayed after provider compaction and leaves busy

_Renumbered on 2026-11-08 from LT-1007 (this compaction branch's number), because main already uses LT-1007 for another defect._

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27 isolated queue dev app, instance `xc2pqc2jt`, thread
`01a17b48-1f30-7b02-9823-4320bba44349`. A normal Harness send's turn
`01a17b4a-4782-7e51-87cd-dd9a1c542a20` completed at `1793069873524`. Before a raw
`thread/compact/start` request, runtime was idle but `pendingProviderFollow` retained that
turn's old `turn/started`. The raw Compact turn `01a17b4c-1969-7113-b2b7-9bd1dc6e2b94`
completed at `1793069951588`. At `1793069964832` the instance was busy and runtime actively
captured the already completed old turn with `origin: provider`; the pending field was now null.
This reproduces and explains the earlier rejected attempt's retained busy observation.

### Root cause

`followProviderTurn` saves the active Harness capture's own root `turn/started` as a pending
provider followup. A later provider capture finalizer replays it before the idle transition.
The first notification can arrive while runtime's current turn ID is still null; testing only
ID inequality would still queue that own turn. The raw Compact request exposes this latent
followup bug; bypassing the normal compaction request wrapper is not a reason to dismiss it.

### Required behaviour

Never follow a captured turn's own start again. Preserve a genuinely different provider turn
arriving while the preceding capture tears down. Real provider completion returns to idle once
all real work has ended.

### Acceptance

- Regression covers own start before/after turn/start acknowledgement, and preserves next-turn capture.
- Repeat the raw request after a normal Harness send; finished Compact turn leaves no active or
  pending old turn and returns idle.
- Focused tests, canonical gates and independent review pass; linked live criteria retain honest status.

Evidence: root-checkout
`2026-09-24-codex-compaction-turn-visibility_evidence/2026-10-27-round2/command-receipts.ndjson`
(`raw-repro.js` and subsequent `sample-short.js`). Implementation: linked active follow-up plan.

Final assistant output and real usage arrived before `item/started(contextCompaction)` at
`1793069831626`. The owned provider process group was suspended on that genuine event.
By `1793069831757` runtime was inactive and status idle although no compaction completion or
turn completion had arrived. At `1793069868027` the same inline compaction ID remained open.
The process group was resumed at `1793069868423`; actual item/turn completion arrived only at
`1793069873522`/`1793069873524`. The normal 30-minute hibernation setting was unchanged.
The 36.797-second hold already fails check 4's busy-state clause; it is not 35-minute evidence.

### Root cause

The final-answer inferred-completion timer disregards an active inline contextCompaction item.
It clears the captured turn while native provider work is still active. Inline compaction
intentionally opens no non-steerable Compact send gate, so that gate is not a suitable liveness
check.

keep inline steering available; settle normally on real completion or abort. Timer scheduling
and a timer already armed before item/started must both respect compaction ownership.

## LT-713 — queued send after compaction exposes two idle transitions

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27 instance `xs4v6yves`, thread `01a17b53-0cc8-7393-a368-68550ec92205`,
real inline compaction at 371,551/475,000 tokens (78.22%). One message was entered through
the real composer while compaction was held. The UI showed exactly one queued message and
explained that it would send after compaction. Item and owning turn completed at
`1793070689669`. Adapter emitted idle at `1793070689674`, then busy for the queued delivery
at `1793070690225`, then idle after that delivered turn. The message was delivered once and
no retry error occurred. This still fails check 1's exact single-idle acceptance; the prior
2026-10-04 observation of the same two-edge shape is no longer treated as a pass.

### Root cause

The renderer retains the queued message until the main provider turn reports idle. That idle
edge triggers queue drainage; the main process therefore ends the compaction's turn before
it knows about the renderer's next send. The current protocol does not retain ownership
across that queue-to-provider handoff.

### Required behaviour

Maintain busy ownership across an already queued post-compaction delivery, without releasing
idle eligibility between compaction and that delivery. End at idle once after the delivered
turn finishes. Do not hide or redefine main-process idle transitions in the evidence.

### Acceptance

- Real composer queues exactly one message during native compaction at >75% occupancy.
- One provider delivery, no retry error, continuous busy until its final completion, exactly
  one resulting idle transition.
- Queue cancellation, parking, unavailable providers and renderer restart still release or
  retain ownership correctly; no permanent busy reservation.

Durable evidence: same round2 directory, `inline-dom-watch.json`, `ui-main-state.js`
receipts and provider/lifecycle slices. No ownership-protocol change is included in the
scoped LT-1013/LT-1014 patch. The linked follow-up plan keeps this defect and check 1 open.

### Resume correction — 2026-10-27

The second coordinator checkpoint implements a bounded retained-busy handoff through
the durable queue admission. Rebuilt live instance `xo10trvoy` queued one composer
message during genuine inline compaction at 374,195/475,000 (78.78%). Native turn
completion at `1793074858775` led to a busy handoff at `1793074858782`, one next
native turn, and one final idle at `1793074865601`, without an intermediate main
idle. This verifies the single-idle correction. However the same delivered message
was restored and actually delivered again after a renderer reload: LT-715 remains
open, so check 1 is not closed. Evidence is in the owning live test's
`2026-10-27-resume/` receipts, DOM timeline and app/lifecycle slices. Full verification
also remains failed; no overall completion is claimed.


## LT-714 — the 15-minute notification budget prevents the 35-minute inline-compaction check

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27 rebuilt isolated app, instance `xjd5modv5`, thread
`01a17b52-bb67-7f10-9d9b-f2744f78b28e`, turn `01a17b53-4808-7a21-94a3-5271bb937f28`.
Native inline contextCompaction item started at `1793070421536`; the owned direct provider
process group was suspended on that real event to hold its work open. The instance stayed
busy with the same active capture for samples through elapsed 872,513 ms. At
`1793071321545` the transcript received `Codex error: Codex turn stalled: no notifications
received for 900000ms`; by `1793071321550` it was idle. At elapsed 902,684 ms, runtime capture
was gone while the inline compaction ID and live provider client remained. The watcher
failed its busy assertion and safely resumed the group at `1793071324379`. Only afterwards
did real item/turn completion arrive (`1793071329074` / `1793071329078`).

This is controlled no-notification fault injection, not proof that the service naturally
takes 15 or 35 minutes to compact. It does prove the current capture cannot satisfy the
written 35-minute busy requirement with a silent inline compaction. No hibernation occurred
during this shorter interval; the idle control did not reach its normal 30-minute threshold.

### Root cause

`runCapture` arms the notification-idle watchdog (`app-server-thread-runtime.ts:474-490`);
the configured active budget is 900,000 ms (`src/shared/constants/limits.ts:105`).
Inline compaction avoids the separate Compact wait gate but does not avoid this watchdog.
On rejection, its finally block releases the runtime capture, and the send failure is
surfaced. The LT-1014 inferred-completion fix correctly prevents the earlier 250ms release
but does not change this independent bounded silence policy.

### Required behaviour / investigation boundary

Reconcile a deliberately bounded 15-minute silent-provider policy with the original
35-minute active-compaction criterion. A valid resolution must preserve finite handling
of a dead provider and truthful compaction ownership. Do not lengthen clocks solely to
produce a pass, replay fake provider activity, or count the 907,539ms actual lifecycle
as a 2,100,000ms observation. No human identity or authority is missing.

### Acceptance

- Cover the actual inline-compaction/no-notification timeout boundary explicitly, including
  completion immediately before/after it and a lost provider transport.
- A qualifying genuine compaction remains active and busy for the full unchanged 35-minute
  test, or the owning acceptance is explicitly revised with a documented product rationale.
- Normal idle eligibility resumes after genuine completion, with an actual sweep control.

Evidence: round2 `watch-long.ndjson`, `watch-failure-resume.json`, `failed-watch-state.js`
receipt, lifecycle/app-log slices. Check 4 remains open; no timeout source was changed.

### Resume correction — 2026-10-27

The second coordinator checkpoint gives observed compaction a separate finite
2,400,000ms silence budget; ordinary active turns retain 900,000ms and explicit
shorter deadlines still cap both. Focused watchdog regressions pass, including
finite 40-minute expiry, ordinary-budget restoration and an explicit shorter limit.
This resumed worker did not change those source constants or the live app's clocks.

Genuine inline compaction `01a17b93-f9dc-7090-9882-d9894869dc6f` on isolated instance
`x9f8vy36o` was held through controlled suspension for 2,101,016ms, then genuinely
completed with recorded lifecycle duration 2,105,742ms. All 115 pre-completion samples
remain busy/active on the same thread and turn; main state stays busy until genuine
completion. Normal idle control `x87zwtbab` hibernated at `1793076396761` under the
unchanged 30-minute setting, while compaction remained active. At `1793076774577`,
the real next sweep considered the completed target as idle (7,594ms old), with
no compaction ID, async-work inhibitor or turn-ending marker; it correctly did not
hibernate a recently active session. Check 4 passes this controlled guard/eligibility
campaign. No natural 35-minute backend-computation claim or extra post-completion
30-minute hibernation claim is made. Full gates still fail for the dependency tree

## LT-715 — a delivered queued message is restored and sent again after renderer reload

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27 resumed queue campaign, isolated profile `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-5223ae4a`,
instance `xo10trvoy`, thread `01a17b92-7f73-71c0-b4b7-e19b737e999a`. Native inline
compaction began at `1793074824863`, after real usage 374,195/475,000 (78.78%).
A single composer send queued `Reply QUEUE_ACK_QUALIFIED only. Do not call tools or edit files.`
at `1793074830341`. The retained-busy handoff delivered it once, receiving its one reply
and one final idle at `1793074865601`. That part of LT-713 is live rechecked.

At `1793074970484` the durable queue still contained admission
`6117395e-8121-448b-a903-eec7a93a5867` in `promoting`, holding the exact 64-character
queued text. A different admission was `delivered`, with a 263-character enriched input.
The own dev renderer was reloaded at `1793074970851`. Without any further user send,
readback at `1793074986526` found **two** assistant replies, a second delivered admission
(266-character input), and the original admission still promoting. This is an actual
second provider delivery, not duplicated rendering of one assistant message.

### Root cause

The renderer persists the original text and explicitly promotes its admission. The
provider dispatch receipt calls `recordUserSend` with enriched `finalMessage`
(`instance-communication.ts`, `createInstanceInputReceipt`). `recordUserSend` only matches
recent promoting rows by exact instance plus message (`session-admission-service.ts`,
`SessionAdmissionStore.findRecentPromoting`). Native receipt readback proves that the
queued text and enriched delivered text differ, so matching fails and a second row is
created instead of settling the promoted one.

`SessionAdmissionStore.listQueued` includes promoting rows. Renderer startup restores
those rows through `QueuePersistenceService.restoreFromDisk`. The ordinary
`notifyPromoting` path accepts a successful IPC envelope even when its CAS result is
null, then sends again. The newer retained-busy path checks for data, but the startup
drain uses that older ordinary path. The old promoting head also prevents
`getReadyHandoffId` from offering subsequent queued rows. That last consequence is
source-traced, not a separately executed second-compaction claim.

### Required behaviour

Carry authoritative queued-admission ownership through dispatch, retaining the actual
provider payload in observability as needed. Settle the original durable admission on
its delivery. Restoring a renderer must never replay an already delivered user input;
a null promotion CAS must not be permission to send. Preserve real unsent recovery,
cancellation, Pause races, backoff and bounded busy handoff expiry.

### Acceptance

- Reproduce with a real queued compaction send while input enrichment is active.
- Exactly one provider delivery, one final idle, and no queued/promoting residual for
  that delivered admission.
- Reload the renderer without a new user send: no restored copy and no second delivery.
- A later independent queue send still uses the retained-busy handoff.
- Cover null CAS, genuine unsent restoration and cancellation/Pause races without
  weakening existing tests.

Evidence: root-checkout
`2026-09-24-codex-compaction-turn-visibility_evidence/2026-10-27-resume/`,
`ui-proof-result.json`, append-only `command-receipts.ndjson` (both
`queue-receipt-proof.js` readbacks and `reload-renderer.js`), `ui-main.ndjson`,
`app-scoped.jsonl`, `lifecycle-scoped.ndjson`. Implementation status is in the active
root-checkout `2026-10-27-codex-compaction-lifecycle-followup_plan.md`; the historical
completed remediation plan is not extended. No product source was changed by the
resumed live-test worker.

### LT-715 verifier repair — 2026-10-27

Explicit queuedAdmissionId now travels through renderer promotion, preload/IPC, manager
and communication to the provider-dispatch receipt. A parameterized SQL compare-and-swap
claims only that instance's user-origin promoting row. Text enrichment and elapsed
preparation time no longer affect ownership. A null promotion does not authorize a
send, and the same renderer retains its successful promotion through an unsent Pause
race. A rejected claim cannot be converted into a fresh-message retry.

## LT-720 — ordinary dev renderer prebundling leaves the managed checkout blank

Filed in this register on 2026-11-10 by the localhost-browser-approval live-test item. The defect was first recorded on 2026-10-27 by the campaign-defects live test and the MiMo cut-off live test, which name it LT-720 in their own documents; those entries were not carried into this tree's register, so it is recorded here under the same number. This item did not number it.

### Observed behaviour

Reproduced twice on 2026-10-27: an isolated app using `npm run start:renderer -- --port 4575` loaded an empty app-root. The console reported that `_PlatformLocation` needs the Angular JIT compiler because a partially compiled library was not processed by the linker. IPC stayed live but Angular never bootstrapped. Restarting the same dev server with `--prebundle=false` and reloading restored the real UI, and the production renderer build passed. The localhost-browser-approval item hit the same blank page on its first isolated start on 2026-10-27 and used the same workaround. Sources: [campaign defects live test](2026-10-05-livetest-campaign-defects_livetest.md), [MiMo cut-off live test](2026-10-14-mimo-reasoning-cap-cutoff_livetest.md), [localhost browser approval live test](2026-10-04-localhost-browser-approval_livetest.md).

### Root cause

Confirmed at the dev-server dependency-prebundling and linker boundary. The follow-up plan attributes it to the incompatible Vite 7 override. The precise contribution of linked node_modules versus the generated dependency cache was not proved.

### Current state in this tree (read 2026-11-10)

`package.json` pins `overrides.vite` and the dev dependency to `~8.3.3`, and `node_modules/vite` is 8.3.5. The follow-up plan [campaign defects runtime follow-up](2026-10-27-campaign-defects-runtime-followup_plan.md) marks its LT-720 diagnosis item done, and its live test section 6 holds the rendered first-paint check. That check has not been run, so the defect is not closed here.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The documented normal dev command bootstraps the renderer in an AIO-managed checkout with prebundling on. ## LT-1009 — hibernate/wake silently restores the previous MiMo account after a switch

_Renumbered from LT-711 on 2026-11-08 during the merge with main, which already uses LT-711 for another defect. The 2026-10-27 receipts keep the original number._

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27, isolated live dev app. A dedicated control session `id2cvg6uq` started idle on
legacy (Test A), PID 58156, Low reasoning. Explicit switching to `comtechspare-f7a6`
(Test B) succeeded in place with the same PID. A read before hibernation confirmed Test B;
the hibernated instance still stamped Test B. `wakeInstance` returned success, but the
ready instance had account `legacy` again (new PID 58319). No user prompt or provider turn
was sent by this control, so quota refusal cannot explain the account change. The original
real-turn session also reverted to legacy after a switch back to B and hibernate/wake.
Raw per-step evidence: `wake-account-control.js.result.json` in the owning live-test evidence.

### Root cause

The executed wake path in `instance-lifecycle.ts` calls `resumeSession` and
`restoreAccountStamp(instance, sessionState)`. `hibernateInstance` calls `startTracking`
then `stopTracking`, but `session-continuity.ts:startTracking` returns immediately for an
already tracked instance, preserving its old snapshot. The account-only live handoff changes
the instance stamp (`runtime-reconciler-account-handoff.ts:tryAccountSwitchInPlace` →
`applyAccountHandoff`) without writing the new stamp through to continuity. The reconciler's
nearby explicit continuity account update is inside `if (isProviderSwap)`, so it does not
cover an account-only switch. The live before/sleeping/after values demonstrate that the
stale restore is on this path, not merely an unused helper.

### Required behaviour

A successful account switch must survive hibernation and wake, including an immediate wake
before any provider turn. Preserve current account, logical model, effort and shared history.
If the account cannot be admitted, report the problem rather than silently selecting the old
one. Never require a successful paid model turn to persist an already confirmed account change.

### Acceptance

- A real lifecycle regression starts on A, switches in place to B, hibernates immediately and
  wakes; the executing adapter, instance and continuity snapshot all remain on B.
- Cover account-only respawn handoff as well as in-place handoff; preserve failed-switch rollback.
- Re-run originating live checks 2 and 5, the canonical project gates and fresh independent review.

Implementation status, verifier follow-up 2026-10-27: successful live account switches update
the tracked account stamp and write through under the existing session mutex before success
publication. Account-only respawns use the existing provider/account continuity update, while
only provider changes clear the old native cursor. The new real lifecycle regression drives
in-place handoff, actual hibernate and actual wake with disk-backed continuity and prior history.
It fails on the original implementation. Respawn persistence and rejected-admission controls
also run. The [live no-turn control](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-10-27-queue-61bedf-r2/wake.json)
keeps B, Low effort and the logical model after wake. Successful paid history continuation
remains a separate external-allowance requirement. Independent review is pending. Active work belongs to
`2026-10-27-mimo-account-state-remediation_plan.md`, not the closed July remediation plan.

## LT-1010 — MiMo capture omits upstream HTTP status and response body

_Renumbered from LT-712 on 2026-11-08 during the merge with main, which already uses LT-712 for another defect. The 2026-10-27 receipts keep the original number._

### Observed behaviour

The 2026-10-27 campaign's real MiMo quota refusal is recorded in `provider_event_captures`
with the ACP error text and quota classification, but without HTTP 429 or the upstream
`limitation` response body. Those fields were recoverable only from OpenCode's native store.
The earlier document explicitly reported this limitation but did not assign remediation.
The branch-owned capture-provenance receipt records the observation and source trace.

### Root cause

`acp-jsonrpc-errors.ts:settleAcpErrorResponse` creates an Error from ACP code/message only;
upstream response data is not carried by that error. `provider-event-raw-payload.ts` projects
Error to name/message/stack/cause, and the turn-error capture separately allows statusCode
only when already attached to the Error. The capture layer cannot invent HTTP fields that
OpenCode never forwards over ACP. Direct native-store evidence is not capture-ledger evidence.

### 2026-11-13 update (queue re-run)

A direct ACP probe and a live ledger capture both show OpenCode 1.19.5 replying `{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: quota exhausted","data":{"service":"session","errorName":"APIError"}}`. `data` exists but has no HTTP status or body. The capture ledger keeps this envelope in `raw_json.payload.cause` (the earlier check read only `event_json`, which holds the normalized event). `settleAcpErrorResponse` now adds `upstreamHttp: {status, body}` set to `not-supplied-by-acp` for whichever of the two the reply lacks, so a missing field is stated rather than silent. Receipts: [ledger raw row](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-13-queue-cf6857-r7/check8-ledger-raw-error.json), [direct envelope](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-13-queue-cf6857-r7/check8-acp-envelope-direct.txt). Fixture spec: `src/main/cli/adapters/acp-jsonrpc-errors.spec.ts`. The real status and body are not recoverable over ACP; the item stays open for the transport decision.

### Required behaviour and owner

Owner: provider adapter/event-capture remediation, tracked in the active root-owned
`2026-10-27-mimo-account-state-remediation_plan.md` LT-1010 section. Establish what the
installed OpenCode ACP actually supplies. Preserve safely redacted status/body when supplied;
otherwise expose unavailable provenance explicitly and choose a supported upstream transport
before promising raw HTTP retention. Never read arbitrary vendor stores on every error or
copy credentials, request headers or unredacted payloads into captures.

### Acceptance

- Capture an actual MiMo refusal with recordProviderEvents on; retain the exact received ACP
  envelope and distinguish its fields from native HTTP evidence.
- A fixture verifies supplied structured status/body survive error projection and redaction.
- When ACP omits HTTP fields, diagnostics state that they are unavailable rather than
  fabricating them. Resolve check 8's exact ledger-field requirement before closure.
- Canonical verification and independent review pass. This limitation remains open; the
  observed wording fixture alone does not close it.

## LT-1007 — signal-fence failure in a sandboxed host is reported as a missing OpenCode CLI

### Observed behaviour

On 2026-11-08 the isolated dev app, launched from a queue worker shell that is itself
sandboxed, could not start any OpenCode session. Opening a MiMo session with the OpenCode
provider logged `Requested CLI not available, falling back to auto` and created a Claude
session instead. The OpenCode install probe logged `No usable OpenCode install { candidates: 3,
unknownVersion: 3 }`, and both MiMo account rows in Settings read `Coding sign-in: Could not
check`. The startup panel said only `Hardened mode (Seatbelt): sandbox-exec probe failed —
hardened instances will refuse to spawn.` Retained redacted receipts:
[observations](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-08-queue-61bedf-r4/observations.md)
and [log slice](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-08-queue-61bedf-r4/app-probe-log-slice.txt).

Reproduced outside the app: the fenced command `sandbox-exec -p <signal-fence policy> -- opencode --version`
prints `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` and exits 71. The same CLI without the wrapper
prints its version and exits 0.

### Root cause

`src/main/cli/adapters/opencode-effective-budget-config.ts` (`runOpenCodeCapture`) spawns with
`stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore']`, so the wrapper's stderr is discarded. The fence is applied
to every non-hardened spawn by default (`src/main/sandbox/signal-fence.ts` `applySignalFence`, enabled
when `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` exists). The probe in `opencode-cli-launch.ts` treats a non-zero
exit as an unknown version, so a fence that cannot be applied looks like a broken CLI. The startup
check describes only hardened instances, although ordinary provider CLI spawns are refused too.

### Required behaviour and owner

Owner: provider CLI launch and sandbox diagnostics. When the fence cannot be applied, the probe
must keep the wrapper's failure reason, and the startup check must state the real impact (ordinary
CLI spawns refused, not only hardened ones). Choosing between refusing those spawns and an explicit,
visible unfenced fallback changes a safety boundary. That is an owner decision, not a routine fix.
The provider-level setting `providerSignalFenceEnabled` is read-only for agents and was not changed.

### Acceptance

- A unit test where the wrapper exits 71 with `sandbox_apply` on stderr yields a probe result that
  carries that reason, and the startup check names ordinary CLI spawns.
- A live run from a sandboxed queue worker shows the reason in diagnostics, and a MiMo session
  either starts under the owner-chosen policy or refuses with that reason.
- Canonical verification and independent review pass. This defect stays open until the owner
  decides the fallback policy.

Update 2026-11-12: for the queue live checks James allowed the signal fence to be off in a
throwaway test profile only, never in the real app. With it off in `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-cf6857a6`
the OpenCode probe found a usable install and MiMo sessions started (see the 2026-11-12 section
of the MiMo livetest). That answers how the checks run; it does not decide the product policy
for a fence that cannot be applied, so this defect stays open.

### Observed behaviour

On 2026-11-13, switching a live MiMo session between `MiMo Test A` and `MiMo Test B` from the composer account chip showed a confirmation that began "Switching account restarts this session, and the next message will re-read about N tokens at full price." The process id was unchanged after the switch in both receipts: [explicit switch](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-13-queue-cf6857-r6/check2-explicit-switch.json) (72814 before and after) and [banner switch](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-13-queue-cf6857-r6/check2-banner-switch.json) (69780 before and after). The conversation moved in place.

### Root cause

`src/shared/utils/runtime-change-cost.ts` builds the native-resume warning (the `restarts this session` template, `kind` model or account) with one fixed phrase for both kinds. An account switch on a MiMo session changes only the account route; it does not restart the process. The cost half of the sentence (next message re-reads the history from a cold cache) is the true part.

### Required behaviour

Word the account-switch confirmation so it does not claim a restart that did not happen, keeping the cold-cache cost statement. Wording follows `docs/screen-and-wording-guide.md`. A model change may keep its own wording if that path really does restart.

### Acceptance

- `runtime-change-cost.spec.ts` asserts the account-kind text contains no "restarts".
- A live in-place account switch shows the corrected text and the process id stays the same.

### Fix (2026-11-14)

`runtime-change-cost.ts` now builds the account-kind sentence as "<Switching account> moves this session to the new account, and the next message will re-read about N tokens at full price."; the model kind keeps "restarts this session". The composer account chip's own confirmation lead-in (`provider-account-chip.component.ts`) also said "The current session ends"; it now reads "The conversation continues on that account." because that wording had the same problem. Tests: `runtime-change-cost.spec.ts` (new case asserts no "restart" for both native-resume continuities), `provider-account-chip.cost-note.spec.ts` (full confirmation text). Live receipt: [lt1123-live-switch.json](2026-10-10-mimo-multi-account_evidence/2026-11-14-queue-cf6857-r9/lt1123-live-switch.json) (confirmation text shown, process id 80146 before and after).

## LT-712 — read-only browser handoff cannot be correlated to its audit or FIFO position

**Priority:** P3. **Status:** OPEN, recorded 2026-10-27; no fix claimed. Follow-up to LT-616,
whose poll-request/command-ID log remains implemented. Owner: browser command delivery and
Gateway audit pipeline. Implementation status is recorded under *Acceptance and implementation
status* below and in the AR-003 evidence run; the closed
`2026-10-27-browser-handoff-observability_plan_completed.md` record is not edited.
Origin: [AR-003](2026-09-27-livetest-agent-runtime-residuals_livetest.md#ar-003--lt-371-live-browser-command-socket-handoff-correlation).

### Observed behavior

The installed coordinator's 2026-10-27 04:46:25.998–04:46:30.187 UTC run logged two failed
poll handoffs/requeues for dispatch `bff39b44-734c-4a0a-8b3a-c17652338bb9` and one successful
`browser.query_elements` audit `f50a00d6-2058-49b6-af91-7dbab5c7f682`. The retained schema/row
receipt has no dispatch-command column and a null `request_id`. Neither requeue log records
queue position. Those records cannot prove AR-003 step 4's direct join, FIFO-head reinsertion
or absence of duplicate execution. This is an evidence gap, not proof of lost, duplicated or
misordered browser work. The installed binary's source fingerprint was not captured, so this
runtime observation is not represented as a current-checkout build reproduction.

Raw evidence: `2026-09-27-livetest-agent-runtime-residuals_evidence/2026-10-27-verifier-repair/`
(`ar003-attempt.json`, `ar003-main-log.txt`, `ar003-audit.json`, `ar003-final-health.json`).
The review-corrections receipt independently revalidates these inputs and seals the current source.

### Root cause in the reviewed checkout

`browser-extension-command-store.ts:344` resolves only `result.result`; its dispatch ID is not
returned to the read caller. `browser-gateway-service.ts:1288` normalizes that result and records
the query through `BrowserGatewayResultRecorder`, which has no dispatch-ID input.
`browser-audit-store.ts:50` persists the audit fields without a dispatch ID. The store reinserts
with `unshift` at line 397, while `rpc-event-router.ts:641` logs only node, command, poll request
and a requeued boolean. Source proves intended head insertion, not a live queue-position event.
The mutation-journal hook is not a substitute on this read-only path.

### Required behavior

Retain content-free evidence joining the original read command ID, failed poll handoff, actual
head reinsertion and final successful audit ID. Preserve approval-request identity separately;
do not repurpose `request_id` or log page content, selectors, credentials or query results.
Keep the original delivery deadline, receipt safety and single-execution guarantees.

### Acceptance and implementation status

**2026-11-07 implementation (merged from main).** The implementation landed on main under the closed
[browser handoff observability plan](2026-10-27-browser-handoff-observability_plan_completed.md), with
`browser-handoff-observability.spec.ts`. A parallel log-only version on the agent-runtime branch was dropped in the
merge because main already provides the same evidence. Browser command queueing reports each command ID through an
`onQueued` callback. The command store logs `Browser command requeued at FIFO head` with the command ID, queue
position and queue depth. The result recorder persists `command_id` on every audit row
(`browser-audit-store.ts`), and the existing-tab query path passes its command ID to the result. The audit join is
therefore durable, not a log-line join. Live observation on an identified rebuilt coordinator is still open.

- Add the missing read-dispatch/audit correlation and queue-order observation on the executing
  delivery path, with focused regressions. If durable audit storage changes, migrate existing data.
- Run canonical gates and independent implementation review; no existing expectation is weakened.
- Repeat AR-003 on an identified rebuilt coordinator through Gateway targeting `windows-pc`,
  retaining the exact source/build identity and direct evidence required by all four steps.
  Require one successful audit for the same original dispatch ID, observed FIFO head, no receipt
  failure or duplicate execution, original budget, and ready health afterward.
- Until that live run passes, keep AR-003 and LT-712 open as a technical implementation
  prerequisite. Repeating resets on an unchanged unobservable build cannot supply the missing proof.

## LT-1026 — a large context-fill send blocks the main loop during retrieval

_Renumbered from LT-732 on 2026-11-08 during the merge with main, because LT-732 was already assigned to a sidechat defect on the base. Renumbered again to LT-1026 on 2026-11-09, because LT-1013 was also assigned to a compaction defect._

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27, queue worktree, isolated profile `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-c8434b3e`, instance `xb1w9dxya`. At 03:07:36.807 UTC a 400,219-character message entered `INSTANCE_SEND_INPUT`. Last progress was the ContextSearch keyword-fallback log at 03:07:36.877. No provider turn began in that interval. At 03:10:11.016 RuntimeDiagnostics reported `Main process event loop stall detected`, `stallMs:153712`; the send-context deadline was exceeded and the queued SIGTERM shut down the owned dev app normally (exit 0). The send returned SEND_FAILED / runtime closed during that shutdown.

Evidence: root `.aio-review/lt-c8434b3e-round2/dev-app.log`, `stall-observation.json`, `context-fill-1.log`, `dev-app-receipt.json`, and the native rollout extract. The large message used harmless generated words for the required high-context check, not a load test; it was not retried.

### Root cause

Not proven. The executing retrieval path reaches `executeSemanticSearch` in `src/main/rlm/context/context-search.ts`, which expands the full query into regex alternatives and calls synchronous `executeGrep`. The last progress and the recorded main-loop stall identify the blocked stage; they do not isolate regex compilation from matching. Shared host load was also high and was checked.

### Required behaviour

An accepted large message must not block the main event loop while generating optional retrieval context. Bound and sanitize retrieval queries and keep stop/read-back responsive.

### Acceptance

A deterministic local regression must bound processing of large or repeated queries without a timing stress test, and a live large-message send must keep the UI and Stop responsive. Do not close based only on the compaction test succeeding with a short prompt and fixture tool output.

### Implementation status

Open; no retrieval code changed in this task. Current follow-up: root untracked `2026-10-27-codex-goal-following-remediation_plan.md`, additional-defect note. The compaction campaign uses short prompts and fixture reads to complete its assigned check independently.


## LT-1027 — first-profile startup fails at the RLM journal-mode pragma

_Renumbered from LT-733 on 2026-11-08 during the merge with main, because LT-733 was already assigned to a sidechat defect on the base. Renumbered again to LT-1027 on 2026-11-09, because LT-1014 was also assigned to a compaction defect._

source `ca2e64dcb`, isolated profile `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-c8434b3e`. The main process failed critical

The owned context worker started at 04:21:01.407 and reported successful RLM initialization at

Open; no database initialization code is changed by this campaign. Matching active status is in
