## LT-1003 — 35B tool smoke misses the specified second-turn cache acceptance

**Status: open acceptance gap, one live smoke on 27 October 2026.**

### Observed behaviour

The 35B on native llama-server 2.60.0, context 65536, parallel 1, through the bundled translator
completed Read → Edit → Bash/npm-test with zero tool errors. Independent file and test checks
passed. Nevertheless, its first two assistant requests report zero cached-read tokens and
16959 / 17083 fresh input tokens. Server prompt evaluation took 1509.08 / 1506.20 ms respectively;
the second is not substantially faster. Requests three and four report 17243 / 17413 cache-read
tokens, with only 108 / 29 fresh input tokens and 360.40 / 309.73 ms prompt evaluation.
Thus caching exists, but A4's explicit second-turn improvement is not demonstrated.

Evidence: `benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/evidence/2026-10-27/smoke-35b.json`,
`smoke-message-usage.receipt.json`, `server-timings.receipt.txt`, and `proxy.log`.

### Root cause / investigation limit

The measured route is `runClaudeAgent` → local endpoint environment → bundled translator →
native Windows 2.60.0 server. The translator lifted one system reminder on each request.
The reason the second request did not reuse its predecessor's prefix has not been isolated.
Do not turn that observation into a claim that the model cannot cache or that application
caching is broken. No source/test/config change was made to hide the result.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Repeat the agreed smoke with request/cache timing evidence. Establish why the second prefix
is re-evaluated and either meet the current criterion or explicitly revise the benchmark
protocol with consistent treatment of every local arm. Keep the successful tool-calling
subcheck separate from the unmet second-turn cache subcheck. Technical investigation remains
agent work; no human authority is needed to collect another bounded local sample.

### 27 October correction run: reproduced again with request-shape evidence

The same native 2.60.0 35B setup at 65536/parallel 1 completed Read/Edit/Bash and an independent
test again (four turns, zero tool errors). First and second requests again report zero cached
reads; third and fourth report 17146 and 17290. Hash-only observation of the normalized request
shows the third system block changes from 9910 to 9610 serialized bytes between the first two
requests, then stays identical; the first two system blocks and tool-schema hash stay unchanged.
That is a concrete changing prefix to investigate, not a controlled proof of the server's cache
invalidation cause. No second-turn prompt-time measurement was collected on this replay, and
the zero-cache result alone leaves the existing acceptance unmet. No protocol was relaxed.

Evidence: `benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/evidence/2026-10-27-review-fixes/cache-retest.receipt.json`
and the original local-only agent output. No model score or final pilot decision follows.

### 27 October resumed run: second-turn cache behavior demonstrated

The translator preserves lifted structured system content instead of serializing the whole
block array into text. A real native35B Read/Edit/Bash smoke plus independent npm test pass,
zero tool errors. Observed request one cache0/input16921, request two cache17106/input43,
and later requests positive. Client request-to-upstream-message_start falls1252.409→88.576ms
(14.139x); that includes network and first-token time, not pure server prompt_ms. The latter
was not measured because native stop/relaunch-with-log was rejected by automatic approval.
Behavioral cache gap is reproduced as fixed; independent final verification remains recorded
separately. All ten new C1 cells require translator-v2 setup identity and a fresh session;
do not merge earlier translator records into this comparison. Evidence:
`benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/evidence/2026-10-27-resume/cache-observed/cache-retest.receipt.json`
and `cache-latency-summary.receipt.json`. No model score or pure server-time claim follows.

### 7 November 2026 re-confirmation with native server timing

One smoke on the native 35B (2.60.0, 65536/parallel 1) through the frozen translator measured
server-side prompt time for the first time. Request one evaluated 17,216 tokens in 1,808.51 ms.
Request two evaluated 39 new tokens in 106.11 ms, reusing about 17,579 cached tokens (prefix
similarity 0.998). The tool sequence was Read, Bash, Write, Bash, with the Write standing in for
the specified Edit; the independent test passed. This supports the second-turn cache result with
server timing; the Edit-tool deviation and the 35B-only scope keep the acceptance check open.
Evidence: `benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/evidence/2026-11-07-livetest-resume/native-timing-lines.txt`.

## LT-1005 — the benchmark translator cannot reach an IPv6 native server

**Status: open, reproduced 7 November 2026. Workaround in use; translator unchanged.**

### Observed behaviour

With the native 2.60.0 server bound to a Tailscale IPv6 address, `local-anthropic-proxy.ts`
pointed at `http://[fd7a:115c:a1e0::434:5d68]:1235` answered every request with HTTP 502 and
logged `upstream error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND [fd7a:115c:a1e0::434:5d68]`. The same server
answered 401/401/200 when reached directly, so the failure is in the translator's upstream
connection, not in the server. Evidence: `benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/evidence/2026-11-07-livetest-resume/translator-8900.log`.

### Root cause

`benchmarks/plan-execute-ab/local-anthropic-proxy.ts` builds the upstream request with
`hostname: up.hostname` (about line 157). For an IPv6 literal, Node's `URL.hostname` keeps the
square brackets, and `http.request` then tries to resolve `[fd7a:…]` as a DNS name.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The upstream connection should accept a bracketed IPv6 literal (strip the brackets before
`http.request`, or pass the unbracketed address). Acceptance: a unit test that starts the
translator against an IPv6 loopback upstream and gets the upstream response; and the same
smoke as the 7 November run passing through the translator with no separate forwarder. The
change alters the frozen translator's behaviour, so the owning plan must decide whether it
counts as a new translator identity before any scored cell uses it. Until then, IPv4 upstreams
and the byte forwarder in that evidence folder are the only tested routes.

## LT-1114

### LT-1114 — the Connectors panel clips its own form and connector list

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026 in the dev app; shipped build pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app from this branch, 1400 x 900 window, MCP Servers, Connectors tab. The `.management-panel` section measured 178 px
tall (`clientHeight` 178, `scrollHeight` 223). Clicking **Add** with the mouse grew its content to 736 px but the panel
stayed 178 px, so Name was cut at the top and the Environment box, the AI-tool checkboxes and **Save** were outside the
panel (Save at y 952-978, panel 296-476). Mouse-wheel scrolling over the form scrolled the page, not the panel, so a
mouse user could not reach Save. A keyboard user could, because focus scrolls clipped boxes into view. A saved
connector list sits below the Add button and was clipped the same way.

### Root cause

`mcp-page.component.scss`: `.page` is a fixed-height flex column with `overflow: auto`. `.management-panel` had
`min-height: 180px; overflow: hidden` and the default `flex-shrink: 1`, so the column shrank it to its minimum instead of
letting the page scroll. The pages' other panels already use `flex-shrink: 0`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The panel grows with its content and the page scrolls. After the fix (`flex-shrink: 0`, `min-height` removed): panel
`clientHeight` 223 with no form and 736 with the form open (equal to `scrollHeight`), Save inside the panel, and the
wheel scrolls the page. Same check at 200 percent zoom: every field and Save reachable by Tab.

## LT-1115

### LT-1115 — a refused mail draft is reported as a calendar refusal and shows the account key

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026 by unit test; live recheck needs the rebuilt app.**

### Observed behaviour

In the real app, `mcp__m365-fortitude__graph_mail_create_draft` (a read-only account) was refused before any Graph write,
as intended, but the text was `Calendar mutation is not permitted for agent calendar mutations: <tenant-id>.<object-id>`.
It is a mail action, and the text exposes the internal account key.

`connector-graph-tools.ts` checks mail writes with `requireWritableAccountKey` from `orchestrator-calendar-tools.ts`,
which hard-codes calendar wording and interpolates the requested key.

One neutral message for every write: "Writes are not permitted for agents on this Microsoft account. Turn on agent
writes for its connector first." No key. `connector-graph-tools.spec.ts` asserts the mail refusal does not contain
"calendar" or the key (it fails on the old wording); `orchestrator-calendar-tools.spec.ts` expects the new text. Live
recheck: a draft attempt through a read-only connector shows the new text on the rebuilt app.

## LT-1117

### LT-1117 — a focused tall text box is only partly in view at high zoom

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026 in the dev app; shipped build pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app from this branch, 200 percent zoom emulated (700 x 450 CSS pixels; the page area is about 158 px tall because
the app header uses the rest). Add form open, Tab to the "Headers (JSON object)" box: its box was at 412-492 px inside a

All other stops were fully visible. (The first run of this check labelled this stop "Environment"; it was Headers.)

Chrome reveals only the caret line of a focused text box, not the whole box, and the page had no space reserved below

A control reached by keyboard is entirely visible. Fix: `scroll-padding-bottom: 96px` on `.page` in
`mcp-page.component.scss`. Re-run at 200 percent after the fix, Tab forward and Shift+Tab backward through the Local
program, Remote server and Microsoft 365 forms: no stop partly hidden (Local forward 16 stops, Local backward 18, Remote
and Microsoft 365 forward and back 28 each). Also none hidden at 100 percent backward.

## LT-1122

### LT-1122 — an explicit account switch on a hibernated session waits for the wake

**Status: open, P3; user-visible effect not confirmed.**

### Observed behaviour

With the MiMo session hibernated, an explicit switch to account B was queued ("Runtime change queued (instance not waiting
for input)") and applied on wake (new process, transcript note, next turn on B). The switch call itself resolved only after

composer and record the control's state until wake; fix the renderer state if it stays busy.

### Observed behaviour

14 November 2026, dev app built at 06:32 from this worktree: after a hibernate that followed an in-place account switch, the
idle monitor logged `process_exited_unexpected: requesting respawn` for the hibernated session at 06:47:09 and 06:48:09
and `Illegal lifecycle transition blocked { from: 'hibernated', to: 'initializing' }` each time, then `Recovery attempts
exhausted` at 06:49:09. `restartCount` rose from 1 to 3. Wake and later turns still worked (log slice
`check1-app-log-idle-monitor-after-hibernate.txt`). A clean hibernate with no queued switch did not do this over 25 s.

### Root cause

The compiled `dist/main/.../idle-monitor.js` the app ran had no hibernation guard (0 mentions of `hibernated`). The branch
was fast-forwarded to main at 06:40:51 that day (reflog), after that build and before the failure. The previous commit
(`f6b4f0f36`) has 0 mentions of `hibernated` in `idle-monitor.ts`; the current source (`de1dcd5e1`) has 4: the detector loop
skips hibernating and hibernated sessions (`idle-monitor.ts:215`), discards a detection that finishes after hibernation
(`:228`), and re-checks before dispatching a recovery (`RECOVERY_INACTIVE_STATUSES` includes both). The guard came in with
`186958a63` on 13 November. The failure was therefore a stale build, not a current-source defect.
`npm run test:quiet -- src/main/instance/lifecycle/idle-monitor-hibernation.spec.ts` passes (8 tests).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A hibernated session is never offered to crash recovery. Acceptance: rebuild the app from current source, switch accounts in
place, hibernate immediately, wait three minutes: no `process_exited_unexpected` for that session and `restartCount`
unchanged. Not done in this run because the dev app was already stopped and rebuilt output was not refreshed.

## LT-1037

### LT-1037 — a gemini worker gets no Harness tools, so it cannot report its work ready

**Status: reproduced live 12 November 2026; not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

In the worker-report live check ([evidence](2026-11-04-pq-b3-report-ready_livetest.md#gemini-check-a-failed-lt-1037)) a Plan Queue run whose saved worker list
named only `gemini` started the worker as `antigravity` (spawn log `requested: 'antigravity'`, model "Gemini 3.8 Flash (Medium)"). The spawn log
had no "Orchestrator tool schemas deferred" line for it. Over about six minutes the worker made 61 tool calls, searching the machine and the source tree for
`plan_queue_report_ready`, and never reported. Claude, codex, cursor and opencode workers found and called the tool in the same app within 20 to 100 seconds.

### Root cause

`ORCHESTRATOR_RUNTIME_INJECTION_PROVIDERS` in `src/shared/types/mcp-scopes.types.ts` lists `gemini` but not `antigravity`. A `gemini` choice resolves to the
`antigravity` CLI type, so `isOrchestratorRuntimeInjectionProvider` is false and `SpawnConfigBuilder.getOrchestratorMcpConfigs` returns no orchestrator-tools
configuration. Not yet confirmed: whether the Antigravity CLI can load an injected MCP server at all (an `AntigravityMcpAdapter` exists for its settings file).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A worker or checker on the Antigravity CLI can discover and call the Harness orchestrator tools, or Harness refuses `gemini` / `antigravity` as a Plan Queue
worker and checker with a plain reason. Acceptance: the `gemini` Check A in the live-check document ends with a `plan_queue_report_ready` call answered
`accepted: true`; then `gemini` goes on `REPORT_REQUIRED_PROVIDERS`. Until then `gemini` stays off that list, so a `gemini` worker keeps the turn-end signal.

## LT-1016

### LT-1016 — a landing skipped its related tests after a checklist with no tests

**Status: source fix verified 8 November 2026; rebuilt-app check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Item `d6b89b52` (livetest run, checklist `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint`) landed as commit `3cb1ae812` on
7 November 2026 at 20:19Z: 252 files, including `src/main/cli/adapters/claude-cli-permission-details.ts`,
`src/main/orchestration/headless-review-runner.ts` and four spec files. Both receipts passed on exactly the
landed tree (no difference outside closed documents), and the landing's `commitCheckMs` was 2,584 ms, far too
short for `npm run test:staged` on that change. The hook's output is not kept on a successful landing, so the skip
is shown by the matching tree, the eligibility rule and the timing, not by the printed line.

### Root cause

`checkedTreeForLanding` (`src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-landing.ts`) granted the covered-tests proof whenever every
receipt of the run's own checklist passed on the landing tree. It never required the checklist to contain a test
run, so a livetest checklist of type check and lint stood in for the hook's tests. The approved design
([batched checks plan, requirement 1](2026-11-02-plan-queue-batched-checks_plan_completed.md)) allowed the skip only
for code that "already passed the full checklist".

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The proof needs, in addition, at least one checklist command that runs tests (`isTestCommand`, the same rule the
receipt classifier uses) whose receipt is `passed`, meaning its output showed tests passing. A test command whose
output was not recognised does not count. Acceptance: `plan-queue-landing.spec.ts` cases `no-test-run` and
`unrecognised-tests` leave the hook without the proof (both failed before the fix), and `green` (with
`npm run test:quiet`) still grants it. On the rebuilt app, a livetest landing that changes code runs the hook's
related tests (commit check takes as long as the tests), and a plan landing with a green full checklist still skips
them.

## LT-1017

### LT-1017 — the hook's test skip never fires for a normal plan landing

**Status: source fix verified 8 November 2026; rebuilt-app check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Five `plans` jobs landed in this repository on 8 November 2026 (12:29Z to 16:59Z), each with an eight-command
checklist that all passed. Compared with each job's tested tree, every landed commit also changed
`docs/generated/architecture-inventory.json`; one also carried base-branch changes. Commit checks took 83 to 264
seconds, so the hook ran `test:staged` every time. Of the ten earlier livetest landings, nine differed from their
tested tree in the same file.

### Root cause

Queue workers' checkpoint commits skip the hook, so the architecture list on a job's branch is stale. At landing the
pre-commit hook runs the generators and stages their output before `test:staged`. `scripts/run-git-hook.js` then
required the staged index to equal the tested tree exactly, so the rebuilt list alone cancelled the skip. The
architecture list is documentation: no runtime code or test reads it (only its generator's own spec), and
`test-staged.js` already leaves generated files out of its test selection.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Before `test:staged`, the hook compares the staged index with the tested tree ignoring regenerated documentation
(`DOCUMENTATION_ARTIFACTS`, the generated files under `docs/`), with `git diff-tree --quiet` and exact literal
excludes. Regenerated code (`register-aliases.ts`, IPC channels) and any other difference still run the tests; any git
failure runs them too. Acceptance: `run-git-hook.spec.ts` case `regenerated: documentation` skips (it failed before
the fix), `regenerated: code` runs the tests, and the mocked changed-tree case still runs them. On the rebuilt app, a
plan landing whose code equals its tested code has a short commit check.

## LT-1157

### LT-1157 — Land anyway always refused a Codex parent ("provider can't report when a turn starts")

**Status: fixed and verified live 12 November 2026. The rebuilt dev app accepted a Codex parent's typed-message `land-anyway` (07:54) and refused the call made in the goal-started turn (07:57), see livetest check 3.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app (isolated profile) with a Codex parent session that started a Plan Queue run. The item parked, a message was typed in the real message box ("Land that anyway…"), and the session called `plan_queue_control` with `land-anyway`. Twice (07:47 and 07:48) the call was refused: "This session's provider can't report when a turn starts, so Harness can't tell that you are answering James's message." The same sequence on a Claude parent was accepted. The item stayed parked.

### Root cause

`InstanceCommunicationManager.setupAdapterEvents` read `adapter.getAdapterCapabilities().reportsTurnStarts` once, when the adapter was attached, and stored the boolean in `InputTurnRegistry`. For Codex that capability is `this.useAppServer`, which is only set to true inside `spawn()`. Every attach path (`instance-lifecycle.ts` create and resume) calls `setupAdapterEvents` before `adapter.spawn()`, so a fresh Codex session was recorded as unable to report turn starts for good. The registry unit tests set the flag by hand and the adapter spec sets `useAppServer` directly, so neither saw the order.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The registry asks the adapter at each check (`setReportsTurnStarts(instanceId, () => boolean)`), so a resident Codex session reports, an exec-mode fallback or terminated one is refused. Acceptance: `instance-communication-turn-start-capability.spec.ts` (fails with the old eager read, mutation-checked), `input-turn-registry.spec.ts` case "asks the adapter at check time"; on the rebuilt app (done 12 November 2026), a Codex parent's typed-message `land-anyway` is accepted ([livetest check 3](2026-11-04-pq-b1-land-anyway_plan_livetest.md)).

## LT-1184 — Word search adds unrelated earlier text as retrieved context (renumbered from LT-1063 on 2026-11-17: main used LT-1063 for a different defect)

**Observed:** 12 November 2026, dev app at commit 36611bb65 with the installed `bge-small-en-v1.5-int8` model, fresh profile, one Claude session. After a note about a staging password rotation and the messages `what is a good recipe for sourdough`, `what is the capital of Australia?` and `yes please`, the message `make this dashboard look modern without touching how it works` reached the model with a `[Retrieved Context]` block (`Source: RLM hybrid search`) holding the earlier sourdough recipe. The model replied that the retrieved context was a recipe, not a dashboard. In the same session `when is the staging database password rotation and who owns it?` correctly got the earlier note (scores 0.83 and 0.78 against the 0.70 floor), and the capital, `yes please` and sourdough questions got nothing. Real model scores of the dashboard message against every stored text in the session were 0.37 to 0.52, all below 0.70.

**Root cause:** two paths ignore the floor. First, when nothing clears it, `executeSemanticSearch` in `src/main/rlm/context/context-search.ts` falls back to a keyword search of the query's words, and still reports the result as a semantic match. Second, `buildRlmContext` in `src/main/instance/instance-context.ts` also runs a `grep` over the session's stored text and added its hits as candidates. `extractQueryTerms` keeps every word of four or more letters (no stop words, first 12), `buildLexicalPattern` joins them with `|`, and `rankRlmSections` adds the matches to the candidates with no similarity floor. `make` and `look` match `makes` and `looks` in the recipe. The meaning floors checked by installed check 7 never see this path, so raising or lowering them cannot fix it.

**Required behaviour:** a stored text is added as retrieved context only when it is about the message. A match on everyday words alone adds nothing.

**Acceptance:** a test with a session holding an unrelated recipe and a message of everyday words (the one above) adds no block, while a message that shares real subject words with an earlier text still gets it. After a rebuild, the same probe on the dev app adds no block for the dashboard message.

**Fix (12 November 2026):** `SemanticSearchParams.keywordFallback` (default true) lets a caller turn the fallback off; `buildRlmContext` sets it false and only adds sections the meaning search returned, using the word search to reorder them. The unused `lexical` source is removed. `instance-context-rlm-retrieval.spec.ts` (2 tests) and a `context-search.spec.ts` case fail on the old code and pass. Dev-app probe on the real model: the related question still got the note, the dashboard message got nothing. Cost: a stored text that shares only an exact identifier with the message, and is not close in meaning, is no longer added; the `local-tfidf` fallback model still matches on shared words at its 0.5 floor.

## LT-1145

### LT-1145 — a keyboard-opened session menu cannot be used from the keyboard

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 11 November 2026; independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), run 11 Nov 2026 in a dev app built from this queue worktree (isolated profile, focus emulation on, renderer served from a development build).

### Observed behaviour

With a session row focused, the Menu key opened the context menu (the `contextmenu` event arrives with `button === -1`;
a right click reports 2). The menu stayed open, but focus stayed on the row: ArrowDown did nothing, Tab moved on to the
row's own buttons and 70 Tab presses never reached the menu, and the menu did not close. A disabled item could therefore
never be focused to read its reason.

### Root cause

`InstanceListComponent` rendered `<app-context-menu>` without `[focusOnOpen]`. Only the new-session options menu in
`sidebar-header.component.ts` set it, so the focus move, arrow-key and Tab handling in `context-menu.component.ts`
never ran for session rows or history rows.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A menu opened by keyboard takes focus on its first item, ArrowUp/Down/Home/End move between items, Enter runs an item
once, Escape closes it and focus returns to the row; a pointer-opened menu keeps focus where it was. Fix:
`instance-list.component.ts` / `.html` pass `[focusOnOpen]` from `contextMenuOpenedByKeyboard(event)`
(`session-menu-groups.ts`, tested in `session-menu-groups.spec.ts`) and restore focus to the opener on close. Rechecked
live: focus lands on "Select session", whose reason ("This session is already selected.") shows on focus; Enter on the
Copy entry opens its submenu; Enter on "Copy session ID" wrote the id exactly once; Escape closed the menu and focus
returned to the row.

## LT-1146

### LT-1146 — a wake-up due during a busy turn does not say it is waiting for the session

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 11 November 2026; independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), run 11 Nov 2026 in a dev app built from this queue worktree (isolated profile, focus emulation on, renderer served from a development build).

### Observed behaviour

A one-time wake-up was scheduled on a disposable Codex session. Its countdown ticked down by itself ("in 47 s", "in 42 s",
... "in 2 s"). Both times the session was busy (a `sleep` tool call) when the wake-up came due. The countdown then read
"Next run unverified" for the rest of the turn (80 s the first time) instead of "Due now, waiting for the session to be
idle". When the turn ended the prompt was delivered and accepted, so the delivery itself works.

### Root cause

`thread-wakeup-runner.ts` admits the send behind the busy turn and ends the run as `skipped` with "That conversation was
busy. Harness will send this when its current turn ends." The one-time automation's `nextFireAt` becomes null.
`AutomationCountdownComponent` takes its deadline from a `pending` run or `nextFireAt` and only sets `waitingForIdle`
when a `pending` run exists, so neither is true and `ScheduledCountdownComponent` falls through to "Next run
unverified". Recorded store state at the time: automation `nextFireAt: null`, run `status: skipped`,
`scheduledAt` equal to the due time.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

From the due time until the held prompt is delivered, the wake-up reads "Due now, waiting for the session to be idle".

### Fix and recheck

The reason text moved to `src/shared/utils/thread-wakeup-deferral.ts` (`THREAD_WAKEUP_DEFERRED_BUSY`) so main and renderer
share it; `thread-wakeup-runner.ts` records it, and `AutomationCountdownComponent` treats a `skipped` run with that
reason and an unconfirmed delivery (`threadPromptDelivered !== true`) as held: its `scheduledAt` is the deadline and
`waitingForIdle` is true. The unconfirmed test includes the redelivery in flight (value null). A skip that was not a
deferral, and a delivered prompt, are ignored. `automation-countdown.component.spec.ts` has three cases and failed (2 of 3)
before the change. Live repeat in a rebuilt dev app: wake-up due 30 s in, session busy with a `sleep 70` tool call; the
countdown read "in 26 s" ... "in 2 s", then "Due now, waiting for the session to be idle" in every sample from 32 s to 76 s,
and the prompt was delivered when the turn ended.

## LT-1032

### LT-1032 — Session facts counts no failed tool for a Codex command that exited non-zero

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 11 November 2026; independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), run 11 Nov 2026 in a dev app built from this queue worktree (isolated profile, focus emulation on, renderer served from a development build).

### Observed behaviour

A yolo Codex session ran `echo lt-ok` (exit 0), `sleep 120` and `cat /nonexistent-lt-file` (exit 1, output "No such
file or directory"). Session facts said "0 failed tools".

### Root cause

`sessionFacts` counted only `metadata.is_error === true`. The Codex adapter deliberately sets `is_error` to false for a
command that ran and exited non-zero and reports `status: 'failed'` instead (`codex-notification-item-events.ts`).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A result the provider reports as `status: 'failed'` counts as one failed tool, also when `is_error` is true as well.
Fix in `src/shared/utils/session-facts.ts` with a case in `session-facts.spec.ts`. Rechecked live after the fix, including
after terminating and restoring the conversation from history: "1 failed tools".

## LT-1033

### LT-1033 — one Codex compaction is counted as two

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 11 November 2026; independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), run 11 Nov 2026 in a dev app built from this queue worktree (isolated profile, focus emulation on, renderer served from a development build).

### Observed behaviour

After one `compactInstance` on the Codex session, Session facts said "2 compactions". The transcript held two boundary
rows: "Codex compacted the conversation to free context space." (`threadCompacted`, `isCompactionBoundary`, marker
`cmark_732c1be5-d1e`) and "— Context compacted —" (`isCompactionBoundary`, marker `cmark_86139f3f-3af`). The count
stayed 2 after restoring the conversation from history.

### Root cause

`sessionFacts` adds one for every system row with `isCompactionBoundary` or `threadCompacted`, and a Codex compaction
writes two such rows with different marker ids, so the markers cannot be used to join them.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

One compaction counts once, by a rule that does not use timestamps.

### Fix and recheck

The two rows come from different writers: the provider's own boundary (`instance-event-forwarding.ts`, `method:
'self-managed'`, `threadCompacted`) and the app's `compaction-runtime.ts` divider (`method: 'native'`). `sessionFacts`
now remembers that a provider boundary was just counted and does not count a `native` divider that follows it with only
system rows in between; any user, assistant or tool message in between ends the pairing, so a later separate compaction
still counts. The rule works on restored conversations too (the continuity projection keeps `method` but drops
`threadCompacted`). `session-facts.spec.ts` covers provider+divider, restored, provider-only, divider-only, a later
compaction after conversation (2) and two back-to-back compactions (2). Live repeat: one `compactInstance` shows
"1 compactions" with the two boundary rows still in the transcript, and the same after terminating and restoring the
conversation from history.

## LT-1034

### LT-1034 — the CLI update pill's waiting-session count is blocked by the event check

**Status: open; outside the Oct-2 later scope, found while its dev app ran.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), run 11 Nov 2026 in a dev app built from this queue worktree (isolated profile, focus emulation on, renderer served from a development build).

### Observed behaviour

The log repeated `Blocked invalid renderer event payload` for `cli-update-pill:delta` with the issue
`Unrecognized key: "waitingSessionCount"` (first at 2026-11-11T01:26:56Z, again at each session start).

### Root cause

`CliUpdatePillStateEventSchema` in `packages/contracts/src/schemas/observability.schemas.ts` is `.strict()` and has no
`waitingSessionCount`, which `cli-update-poll-service.ts` sets and `cli-update-pill.component.ts` shows. The whole delta
is dropped, so the pill neither updates its count nor shows the waiting sessions.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Add `waitingSessionCount` (non-negative integer, optional) to the schema; a `renderer-event-validation.spec.ts` case
with a delta carrying it passes; the log line stops appearing while sessions wait.

## LT-1035

### LT-1035 — a message delivered by crash recovery stays marked "not sent"

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 11 November 2026; independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-11), dev app built from this queue worktree.

### Observed behaviour

On a disposable Codex session the CLI child process (a direct child of the dev app, pid taken from the app's own
instance record) was killed with `kill -9`. The app marked the session `error` and began its automatic restart
(01:56:02.007Z). A message sent from the composer 0.5 s later (01:56:02.532Z) found no adapter
(`No adapter found for instance`, `adapterExists: false`) and the bubble `2d0e2e4b` became `uncertain`. The transcript
showed the error row "Your message wasn't sent." The restart then recovered by replay, `InstanceContinuityInputQueue`
logged "Model replied after continuity text; no longer holding it" (01:56:07Z), and the assistant answered
"LT-RETRY-OK". The final bubble state stayed `uncertain` ("Delivery uncertain, not retried") and the composer held the
original text again: the next send combined the old and new text into one message (bubble `b618910f`).

### Root cause

The restart (`restartInstance` in `instance-lifecycle.ts`) holds the session mutex, removes the old adapter and rebuilds
a new one, but nothing told the send path that a restart was running. `awaitInstanceInputReady`
(`instance-input-ready.ts`) waits only for an init (`readyPromise`), an interrupt respawn (`respawnPromise`), a hibernation
wake and a queued runtime change. A send arriving mid-restart therefore reached `communication.sendInput` with no
adapter (log: `adapterExists: false`, `No adapter found for instance`), which is not in `isKnownSendRefusal`, so the bubble
became `uncertain`, the error row appeared, the composer text came back and the session was pushed to `error` under the
restart. The user's bubble had already been added to the transcript, so the restart's replay fallback
(`buildFallbackHistory` then `sendHeldHistory`, adapter-level) carried it to the model, which answered. No second send
call was logged (one `INSTANCE_SEND_INPUT` only), so the "delivery" was the replay, which never updates the bubble. An
earlier version of this entry guessed at the continuity queue; the "Model replied after continuity text" line it cited is
about the replay text, not the user's message.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A message sent while a restart is rebuilding the adapter waits for the restart and is then delivered once, with its bubble
moving to accepted, no "wasn't sent" row and an empty composer. A restart that fails gives the usual terminal failure.

### Fix and recheck

`holdInputWhileRestarting` (`lifecycle/overflow-replacement-readiness.ts`) sets `instance.readyPromise` for the length of
`restartInstance` (released in its `finally`, so also on failure) unless an init or wake already holds input.
`awaitInstanceInputReady` runs before the bubble is published, so the transcript has no copy of the message for the replay
to carry and the message goes out once, after the restart. `instance-lifecycle-spawn-rollback.spec.ts` (describe "input
sent during an in-place restart") covers hold while spawning, release after success and failure, and an existing hold left
in place; the first case failed with the hold line disabled. Live repeat in a rebuilt dev app: CLI child (direct child of
the dev app) killed with `kill -9`; the automatic restart began 21 s later (03:48:11.3Z) and the message was sent at
03:48:12.5Z, mid-restart. The log shows `INSTANCE_SEND_INPUT` at 03:48:12.487, the replay fallback succeeding at
03:48:12.873 and `sendInput called` at 03:48:12.880 with `adapterExists: true`. The single bubble went `sending` then
`accepted`, the model answered "LT-RETRY-OK2" once, no error row appeared and the composer was empty.

<a id="lt-1110"></a>

## LT-1110

### LT-1110 — Pause and "move in progress" abort a landing that is already committing

**Status: reproduced live 11 November 2026; fixed and re-run live 12 November 2026 (Pause and a move-in-progress route change now wait for a running commit hook; the document lands in the same round).**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app from the queue worktree, scratch repository whose pre-commit hook sleeps 50 s while a marker file exists (a
global `core.hooksPath` had to be overridden locally for the hook to run at all). Plans of two lines, Codex worker,
Claude checker.

1. Route change with "move in progress" (`planQueueControl set-routing`, `moveInProgress: true`) sent 7 s into the
   hook (log `slow hook start 21:23:49`, change at 21:23:56): the hook never wrote its end line, the item went back
   to `verifying` with a new Claude checker (round 1 to 2), and it landed on a second hook run (21:24:10 to
   21:25:00). A first attempt, sent 3 s after the check passed and before the hook began, behaved the same way.
2. Plain Pause on the page 9 s into the hook (start 21:28:32, Pause 21:28:41): the item became `awaiting-slot`, detail
   "Paused before landing.", the hook never finished, `main` and the item's folder were untouched. Resume re-checked
   it (round 1 to 2) and it landed.

### Root cause (from the code, not yet changed)

`PlanQueueCoordinator` `holdRun` (`plan-queue-coordinator.ts:568`) calls `flow.hold(item.id)` with no `stillHeld`
test. `PlanQueueItemFlow.hold` (`plan-queue-item-flow.ts:263`) then calls `landing.cancel(itemId)`, which aborts the
landing's `AbortController`. The signal reaches `commitWithHooks` (`plan-queue-squash.ts:276`) and
`runInProcessGroup` (`plan-queue-process.ts:102`), which kills the hook. `PlanQueueItemLanding.land` also aborts a
landing at once when the run is `paused` (`plan-queue-item-landing.ts:98`), and its abort handler moves the item to
`awaiting-slot` "Paused before landing" (`plan-queue-item-landing.ts:107-112`). The hold comment at
`plan-queue-item-flow.ts:257-260` promises a targeted hold does not abort a landing, but `holdRun` is not one.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A landing whose commit has begun finishes, as decision 2 of the plan states: Pause and a move-in-progress route
change wait for it, then hold the item. A landing that has not reached its commit may still be held. Acceptance: with
a slow commit hook, Pause (and a move route change) pressed during the hook leaves the hook to finish, the document
lands once without another check round, and the run is then paused or on the new route.

### Repair (12 November 2026)

`buildLandingCommit` (`plan-queue-squash.ts`) calls `beginCommit` right before the hook and runs the hook without an abort signal; `PlanQueueItemLanding.cancel` (`plan-queue-item-landing.ts`) skips a landing in its `committing` set; `landItemBranch` passes the callback. Pause and a move-in-progress route change still stop a landing before its commit. Tests: `plan-queue-pause-landing.spec.ts` (new case, mutation-checked), `plan-queue-item-stage.spec.ts`. Live re-run on a rebuilt dev app with the 50 s hook: Pause at 8 s and a move-in-progress route change at 6 s into the hook both left the hook to finish, and the document landed in round 1 (`461dea1`, `5274a92`). Details are in the livetest document's 2026-11-12 section.

<a id="lt-1067"></a>

## LT-1067 — an expired delegated task leaves the stuck-process detector armed on an idle session

**Status: open, reproduced 10 November 2026. No source change made.**

Origin: [provider hardening check 2](2026-10-02-provider-hardening_livetest.md), second case (child stops showing activity).

### Observed behaviour

Dev app (isolated profile, OpenCode 1.19.5, free `opencode/big-pickle` model, YOLO, root orchestrated session
`iengl8rxs`). A foreground Task child started three `bash` calls at 05:52:48Z that never returned (a bare
`opencode export` of the child shows all three parts `running` for the whole hour). At 06:52:48Z, exactly 60 minutes
after the child's last activity, Harness ended the turn correctly: the transcript got "The delegated task stopped
showing any activity before its time ran out…" and `Instance error … recoverableKind: acp-prompt-timeout`, and the
instance was `idle` (readback at 06:55:18Z). Then:

- 06:54:55Z `StuckProcessDetector` "Process alive — deferring stuck warning", `state: "generating"`, `elapsedMs: 126269`
  (so its clock started at about 06:52:48.9Z, right after the `Tool execution reported an error` line at 06:52:48.682Z).
- 06:55:05Z soft warning "No output for 136s. If it stays silent, Harness will restart the session." in the transcript
  of an idle session.
- 07:00:55Z "Process stuck — hard timeout exceeded" → `InterruptRespawn` respawn (the old CLI, still running the
  child's bash, was terminated) → 07:00:59Z `sendInput … autoContinuation: true` ("Continuing the interrupted turn
  automatically (attempt 1 of 2)") → 07:01:04Z a new `task` tool call. The work the notice told the user to check
  first was started again with no user action.

Receipts (metadata only): `_scratch/ph-lt-20261110/receipts/stuck-child-rows.json` and `stuck-child-applog.txt` in the
queue worktree of this item.

### Root cause

`instance-communication.ts` (adapter output handler, about line 1290) calls `onToolStateChange(id, 'generating')` for
every `tool_result` message. The timeout path emits the error, the idle transition and the cancelled `tool_result`
within the same 30 ms, and the `tool_result` arrives after the `'idle'` call, so the detector ends in `generating`
on an idle instance. `StuckProcessDetector.checkAll` (`stuck-process-detector.ts` about line 372) only skips trackers
whose own state is `idle`; it does not consult the instance status, and the `process:stuck` handler in
`instance-manager.ts` (about line 682) calls `respawnAfterInterrupt` without checking it either. The ordering is
inferred from the timestamps above; the handler order was not instrumented.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A `tool_result` that arrives after the instance has gone idle must not re-arm the detector, or the detector's hard
timeout must not respawn an instance whose status is `idle`. Acceptance: a unit test where an idle instance receives a
late `tool_result` and the detector never emits `process:stuck`; and live, the same stuck-child run ends at the
"delegated task stopped" notice and stays idle with no soft warning, no respawn and no automatic continuation.

## LT-1119

### LT-1119 — the leftover-program sweeper has no back-off when the process table is slow or unreadable

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026; rebuilt-app check pending. Observed 11 November 2026 in the production `app.log` series.**

### Observed behaviour

From the Harness logs (`app.log` and its four rotated files, 10 to 11 November 2026), subsystem `LeftoverProcessSweeper`:

- `Leftover process table read` lines (written only for a run's first read, or any read over 500 ms): 720 lines, 1,093 to
  2,487 rows each. `costMs` minimum 255, median 1,229, 90th percentile 3,043, maximum 8,318. Only 3 of the 720 are under
  500 ms. The livetest asks for "well under 500". The Mac was at a load average of 50 to 350 on 18 cores, so this
  measures an overloaded host, not an idle one; no read on a quiet machine has been logged yet.
- 16 warnings `Leftover process check failed: Command failed: ps -A -ww ...` between 10 November 21:19Z and 11 November
  05:47Z. `host-process-inspector.ts:26` sets `PS_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000` and the slowest logged read was 8.3 s, which fits a
  timed-out `ps`, but no log line states the reason, so this is untested.
- 4,012 identical `Leftover process check failed: spawn EPERM` warnings. This run's own dev app, started from an agent
  sandbox that blocks `ps`, logged the same warning every 10 s from its first tick; the other writers are presumed to be
  the same kind of app but were not individually checked. The sweeper warns every tick for as long as the app runs.

No parse failure from the BSD `time` column appears in any log (see the evidence run for LS-1).

### Root cause

Not established. The tick (`LINEAGE_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000`) reads the whole table whenever a session is live, and every sixth
tick also reads the environment table, whatever the previous read cost or whether the last read failed. Nothing
lengthens the interval after a slow or failed read.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After a read that is slow (over the 500 ms threshold already logged) or fails, the sweeper waits longer before the next
read, and returns to 10 s once reads are quick again; a repeated identical failure is logged once, then summarised, not
every tick. Acceptance: a spec with a fake `runPs` that is slow or throws shows the interval growing and resetting, and the
repeated-failure case logs once; on the rebuilt app, `app.log` shows no run of identical failures at 10 s spacing. Measure
`costMs` on a quiet Mac as well, before deciding the threshold.

### As built (12 November 2026)

`leftover-process-sweeper.ts`: a table read slower than `SLOW_TABLE_MS` (500 ms) or a failed tick sets a skip of 1 tick,
doubling on each repeat up to `MAX_BACKOFF_TICKS` (6, a minute); the next fast read resets the length to 0. A failure is
logged as a warning when it first appears or its message changes, then once per `REPEAT_FAILURE_LOG_EVERY` (30) repeats,
with the repeat count; a later successful tick logs one "works again" line. Specs in `leftover-process-sweeper.spec.ts`:
slow reads (31 table reads in 5 minutes without the fix, under 10 with it, back to every tick afterwards) and a repeating
failure (3 warnings without the fix, 1, then 2 after the message changes). Both specs fail with the skip disabled.
Still open: a table-read cost figure on a quiet Mac, and a rebuilt-app check that `app.log` shows no run of identical
failures at 10 s spacing.

### Rebuilt-copy check for LT-1119 (14 November 2026)

On the test Mac (copy built from this worktree, load 24 to 36 on 10 cores) the first table read of each run logged `rows` 1,807 to 1,862 and `costMs` 85 to 93, a direct `ps -A -ww` took 74 to 76 ms eight times in a row, no `Leftover process check failed` warning appeared in the whole test Mac log, and no read was slow. So the back-off never had to act on a live machine; its behaviour is covered by the two specs. The machine was loaded, not quiet.

## LT-1118

### LT-1118 — a dev app started on the test Mac cannot find the `aio-mcp` helper, so its sessions get no marker and no orchestrator tools

**Status: reproduced live 14 November 2026; not repaired. Test tooling and path lookup, found while running the leftover-programs live checks.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app started with `node scripts/remote-checks/dev-app.js start --port 9648 --data /tmp/aio-lt-queue-a4ff3794` (copy built from
this worktree; `dist/aio-mcp-cli-sea/aio-mcp` exists in its checkout, 124 MB, built 05:18Z):

- Its main process has working folder `/` (`lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd` shows `/`), while `dev-app shell` runs in
  `~/remote-checks/devapps/apps/9648/repo`.
- `app.log` on the test Mac, for the copy's first session (`c1u0mib0i`, 05:19:48Z): `Codemem MCP not configured — aio-mcp SEA binary
  or codemem RPC socket missing` and `Orchestrator-tools MCP not configured — aio-mcp SEA binary, RPC socket or instance capability
  missing`; at start-up `aio-mcp SEA binary not found — Chrome native-messaging host wrapper not installed`. The orchestrator-tools
  RPC server itself was listening (`/tmp/aio-lt-queue-a4ff3794/ot-c364603f4a43.sock`), so the socket and capability were present.
- A Claude session in the copy asked for `list_host_processes`: "The tool isn't available in this session" (ToolSearch found nothing).
  A background `node` started from that session had no `AI_ORCHESTRATOR_INSTANCE_ID` in its environment (`ps eww -p <pid>`), so the
  sweeper's marker route could not attribute it; only the recorded process groups attributed anything.

### Root cause

`scripts/remote-checks/remote-run.sh` opens the copy with `open -n -g -a Electron.app --args ... "$work"` so it can read the login
keychain; Launch Services starts it with working folder `/`. `src/main/util/aio-mcp-cli-path.ts:40` looks for
`dist/aio-mcp-cli-sea/aio-mcp` relative to `options.cwd ?? process.cwd()` and, in an unpackaged run, there is no
`process.resourcesPath` candidate, so it returns null. `spawn-config-builder.ts` then skips the orchestrator-tools config
(including the marker and `AIO_MCP`) and the codemem config.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A development copy finds the helper wherever it was started from: either resolve the dev candidate from the application folder
(the folder Electron was given) instead of the working folder, or have the launcher set the working folder to the checkout. Acceptance:
in a copy started by `dev-app.js`, a Claude session's shell commands carry `AI_ORCHESTRATOR_INSTANCE_ID`, `AIO_MCP` is set, the session
lists the orchestrator tools (`list_host_processes`), and `app.log` shows no `Orchestrator-tools MCP not configured` line.

### Second reproduction, 14 November 2026

The agent-issued pairing live checks hit the same fault independently (`dev-app.js start --port 9755`, test Mac): two yolo Claude sessions had no `AIO_MCP` or `AI_ORCHESTRATOR_*` variables, `$AIO_MCP remote-nodes pair` found nothing, and ToolSearch did not list `issue_remote_node_pairing`. The root cause is the one above (`resolveAioMcpCliPath`, `src/main/util/aio-mcp-cli-path.ts`, working folder `/` under `open`). Evidence: [agent-issued pairing live checks](2026-11-07-agent-issued-remote-node-pairing_plan_livetest.md).

## LT-1099

### LT-1099 — explicit Harness deny rules never match on the legacy permission-denial path

**Status: fixed and rechecked live on 12 November 2026 (verifier round 1 of the permission remediation item).**

### Observed behaviour

In an isolated dev app, a non-YOLO Claude session whose adapter had no permission hook (the legacy `permission_denial`
class that LT-708 kept reachable) was asked to run `rtk proxy pwd`. A project rule in the disposable workspace
(`.orchestrator/permissions.json`, rule `bash_execute` literal `bash:rtk proxy pwd`, action deny) was loaded. The CLI
returned the genuine error `This command requires approval`, and the card still offered **Always allow (adds a rule to
~/.claude/settings.json and restarts)**. A second workspace used a rule in the scope the legacy branch actually uses
(`tool_use`, literal `bash:rtk proxy pwd`, deny) and showed the same card. On the normal hooked path the first rule
was honoured: the session logged `Permission auto-denied for Bash: Matched rule: LT fixture deny pwd`, showed no card
and the model was told Harness's rules refused the call. For a read of a file outside the folder, the legacy request's
resource was `<working folder>/from /tmp/.../protected/data.txt`, which no real path rule can match (the call was
refused anyway by the filesystem policy, not by the fixture rule).

### Root cause

`InstancePermissionRequestFlow.handleInputRequiredInternal` (`src/main/instance/instance-permission-request-flow.ts`,
the `permission_denial` branch) builds its resource from `meta['path']`. The adapter puts the shortened display label
there (`claude-cli-adapter.ts`, `path: displayPath`) and the real value in `full_path`. For Bash, and any input that is
not path-like, `describePermissionTarget` (`claude-cli-permission-details.ts`) returns `command (13 chars)`, so the gate
sees `bash:command (13 chars)`. Calling the live gate directly with the same fixture showed `bash:rtk proxy pwd` ->
deny (`Matched rule: LT fixture deny tool_use pwd`) and `bash:command (13 chars)` -> ask (`No matching rule`). For reads,
the CLI wording `permissions to read from <path>` makes `extractPermissionDetails` return `from <path>`, and
`normalizeRequestedPath` joins it onto the working folder.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The branch evaluates the gate with the real tool input (`full_path`, and the original Bash command carried in the
tool-use context) and the scope the hooked path uses (`bash_execute` for Bash), and strips the leading `from ` from read
targets. Display labels stay shortened. An explicit deny short-circuits as the branch's own comment says it should, with
no override card. Acceptance: a new spec drives a `permission_denial` with a Bash command and a matching literal deny
rule and expects no `instance:input-required` event; a read-target case expects the exact path; a command without a rule
still reaches the card. On the rebuilt app the two fixtures above end with a system note and no card.

### As built

`instance-permission-request-flow.ts` (the `permission_denial` branch) now reads `meta.full_path` (falling back to `path`),
judges a Bash denial with `deferredPermissionResource('Bash', { command })` (scope `bash_execute`, resource `bash:<command>`, gate
tool input `{ command }`), and clears the pending entry when it auto-denies. `claude-cli-permission-details.ts` drops the `from `
wording from `permissions to read from <path>` so `full_path` is the exact path. New specs: the flow spec group "permission_denial
is judged by the real target" (three of four cases fail without the fix) and `extractPermissionDetails targets`. Rebuilt-app
recheck: hookless session in the workspace with the `bash_execute` deny rule ends with `Permission auto-denied for Bash: Matched rule:
LT fixture deny pwd`, no input event and no card; a read of the protected file is refused with the exact path in the reason
(filesystem policy answers first, so the file rule itself is covered by the unit spec); a hookless session with no rule still shows
the card and rejecting it leaves both settings files byte-identical.

## LT-1092

### LT-1092 — Escape in a clean-up dialog also closes Settings

**Status: fixed in the working tree 11 November 2026; landing pending.**

### Observed behaviour

On a rebuilt dev app (isolated profile), Settings → Health → Doctor → Storage → "Review and clear" opened the dialog.
A real Escape key press (`Input.dispatchKeyEvent`) closed the dialog and also navigated from `/settings#doctor` to `/`.
The Cancel button closed only the dialog. The leftover work-folder removal dialog has the same Escape binding.

### Root cause

`settings.component.html:5` binds `(keydown)="onKeydown($event)"` on the Settings host, and `onKeydown` calls `goBack()` for
Escape unless the Help drawer or compact navigation took it first (`settings.component.ts`). Both dialogs handled
`(keydown.escape)="store.cancel()"` without stopping propagation, so the same key also reached the Settings host.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Escape closes the deepest open overlay only. Both dialogs now use `(keydown.escape)="$event.stopPropagation(); store.cancel()"`.
Acceptance: `storage-usage-card.component.spec.ts` and `leftover-worktrees-card.component.spec.ts` case "keeps Escape inside
the dialog so Settings stays open"; on the rebuilt app a real Escape in the backups dialog closed the dialog, left the URL at
`/settings#doctor`, and kept the fixture file. The work-folder removal dialog's identical change is covered by its unit test only, not by a live key press.

## LT-1093

### LT-1093 — an `.asar` file reads as a folder, so retired work folders cannot be inspected or archived

**Status: fixed in the working tree 11 November 2026; landing pending.**

### Observed behaviour

With a Harness-made, 56-day-old fixture folder holding `node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/Resources/default_app.asar`,
the Doctor card showed "Folder details could not be verified. Harness will not remove it." and the report error
`ENOTDIR: not a directory, opendir '…/default_app.asar'`. Against the real repository, 12 of the roughly 100 listed folders (those with a real `node_modules/electron`)
failed the same way before the change; after it, 99 rows were read with 0 errors.

### Root cause

Electron patches `fs` so an `.asar` file is a folder: `lstat` reports `isDirectory() === true`, size 0, while `opendir` still fails
with ENOTDIR (measured with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` against plain Node). `folderBytes` in `leftover-worktree-report.ts` and
`worktreeFingerprint`/`cp` in `leftover-worktree-archive.ts` trusted `lstat`. The fingerprint of such a folder also differed between
Electron and plain Node, so an archive would fail its own verification. `remove-tree.ts` already solved the delete side (2026-10-26).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Scans, hashes and copies of checkouts use Electron's unpatched `fs`. New `src/main/util/unpatched-fs.ts` returns `original-fs` inside
Electron and plain `fs` elsewhere; `removeTree`, the report and the archive module use it. Acceptance:
`leftover-worktree-asar.spec.ts` (runs the real code under Electron-as-Node; both cases failed before the change and pass after),
`remove-tree.spec.ts` unchanged and passing; live: the fixture reported 111,043 bytes, archived, was removed with its branch kept,
and Restore reproduced every file and permission.

## LT-1094

### LT-1094 — every CLI update pill refresh was blocked by the renderer event schema

**Status: fixed in the working tree 11 November 2026; landing pending.**

### Observed behaviour

At every dev-app start the log carried `Blocked invalid renderer event payload` for channel `cli-update-pill:delta` with
`Unrecognized key: "waitingSessionCount"` (5 times in the first run, 2 in each restart).

### Root cause

`CliUpdatePillStateEventSchema` (`packages/contracts/src/schemas/observability.schemas.ts`) is `.strict()` and omitted
`waitingSessionCount`. `CliUpdatePollService.refreshInternal` puts that key on every state it emits (set or `undefined`), and
`setWaitingSessionCount` emits states carrying a number, so every push was dropped before reaching the pill.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The schema lists `waitingSessionCount` as an optional non-negative integer. Acceptance: `renderer-event-validation.spec.ts` case
"CLI update pill delta validation" (failed without the field); live: a refresh delivered one delta with the key present and zero
blocked-payload lines were logged in that run.

## LT-1096

### LT-1096 — storage card shows 0 B silently when the profile path contains a symlink

**Status: open.**

### Observed behaviour

With `AIO_DEV_USER_DATA_PATH=/tmp/aio-lt-queue-abb47706` (macOS `/tmp` is a link to `/private/tmp`) the card showed "Total: 0 B", 0 B for
the learning database (a 2.8 MB folder), and 208 KiB for conversation history (read from the database, not the walk). Relaunching on the
real path `/private/tmp/aio-lt-queue-abb47706` showed 11.0 MiB, equal to an independent byte count (11,571,607).

`listStorageFiles` returns `[]` when `safeStorageDirectory` finds a link anywhere in the root's path (`storage-files.ts`). That is a deliberate

are not behind a link, so impact is low.

## LT-1097

### LT-1097 — opening the Wake screen counts every displayed note as shown

**Status: open.**

### Observed behaviour

A fixture legacy note (created and last shown 1 March, shown 3 times) read "Shown 4 times, last shown 11 Nov" after one visit to
Knowledge → Wake, and moved out of Hidden. The mined fixture notes read "Shown 1 time" with no session started. The summary line counted them
in "shown this week".

### Root cause

The screen loads `wakeGenerate`; `WakeContextBuilder.generateWakeContext` → `generateL1` calls `recordHintUsage` for the notes it renders
(`wake-context-builder.ts:254`, `:270`), which increments `usage_count` and sets `last_used`. A page view and a real prompt build are not
distinguished.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Only notes put into a session's prompt count as shown. Viewing the screen records no usage. Acceptance: after a visit to the Wake screen a
fixture note's `usage_count` and `last_used` are unchanged and legacy notes stay under Hidden. Needs a product decision on what "shown" means
for cached contexts.

## LT-1098

### LT-1098 — removing a Wake note leaves its duplicate visible

**Status: open.**

### Observed behaviour

Fixture state: the miner note "Never edit generated files by hand." and a duplicate "never  edit generated files by hand." in the same room
(shown under Hidden). After the confirmed removal the list read "5 notes, 5 different"; the duplicate became the visible note. The tombstone
was written and the miner did not re-add the note after the project changed.

### Root cause

`WakeContextBuilder.removeHint(id)` deletes one row and writes the tombstone for its normalised text, but other rows with the same
normalised text in the same room are left (`wake-context-builder.ts:137`).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Removing a note removes every copy with the same normalised text in that room (the prompt says "Removes 1 note"; it should state the true count).
Acceptance: with a duplicate fixture, one confirmed removal leaves no row with that text and the summary falls by the number of copies.
## LT-1090

### LT-1090 — opening Settings threw a route-snapshot exception in the page shell

**Status: source fix present in this branch (`b277e3f39`, `control-surface-shell.component.ts:180`); live re-check passed 11 November 2026; independent verification pending. Further Electron re-checks with the real preload passed on 12 November (coordinator Mac) and 14 November 2026 (`ct-test-mac`): dashboard, Settings, Automations, Settings and Back three times plus direct loads, 18 of 18 steps each, no exception, console error or stored renderer crash; see the [Settings navigation live checklist](2026-10-27-mimo-campaign-settings-navigation_livetest.md).**

Identifier note: the 2026-10-27 MiMo live test recorded this defect as LT-711. In this register LT-711 is the unrelated historical Cursor report, so the MiMo document's "LT-711" for this defect is wrong. The same exception was recorded as LT-723 by the host-process campaign and LT-790 by the Local AI parity campaign; neither number has a section in this register (LT-723 here is an unrelated Plan Queue check defect). Those campaigns' follow-up plans (`2026-10-27-control-surface-route-snapshot_plan_completed.md`, `2026-10-27-control-surface-route-snapshot-remediation_plan_completed.md`, `2026-10-27-mimo-campaign-settings-navigation_plan_completed.md`) keep their own numbers; this entry is the register's single record of the defect.

### Observed behaviour

On 27 October 2026 a MiMo live-test run reported that clicking the dashboard's Open settings button on a fresh production renderer raised `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')` at `ControlSurfaceShellComponent.findActiveSurfaceId`, although Settings still rendered and Accounts stayed reachable. The raw receipts for that run are no longer on disk, so this entry rests on the plans above and on the re-check below.

### Root cause

The shell constructor read the active surface synchronously and walked live `ActivatedRoute` children, whose snapshots are only assigned once their outlets activate, so a child with no snapshot yet was dereferenced (`current.snapshot.data`). Per the remediation plan, the fix walks `this.route.snapshot` and its `firstChild` chain instead, which is complete before the shell is constructed.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Opening Settings, Automations or Local AI from the shell raises no route exception, on first and later visits. Current-build check (11 November 2026, dev renderer, real Open settings and Back controls, focus emulation on, two visits): `/` to `/settings` and back twice, zero `Runtime.exceptionThrown` and zero console errors (`docs/plans/evidence/2026-11-11-mimo-saved-usage-session/settings-navigation-current-build.json`). Remaining: the follow-up plans' independent verification and their Electron integration checks.

## LT-821 — retained accounting contains an apparent cumulative duplicate

### Observed behaviour

Read-only production evidence: instance `cp6lr11gj` records $306.04632500000037 at 2026-10-26 22:39:43 UTC under a new native session ID with zero input/output/cache tokens, equal to the sum of its preceding five entries under native session `c6ea2c69-e20e-45e2-b065-b92b80852588`. The attribution log independently carries the amount.

### Root cause

A native fork inherits the source's cumulative dollars and model counters. The ledger reset a fork to zero and rebooked the inherited history. Reproduced with a real native fork: source $0.0026191300000000003, fork charge $0.0034881500000000006 against new spend of only $0.0008690200000000003. The exact callback sequence of the October row is not available and is not asserted.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Forks read the source cost state and subtract inherited dollars and model usage (as `resume` already did). Unknown inherited history stays unknown, fresh conversations start at zero, genuine counter resets are supported. Acceptance: `claude-session-cost-ledger.spec.ts` and `claude-turn-spend.integration.spec.ts` pass; native fork after the fix books only new spend. No historical row, backup or migration marker is changed and no repair of retained history is authorized.

## LT-822 — model-breakdown cost events fail renderer validation

### Observed behaviour

In the rebuilt dev app the main logger reported `cost:usage-recorded` rejected with `Unrecognized key: "byModel"` on actual priced Claude completions.

### Root cause

CostTracker attaches `byModel` and emits the entry; cost IPC forwards it unchanged; the main event bus validated against strict `CostEntryEventSchema`, which had no `byModel`. The event was suppressed before renderer delivery.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The schema accepts a bounded, strict per-model delta array without loosening unrelated fields. Acceptance: `cost-handlers.spec.ts` (tracker to handler to validator) accepts measured/estimated breakdowns and rejects unrelated fields and invalid model dollars. Full-app header/Costs update is a deferred live check in the [live-check document](2026-10-27-phase0-livetest-remediation_livetest.md).

Borrowed resident requests survive the native defer/exit and resume on the same adapter after an explicit decision, without replaying the original input; loop timeouts exclude the wait. ## LT-826 — Close all leaves the original resident provider alive

### Observed behaviour

At 10:18 UTC Close all confirmed and cancelled the borrowed loop and removed session `clnvef0s0`, but its original Claude PID 94693 stayed alive (same executable, original start time, parent app PID 14279; not a new spawn or reused PID).

### Root cause

Inherited `requestResponse` used one-shot `sendMessage`, which replaced `this.process` while the original resident process stayed alive and unreferenced.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Borrowed requests send on the resident pipe. One-shot/streaming overwrites and overlapping sends are refused; controlled restarts reap the old process first. Acceptance: `claude-resident-request.spec.ts` and `claude-cli-adapter.spec.ts` pass, and a native run through the real loan registry and termination coordinator leaves no instance, adapter or surviving PID after five seconds. Full Close all confirmation (original and invocation PIDs absent, no respawn over 30 seconds) is a deferred live check in the [live-check document](2026-10-27-phase0-livetest-remediation_livetest.md). ## LT-1028

### LT-1028 — the hub menu fills half a narrow window

Source: [Oct2 later live checks, section 4](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md), run in-loop on 9 Nov 2026 by the
set-aside merge session as a compiled renderer preview (production build of main 50b2a4287) in a worker-managed
browser on `windows-pc`. Screenshots are kept locally under `_scratch/hub-strip-fix/evidence/`.

### Observed behaviour

At an 820x800 viewport (the app window's minimum width is 800px; the narrow layout applies at 840px and below), on standard
Control Center pages the hub menu became a 353px-tall block (465px on Git) holding all twelve hubs in one column, with
empty space beside it. The page kept 280px of height on Automations and 168px on Git. "Connections" was cut in half and
"Storage" hidden unless the menu was scrolled down. Collapsing the menu saved about 3px and left a column of icons at
the far right. At 1200px the layout was correct.

### Root cause

`control-surface-shell.component.scss` turns the menu into a strip at 840px and below with `display: flex` and sideways
scrolling, written for the old menu's several groups sitting side by side. Navigation hubs (c58792194) put every hub in
one group, whose links are block-level, so they stacked. The stacked layout's implicit grid rows also share spare height
with the strip, so on a short page the strip grew further. In the collapsed state, the collapsed toggle's
`margin: 0 auto` (outside the media query, higher specificity) pushed the icons to the right.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

At 840px and below, on standard pages the hubs sit in one row about 66px tall that scrolls sideways, the page takes the
remaining height on every page, the open hub and tab scroll into view, and the collapsed strip is a row of usable icons
after the toggle. Wide and full-bleed pages keep their left column; 1200px is unchanged. Acceptance: the preview
measurements on Automations, Git and Costs & Usage at 820px (one row, 66px strip, page 567px tall, open hub visible on
load, collapsed icons 31px wide starting after the toggle); the shell spec case "scrolls the open hub and its tab into
view" fails on the old code and passes; and the rebuilt-app narrow-window check in the Oct2 later live-test section 4.

<a id="lt-1029"></a>

### LT-1029 — a disposable worker spawned from a run_on_node agent turn dies at turn end (accepted-then-disconnected symptom)

Source: [browser-gateway-wedged-tab-and-node-recovery-2026-09-11_livetest.md](/Users/suas/work/communitytech/browser-gateway-wedged-tab-and-node-recovery-2026-09-11_livetest.md),
check 3 (signed-out-Cursor refusal), rounds 3–4, 11 November 2026.

### Observed behaviour

Three disposable signed-out-CLI worker profiles on `windows-pc` (nodes `f1310c7b-6562-4dee-9644-336f6f885acc`,
`e5741e03-f967-4aab-a9ed-33eff917b87e`, `8639a145-f12c-4643-9b27-f221bcfcb2ea`) each completed a real registration:
the worker logged `[WorkerAgent] Registration accepted … enrolled: true`, and the coordinator logged `Issued remote node
session token`, `Node registered via WebSocket`, `Node registered via RPC` and started health monitoring. Yet 7–8.3 s
later the coordinator logged `Worker WebSocket closed (closeCode: 1006, closeReason: '', sessionMs: 8018 / 7189 /
8274, heartbeatAgeMs equal to sessionMs)` and 30 s later deregistered the node. The roster then showed the enrolled
node `disconnected`, so every `run_on_node` gate call targeting it failed at node matching (`No connected worker node
matching …`) before provider admission. The worker log shows no close or error line — the worker process itself was
gone. (Coordinator forensics: `~/Library/Application Support/harness/logs/app.log`, 2026-11-11 02:17–02:50 UTC.)

### Root cause

Not a registration defect. Each worker was started as a background child of the `run_on_node` coding-agent turn
(`lt3-startworker.mjs`, run by the agent's shell). When the agent turn completed (its "report SERVICE-STARTED" message),
turn teardown reaped the process tree; the worker's TCP socket died without a close handshake (WebSocket close 1006 is
the abnormal-closure code) at exactly the turn-end second in all three runs. The coordinator behaved correctly
throughout: registration, session issuance, health monitoring, the disconnect grace window, then deregistration. The
same surface symptom appears under LT-604 ("Registration accepted" on the worker while the roster says disconnected),
but the mechanism differs: LT-604 was a missing `RpcEventRouter` after a late server start, fixed in code and pending
live verification. This run is that verification — on the current packaged build a worker enrolling after app launch is
registered via RPC (`RpcEventRouter | Node registered via RPC`), heartbeats and stays connected.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

No product change is required for the observed failure. The harness procedure for long-lived test workers: start the
worker outside the agent-turn process tree (for example a Windows Task Scheduler task running a wrapper that launches
`node dist/worker-agent/index.js --config <isolated config>` with an isolated home) and confirm `list_remote_nodes`
shows the node `connected` before making any `run_on_node` gate call. Acceptance, observed 2026-11-11: the same worker
started via Task Scheduler stayed registered well past 60 s with heartbeats flowing, and
`run_on_node {node:"lt3cursor-r4", provider:"cursor"}` reached provider admission and returned the expected
`[cli_not_signed_in] Provider "cursor" is not proven signed in on worker node "lt3cursor-r4"` refusal before any
instance creation or CLI spawn. LT-604's registration-path live verification is recorded in its index row.
<a id="lt-1030"></a>

## LT-1030 — Queue health words a count of one in the plural and a sub-second wait as "0 seconds"

**Status:** reproduced live 12 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, a scratch repository), not repaired.
Found while running [the Queue health live checks](2026-11-04-pq-a5-measure_plan_livetest.md); cosmetic, no measure is wrong.

**Observed behaviour.** After one finished check the Plan Queue page and `plan_queue_status` read "3 min typically (1 checks)";
after one landing, "3 seconds typically (1 landings)"; after one slot wait, "0 seconds typically (1 starts)". The slot wait was
498 ms, which `describeHealthDuration` rounds to "0 seconds". The same helper prints "adding it to the base branch 0 seconds"
for a 177 ms step.

**Root cause.** `typical()` in `src/shared/utils/plan-queue-health-lines.ts` always appends the plural noun it is given
('checks', 'landings', 'starts'), and `describeHealthDuration` rounds to whole seconds with no case for under one second.

**Required behaviour.** A count of one reads in the singular ("1 check", "1 landing", "1 start"); a duration under one second
reads "under a second" (the 0-second wording says nothing a reader can use). Same words on the page and in the status tool.

**Acceptance.** Unit tests for `describeHealthDuration(498)` and for a count of one on each timed line; on the rebuilt app one
finished run shows "(1 check)" and a sub-second wait reads "under a second".

**Evidence.** [Queue health live checks](2026-11-04-pq-a5-measure_plan_livetest.md), evidence run 2026-11-12, checks 2 and 3.
