## LT-1120

### LT-1120 — the "planning files were moved" note is wiped by the next state change

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026 in the queue worktree; live re-run passed on that build; installed-app check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Live Plan Queue runs in an isolated dev app (scratch repository, real Claude worker) with a worker-created planning
file in the work folder. The file handling was correct every time (moved to the same path in the main folder at the
first checkpoint, never on the item branch, never on `main`; saved beside a differing root copy as
`<name>.from-queue-<item>.md`, then `-2`). But the item's note never showed it. The `PLAN_QUEUE_STATE_CHANGED`
event stream for the item shows the note set and cleared in the same millisecond:

```
07:25:04.937Z working        detail="docs/plans/scratch-note_history.md could not be moved ..."
07:25:04.937Z awaiting-slot  detail=null
```

The same happens for a successful move or a beside copy: the 'moved' and 'saved beside' notes were never present in any
later poll (`detail: null` while `verifying`, `landed`). The note was only visible when the move failed and the item
parked, or briefly during landing.

### Root cause

`PlanQueueWorktreeManager.checkpoint` returns the item with `detail` set to the planning note
(`plan-queue-worktree.ts:281`, `checkpointDetail`). The round-work caller then transitions it with an explicit
`detail: null` (`plan-queue-item-flow.ts:428`), so the note is dropped before anything reads it. Later transitions also
reset `detail` (`plan-queue-checker-spawn.ts:59`, `plan-queue-item-flow.ts:602`). `detail` is a single field for the
item's current one-line status, so a note that must outlive several state changes has no home.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After a checkpoint moves a planning file or saves it beside an existing one, James can still see which file went where
until the item lands or parks, from the Plan Queue page, without the note being overwritten by the next status line
(for example a run event or parent notification, or a separate field, rather than reusing `detail`). Acceptance: a
real-flow test (coordinator or item-flow level, not only the worktree manager) where a worker's checkpoint moves a file
and the note is still readable once the item reaches `verifying`; plus a live re-run of check 1 and check 2 of the
planning-files live test showing the note on the page after the first checkpoint.

### Fix (12 November 2026)

The note moved out of `detail` into its own item field, `planningNote` (new column `planning_note`, migration 55,
`PLANNING_NOTE_LIMIT` 4000 characters). `checkpoint` and the landing preflight append one line per report
(`appendPlanningNote`: oldest lines dropped first, a repeated line skipped); no status change touches it. It reaches the
page in the item data and shows on the item row (`.pq-item-planning-note`). Tests: `plan-queue-coordinator-landing.spec.ts`
(whole run: moved note and beside-copy note still on the landed item; fail with the fix removed), `plan-queue-planning-files.spec.ts`
(checkpoint note and the `appendPlanningNote` cases), `plan-queue-store.spec.ts` (survives a status change that clears `detail`).
Live evidence: [planning-files live test, 12 November re-run](2026-11-04-pq-a2-planning-files_plan_livetest.md#evidence-run--12-november-2026-fix-re-run-lt-1120).

## LT-1043

### LT-1043 — OpenCode 2 retry-attempt messages survive the ended turn

**Status: open on this base. A fix exists on the parked branch `queue/2026-10-16-opencode-2-support-1c80fb` (`acp-retry-state.ts`) and is not landed here. Priority P2.** Found by OpenCode 2 live check 2.2 on 27 October 2026. Earlier numbers in the livetest document: LT-723 (round 1) and LT-732 (round 3); both clash with other defects in this register.

### Observed behaviour

A native OpenCode 2.0.30 session using an authenticated Amsterdam MiMo account received HTTP 429 on a harmless prompt. Live main IPC showed repeated safe retry notices. `interruptInstance` succeeded and the instance went idle. The per-turn retry message was finalised to `Provider request ended after retrying.` (`phase:ended`) but nine other messages still said `Provider is trying the request again.` (`phase:attempting`) under independent message ids. Native fork and History restore kept those stale entries. This is a main-side transcript reproduction, not a DOM claim. The 2026-11-11 round did not rerun it (MiMo is out of quota); this base still has the code described below.

### Root cause

`OpenCodeAcpUpdates.retry` maps native `_meta["opencode/retry"]:null` to null (`src/main/cli/adapters/opencode-acp-updates.ts`). In `AcpCliAdapter.handleSessionUpdate`, null while a retry notice is active emits a new `phase:attempting` message instead of updating the owned notice. `resolveRetryNotice` finalises only that owned id, so the extra messages have no terminal update.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Retry metadata updates one owned per-turn notice; completion, error, Stop and process exit leave no notice saying another attempt is happening. Provider error bodies stay private. Acceptance: regression sequences (retrying, null attempt, retrying, then Stop, completion, terminal error) assert one owned notice; History restore and native fork do not preserve stale retry prose; the real retry check is rerun live.

## LT-1045

### LT-1045 — OpenCode complete checkpoints lack a native recovery cursor

**Status: open on this base; reproduced 11 November 2026. A fix exists on the parked branch (`acp-session-replay.ts`, `acp-runtime-snapshot.spec.ts`) and is not landed here. Priority P2.** Earlier numbers in the livetest document: LT-726 and LT-735.

### Observed behaviour

After a real OpenCode 2.0.30 turn on this base, the persisted continuity checkpoint held two messages, `conversationHistoryComplete:true` and `resumeCursor:null`. History restore of the same session sent `session/load`. The complete-checkpoint recovery path was not executed (startup archives complete autosaves to History, so the recovery list was empty); the evidence is the checkpoint plus the source below.

### Root cause

`continuity-revival.ts` (`isValidNativeCursor`, and the `resume: true` argument) only requests native resume with a valid cursor, and ACP's runtime snapshot publishes none, so a complete checkpoint never reaches `preferSessionResume`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After a successful native session open and startup configuration, the adapter snapshot publishes a canonical cursor; confirmed identity survives process exit; a complete retained checkpoint sends `session/resume` with each message restored once, and an incomplete one sends `session/load`.

## LT-1046

### LT-1046 — typed answers to an OpenCode 2 question are declined

**Status: open on this base. A fix exists on the parked branch (`isQuestionToolPermission` in `acp-elicitation-questions.ts`, used in `acp-cli-adapter.ts`; live recheck passed 2026-11-09) and is not landed here. Priority P1.** Found by OpenCode 2 check 2.5 on 8 November 2026. Earlier numbers in the livetest document: LT-1007 and LT-1018.

With Auto-approve off, the question tool first sends `session/request_permission` (options allow once, always, reject) and only then `elicitation/create`. Harness showed an approval card with a reply box; typing `red` and pressing Submit recorded "You answered: red", and the tool result was "The user declined this tool call", ending the turn with no reply. Cancel recorded "You answered: " with no text.

`selectAcpPermissionOutcome` in `src/main/cli/adapters/acp-permission-outcome.ts` returns a rejection for any reply that matches no option, and the permission gate has no answer channel.

## LT-1047

### LT-1047 — a successful OpenCode 2 compaction reports "The model sent no reply"

**Status: open. Priority P2.** Found by check 2.3 on 8 November 2026 (earlier number in the livetest document: LT-1009).

### Observed behaviour

`compactInstance` on an idle OpenCode 2.0.30 instance returned success with `method: native`. The transcript showed "Compaction completed.", the marker "— Context compacted —", then "The model sent no reply. Your message and the work above are kept." The compaction turn had `stopReason: end_turn`, `outputTokens: 0` and classifier reason `empty_result`. A later prompt was answered normally. The main log labels the completion "Codex compaction completed" for this OpenCode instance.

### Root cause

`src/main/providers/adapter-turn-ending-observation.ts` sets `emptyResult` for any completed turn with no reply text; nothing exempts compaction turns. `turn-ending-classifier.ts` classifies it `empty_result` and `turn-ending-continuation-policy.ts` produces the notice. The "Codex" label comes from `InstanceEventForwarding`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A compaction turn with no reply text is not an empty reply; the log names the provider. A native compaction on OpenCode 2 ends with the marker and no notice, and a turn that really produces no reply still shows it.

## LT-1048

### LT-1048 — the renderer drops cost-usage events that carry an origin

**Status: open. Priority P2.** Found by check 2.1 on 8 November 2026 (earlier number in the livetest document: LT-1010). Also present on main.

### Observed behaviour

After an OpenCode 2 turn on a free model the dev log showed "Blocked invalid renderer event payload" for `cost:usage-recorded` with `Unrecognized key: "origin"`. `CostEntryEventSchema` in `packages/contracts/src/schemas/cost-events.schemas.ts` is `.strict()` and has no `origin`, but main sends entries with it (`src/main/core/system/cost-tracker.ts`, `src/main/ipc/handlers/cost-handlers.ts`), validated in `renderer-event-validation.ts`.

The renderer accepts every cost entry main can send (schema carries `origin` or main strips it); a test passes a main-built entry through the validator; no blocked-event warning after an OpenCode turn.

## LT-1139

### LT-1139 — allowing a `read_session` permission card in a non-Auto-approve session ends the session in `error`

**Status: reproduced live twice on 14 November 2026; not repaired. Found while running the review follow-ups live check; it is outside that plan (the plan's read rule is not involved).**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app started with `node scripts/remote-checks/dev-app.js start --port 9618 --data /tmp/aio-lt-queue-efd4d1d0` on the test Mac (copy built from the
queue worktree; Claude signed in, no other provider; the `aio-mcp` helper linked into Electron's `Resources/aio-mcp-cli/` as a workaround for LT-1118, so
sessions have Harness tools). Two fresh Claude sessions with `yoloMode: false`, each started with a first message carrying an `@session` chip and "Read that
session with read_session and tell me its first message":

1. `i7xh7z55e`: permission card "Claude wants to run mcp__orchestrator__read_session" appeared at 10:26:36Z. I clicked **Allow this once** at 10:27:05Z.
   `app.log` (production profile path on the test Mac; the dev app writes there): `Resuming after deferred permission` (10:27:05.796), `Adapter exited during a recovery
   respawn; deferring to the recovery owner` (10:27:06.302), `Native resume attempted but unconfirmed within probe window; treating as inconclusive` (10:27:16.462),
   then `Failed to resume after deferred permission` with `Native resume did not stabilize after deferred permission` (10:27:16.468). Instance status became `error`.
2. `i030dz29g`: the same, clicked 10:29:49Z, failure logged 10:30:00Z (about 10 s later), status `error`.

In neither session did the tool run: the copy's `session_messages` read audit has no row for either session id. The same message was seen earlier the same day on a `read_session` permission card in the
first run of the follow-ups check, so it is repeatable.

Control in the same copy: a session whose pending call was `Bash` (`sleep 170; echo done`, then two follow-up Bash prompts), allowed three times, logged
`Resumed after deferred permission successfully` each time, 0.5 to 1.7 s after the click. A session that called `mcp__orchestrator__list_settings` showed no card at all (that
tool is allowed without asking), so it could not serve as a second control for an MCP tool.

### Root cause

Not isolated. What the code and log establish: the error is thrown at `src/main/instance/lifecycle/deferred-permission-handler.ts:339` (and `:274` on the resident-request
path) when `waitForResumeHealth` returns false. `waitForResumeHealth` (`instance-lifecycle.ts:1154`) returns true only for `healthy`; the interpretation helper
(`resume-attempt-interpretation.ts:59`) says an alive resume whose session-id echo has not arrived is `inconclusive`, and the boolean wrapper maps `inconclusive` to
false. The handler then sets `error` and rethrows. So an alive-but-unconfirmed resume is treated as a failed one on this path. Why the echo is late only for the MCP tool
(about 10 s here, against under 2 s for Bash) is not established; a resumed Claude process that has to bring up its MCP servers before running the approved tool call is the
obvious suspect, but I have not measured it, and I have not tried the packaged app, where it may differ.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Approving a `read_session` card (or any MCP tool card) in a non-Auto-approve session resumes the session and runs the approved call; a slow-but-alive resume is not turned
into `error`, and if the resume truly fails the user is told the approved call did not run. Acceptance: in a copy, a non-Auto-approve Claude session asked to read another
session with a chip shows the card, **Allow this once** leaves the session `busy` then `idle`, the read audit has a `read` row for it, and `app.log` has no
`Native resume did not stabilize after deferred permission` line. Add a regression test with a resume whose echo arrives after the probe window.

## LT-1121

### LT-1121 — a shared start fault sets aside every job launched in the same pass

**Status: fixed in source and verified live 14 November 2026.** Reproduced 12 November 2026. The fix: `PlanQueuePreparationErrors.defer` counts a start failure with the breaker before the job is parked (the old `failed` call after parking is gone), and `PlanQueueRunBreaker.isHeldFault` sends any start that hits the fault the run is held for back to `queued`, whether it is the trial or another start already in flight. The third matching failure sets the hold and goes back in line itself, so at most the first two are set aside. Live result on a rebuilt dev app at Workload 5: 4-plan run, 2 set aside and 2 waiting; 6-plan runs, 2 set aside and 4 waiting; 8-plan run with the fault starting after five workers were up, 2 set aside and 1 waiting while all five live jobs landed. Evidence: [Evidence run: 14 November 2026](2026-11-05-plan-queue-reliability_plan_livetest.md#evidence-run-14-november-2026).

### Observed behaviour

Run on a dev app built from the Plan Queue reliability branch, Workload 5, in disposable repositories whose `.worktrees` folder was read-only, so every worker start failed with `EACCES ... mkdir .../.worktrees/queue`.

- Default run (three worker slots, four plans), run `f`: all four jobs went `queued > preparing` within 4 ms (09:54:07.234 to .238) and were parked `worktree-error` between 09:54:07.754 and .831. Run `g` did the same.

- Six-plan runs: `h` parked five jobs in the same 120 ms (09:56:00.951 to 09:56:01.063) and left one waiting; `i` and `j` parked all six.

- The run showed "On hold" with the error text, as designed, but in `f`, `g`, `i` and `j` there was no job left waiting, so the ten-minute trial had nothing to try and the run ended `completed`.

### Root cause

Workload 5 sets `queueWorkerMinimum` to 5 (`workload-policy.ts:30`), and `queue-admission.ts:16` takes the larger of that and the run's `workerSlots`, so the pump launches five jobs in one pass (`plan-queue-pump.ts:126-131`). The breaker counts a failure only after `parkUnlocked` returns (`plan-queue-item-flow.ts:203-206`), by which point the other launches are already in flight. `PlanQueuePreparationErrors.defer` requeues a failing start only when it is the hold's own trial (`plan-queue-error-class.ts:29`), so a start that fails after the hold is in force is still parked. Jobs that fail in the same few milliseconds all park.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A start that fails with the fault the run is already held for, or that would be the third such failure, goes back to `queued` and not to Set aside, so at most the first two matching failures park a job (or none), and every other job stays waiting for the trial. Acceptance: a spec that launches five starts failing the same way in one tick leaves no more than three parked and the rest `queued`; on the rebuilt app the check 7 steps in [the reliability live checks](2026-11-05-plan-queue-reliability_plan_livetest.md) leave jobs waiting, show the ten-minute trial, and lift the hold when it succeeds.

## LT-1120

### LT-1120 — a document whose Harness command checks stay red at the round limit parks instead of going to the step-up worker

**Status: reproduced live and repaired 14 November 2026 in the "stuck worker step-up" queue item; the repair is verified live in a dev copy, shipped build pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev copy on this Mac (data `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-1f911387`, build of the step-up branch before the repair), scratch repository with one plan, run `221f616e-c02d-4ceb-b20b-2c03d162b1d9`: workers `claude / haiku`, step-up `claude / opus`, `max_rounds: 1`, `verifier_gates: ["/tmp/stepup-gate-restart.sh"]` (a script that exits 1). `plan_queue_status` showed `routing.stepUp` as `claude / opus`. The Haiku worker finished at about 07:35Z; the item went `verifying` then `parked` in under a minute with `parkReason: round-limit`, detail "Checks still fail after 1 rounds: /tmp/stepup-gate-restart.sh", `steppedUpAt: null`, no checker session, no Opus session, and no handover message to the starting session. Run status `completed`.

### Root cause

`PlanQueueVerification.prepareChecks` (`src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-verification.ts`) records a failing round when Harness's own commands are red and, at the round limit, returned `{ kind: 'park', reason: 'round-limit' }` straight away. `canStepUp` was only asked on the other path, after an independent checker's verdict (`plan-queue-item-flow.ts`, `onVerifierOutcome`). The verdict the gate path builds already carries a `code` finding ("Harness's own gate run failed"), so it is exactly the case a stronger worker can fix.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Out of rounds with Harness's own checks red, a run that has a step-up choice and a document not yet handed over goes to the step-up worker, once, through the same hand-over as the checker path (same notice to the starting session, same `steppedUpAt` mark, a fresh round count). Without a step-up choice, or after the hand-over, it parks as before.

Repair: `prepareChecks` returns a new `step-up` result when `canStepUp` is true; `startQueueVerification` hands it to the new `stepUp` callback, which `PlanQueueItemFlow.stepUp` shares with the checker path. Regression test: `plan-queue-coordinator-routing.spec.ts`, "hands a document to the step-up worker when Harness's own checks are still red at the round limit, without starting a checker" (fails with the repair removed, passes with it).

### Evidence

[Step-up live checks, evidence run 2026-11-14](2026-10-27-plan-queue-stuck-worker-step-up_plan_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-14): after the repair the same run shape (run `ff3c3495-5f7f-4d2f-9c64-ef781dc809dd`) handed the document to an Opus worker at 07:50:40Z.

## LT-1091

### LT-1091 — an apparently idle worker never applies a pending update

**Status: open, observed 11 November 2026; the stall ended by itself on 12 November 15:23; cause not established, no code changed.**

### Observed behaviour

On 11 November 2026 the coordinator's `list_remote_nodes` showed node `ct-test-mac` (Mac, worker build `a9de0f2c`, up since
9 November 00:21Z) with `autoUpdate.state: waiting_for_idle`, `targetCommit: 2924bfba` and `activeInstances: 0`, read at
07:18Z, 07:20Z and 07:27Z (`lastCheckedAt` advancing every five minutes, so the updater was running). Its own worker log
shows natural updates every few hours up to 9 November 00:21Z and none since, although windows-pc applied the three
later commits (`50b2a428` on 10 November 00:12Z, `1e25ac28` 18:52Z, `2924bfba` 20:11Z). Checked directly on the Mac over
SSH at 07:2xZ: the worker child (pid 63975) has no child processes (no terminal shell), and the managed Chrome's debug port
has no established connection (no remote browser tunnel). The coordinator log (`app.log` to `app.log.4`) holds no browser
command for the node between 10 November 01:32Z and 11 November 06:38Z (over 29 hours) and no dispatched work in the one
hour sampled (03:00-04:00Z on 11 November). The next browser commands (06:38-07:00Z) came from another session, and
nothing arrived after 07:00:30Z. The updater needs three quiet minutes, so the node should have updated at its 07:23Z check.

### Root cause

Not established. By reading `worker-activity.ts` and `worker-agent.ts:125-128`, the updater counts a node as busy while any
of these is non-zero: retained instances, local model sessions, terminal sessions, CDP tunnel sessions, or a coordinator
request still in flight (`WorkerActivity.inFlight`); and it restarts the quiet period on every request that is neither
housekeeping nor in-flight-only, plus every browser command result. The checks above rule out terminals and tunnels. The
remaining candidates are a request that started and never settled (`inFlight` stays above zero), a local model session left
open, or a periodic request that counts as work. Nothing in the worker log says which, because the updater logs nothing
while it waits.

### Follow-up observation, 14 November 2026

ct-test-mac applied `f6b4f0f3` on 12 November 15:23:03 (supervisor `Worker child exited to load an update`), about 63 hours after the first pending target (windows-pc took
`50b2a428` at 10 Nov 00:12), then `66c566c2` 13 Nov 00:46, `fb8eb1e6` 10:26, `e0cb0ebb` 11:07 and `37829d0f` 17:28, each with a coordinator `Node re-registered within disconnect grace` line.
Both nodes were `idle` on `37829d0f` at 03:40 on 14 November. No code changed between the stall and the recovery. What is known about the stuck period: the worker's coordinator socket closed 37 times on
11 and 12 November (code 1006, often about a minute after reconnecting), and the worker log is empty from 12 Nov 10:59:49 to 15:00:10 although the process uptime ran on. The coordinator logs that old have
rotated away, so the recovery cannot be matched to a coordinator event. The periodic `OpenCodeCliLaunch` warnings repeat all week, including after recovery, so they are not the cause. The holder remains unidentified
and a repeat is possible. Evidence: `evidence/2026-11-14-worker-auto-update/receipts.md`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A node with no sessions, no tunnels and no recent work reaches `idle`/updates within about eight minutes (a five-minute check
plus three quiet minutes). When it is waiting, the summary or log should name what it is waiting for (the count of
instances, local sessions, terminals, tunnels and in-flight requests, and the age of the last stamped activity) so that this
state can be diagnosed without attaching a debugger. Acceptance: first reproduce and name the holder on ct-test-mac (log the
busy reason, or read it over a debugger on the Mac only with James's say-so, since it is a shared test node); then a focused
`worker-activity.spec.ts` case for that holder, and on the rebuilt Mac worker `autoUpdate.state` moves from
`waiting_for_idle` to `idle` with `buildCommit` equal to the checkout HEAD with no sessions open.

## LT-1085

### LT-1085 — Compact now on a resident Claude session reports "The model sent no reply"

**Status: source fix verified 10 November 2026; rebuilt dev app rechecked live.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app built from this branch (`30757ee7c`), Claude CLI 2.1.321, resident session `chb5s8qoh`. Pressing Compact now (the `compactInstance` call) compacted natively: same provider session and process, `compact_boundary` trigger manual, 50,202 to 16,867 tokens, one "Context compacted" divider. It then also added a system notice, "The model sent no reply. Your message and the work above are kept.", with source `empty-result` and a Retry action. The app log showed `Provider turn completed ... outputTokens: 0, classifierReason: 'empty_result'` right after `Compaction completed`. Repeated with no queued message: same notice, so it is not caused by a queued send.

### Root cause

The raw `/compact` turn ends with an empty `result`. `ClaudeCliAdapter` completed it like any resident turn, so `adapter-turn-ending-observation.ts` saw no text, tools or thinking and classified it `empty_result`. The unit tests fed the adapter only, never the turn-ending observer, so they passed.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The compaction turn still completes (cost and usage recorded once) but is marked `compactionTurn: true` and is never judged an empty reply. Acceptance: `adapter-empty-result.spec.ts` case "does not call a provider compaction turn an empty reply (LT-1085)" and `claude-cli-adapter.native-compaction.spec.ts` (metadata assertions) pass; on the rebuilt dev app, Compact now on a resident Claude session shows only the divider (checked live 10 November on session `cqus467nh`: divider, no notice, queued messages delivered once each, recall correct).

## LT-1088

### LT-1088 — The rewrite-only RTK hook lets wrapped `git push` past a deny rule

**Status: source fix verified 13 November 2026; `rtkAutoApproveScope` stays `off` (rollout is a separate decision).**

### Observed behaviour

Claude CLI 2.1.323, bundled RTK 0.52.0, rewrite-only mode (`ORCHESTRATOR_RTK_REWRITE_ONLY=1`), disposable repo with no remote and `.claude/settings.local.json` denying `Bash(git push*)`. Plain `git push` was refused (RTK exit 2, hook printed nothing, Claude's deny rule fired). The wrapper forms were rewritten (RTK exit 3) and the hook answered `allow` with `updatedInput`: `FOO=1 git push` became `FOO=1 rtk git push`, `timeout 5 git push` became `timeout 5 rtk git push`, `git -C <dir> push` became `rtk git -C <dir> push`. All three ran (`fatal: No configured push destination`, exit 128). Control with no hook: the env and `timeout` forms were denied by Claude itself and `git -C` needed approval, so the hook turned a refusal into an executed command. Receipts: `rtk-live-check1-BEFORE-fix.json` and `rtk-live-check1-control-no-hook.json` in [the queue 354fcc evidence folder](2026-10-10-oct-phase1-token-levers_evidence/queue-354fcc-20261113/).

### Root cause

Claude matches deny and approval rules against the command the hook returns. RTK rewrites wrapper forms by inserting `rtk` after the wrapper, so the rule's `git push*` pattern no longer matches, and the hook's `allow` removes the approval step. `rtk-defer-hook.mjs` rewrite-only mode rewrote every command RTK accepted.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Rewrite-only mode never rewrites a command in which any segment starts with a `NAME=value` word, a wrapper program (`timeout`, `env`, `nice`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `sudo`, `xargs`, `exec` and similar) or `git` followed by a global option; it logs `wrapper-not-rewritten` and prints nothing. Plain commands, pipelines and `&&` chains still rewrite. Acceptance: `rtk-defer-hook.spec.ts` case "never rewrites a wrapper or prefix form" passes; live, the same probe now shows `FOO=1 git push` and `timeout 5 git push` denied by Claude and `git -C <dir> push` stopped at the approval step, with the three hook log lines reading `wrapper-not-rewritten` (checked 13 November 2026, `rtk-live-check1.json` in the same folder).

## LT-1083 — the Context details popover, home of "Compact now…", is clipped out of view by the composer panel

**Status: fixed and verified live on 13 November 2026. Priority P2.** Reproduced the same day in a rebuilt dev app (1400×900 window). The popover came in with the calm-screen phase 3 work (`ab5a879db`).

**Repair.** `context-details-popover.component.ts` now positions the popover `fixed` in the window, just above the toolbar that holds it (`place()` reads the toolbar's rectangle when the popover opens and on window resize, keeps it inside the window and caps its height to the room above). The composer panel's `overflow: hidden` no longer clips it. Unit test: `context-details-popover.component.spec.ts`, case "sits in a fixed position just above its toolbar…". Live: a rebuilt dev app, the real ring then "Compact now…" then Confirm with no style override; see the livetest's 13 Nov re-check section.

### Observed behaviour

With a Codex chat selected, clicking the context ring (`button.ctx-ring-btn`, label "Context window: N% used") opens `section.context-details` (not hidden), but nothing readable appears: the screenshot shows only a ~9 px dark strip above the composer. Measured with `getBoundingClientRect` in an idle chat: popover top 538, bottom 700; `div.input-panel` top 691, bottom 872 and `overflow: hidden`; the "Compact now…" button spans 655–685, wholly above the panel. `document.elementFromPoint` at that button's centre returns `button.backdrop`, not the button. A real mouse click there (Input.dispatchMouseEvent at x 490, y 669.75) only closes the popover; the compaction preview dialog never opens (waited 18 s, no `button.cpd-btn`). Repeated on two separate chats (one idle, one busy on a goal) with the same result. For Codex the "Compact Now" banner never shows (`resolveContextWarningLevel` returns null when `selfManagesAutoCompaction`; context reached 89.7% with no banner), so the popover is the only place a person can start a manual compaction.

### Root cause

Source-supported, not yet fixed. `ContextDetailsPopoverComponent` (`context-details-popover.component.ts`) is `position: absolute; bottom: calc(100% + 6px)` inside `app-composer-toolbar` (`position: relative`), which sits inside `.input-panel` (`input-panel.component.scss:14`, `overflow: hidden`) and `app-input-panel` (`:host { overflow: hidden }`, line 6). Everything the popover draws above the panel's top edge, which is nearly all of its 162+ px, is clipped.

### Required behaviour

The popover and its "Compact now…" button are fully visible and clickable from the context ring in the normal composer, at normal window sizes, including while a turn is running.

### Acceptance

A renderer test or rendered-DOM check that opens the popover in the real composer layout and asserts that the "Compact now…" button's centre point hit-tests to the button itself (not the backdrop) and lies inside the visible window. Live: with a Codex chat busy on a goal, open the ring, click "Compact now…", click Confirm, and see the busy refusal ("Busy: compaction is available once the current turn finishes.") from the real control with no style override.

[Codex goal-following livetest](2026-10-27-codex-goal-following-remediation_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-13-queue-worker-rebuilt-dev-app), Check 3. With only a test-injected `div.input-panel, app-input-panel { overflow: visible !important }` the same button is reachable, opens the dialog, and Confirm returns the busy refusal, so the action works once it can be clicked. ## LT-1084 — status goes idle 250 ms after a goal turn's final answer, before Codex ends the turn

**Status: fixed and verified on 13 November 2026. Priority P2.** Found by the independent verifier's round-2 review of the goal-following livetest, which pointed at a 1.6 s idle span recorded in Check 1's Run B. A recurrence of the LT-683 acceptance ("no idle span longer than the turn gap").

### Observed behaviour

Run B (instance in a rebuilt dev app, 13 Nov 2026): the final reply of native turn `b420ee` was written to the rollout at 19:13:52.769 and Codex's own `task_complete` at 19:13:54.608 (1.84 s later; the normal gap is 65 to 130 ms, measured over 32 other turns). The chat status went `idle` at 19:13:53.051, 0.28 s after the reply, and back to `busy` at 19:13:54.824 when the next goal turn started. The Stop button was gone for those 1.6 s while the native turn was open.

### Root cause

Source-supported and matching the timing. `handleItemCompleted` (`codex-notification-item-events.ts`) called `scheduleInferredCompletion` on every root-thread `final_answer`. That timer (`INFERRED_COMPLETION_MS = 250` in `codex-app-server-notification-adapter.ts`) calls `completeTurn(state, null)`, which resolves the capture, and the provider-turn follow code then emits `idle` (`codex-app-server-turn-adapter.ts`, the `.finally` after `finishProviderTurn`). The inference exists for multi-agent turns whose root `turn/completed` may not arrive after the helper agents drain; a plain turn always gets `turn/completed`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A turn that used no helper threads is completed only by Codex's own `turn/completed`, however long after the final answer it arrives; a turn that used helper threads still gets the inferred completion. Acceptance: `codex-notification-item-events.spec.ts` ("records a completed agent message on the root thread" now expects no inference; "still infers completion after a final answer when helper threads took part") and `codex-cli-adapter.app-server.spec.ts` ("keeps a plain turn open until Codex sends turn/completed, however long after the final answer"); both new expectations fail on the old code. Live, rebuilt app: four 8-turn goals (28 turn boundaries) had idle spans of 3 to 17 ms, each matching the native gap, none starting while a native turn was open, every `TURN-n` reply once, 7 of 7 provider-started turns followed per run, no error lines. The 1.8 s tail itself did not recur live, so the slow-tail case is proved by the unit test, not by a live repeat.

### Evidence

[Codex goal-following livetest](2026-10-27-codex-goal-following-remediation_livetest.md#check-1-idle-while-the-native-turn-was-open--lt-1084--2026-11-13-queue-worker-third-pass).

## LT-1090 — a context-policy steer loses Codex's reply to it and the session reads idle early

Found by the Codex compaction lifecycle follow-up current-build live check 7 (see
`2026-10-27-codex-compaction-lifecycle-followup_livetest.md`, evidence run 2026-11-13). Source
`f6b4f0f36`, isolated profile `/tmp/aio-lt-queue-ce682cdf`, real Codex app-server.

### Observed behaviour

Twice, on instance `x2brmqwql` (thread `01a1d661-a4e4-7fc1-810c-80df4e067057`), a numbered-list task
was running when the real configured executor ran `steer-turn` on its first `agentMessage` start. The
executor returned `executed / acknowledged`; the provider request was a developer-role
`thread/inject_items` message; the Harness-authored notice (`internalInput.actor:harness`,
`source:context-policy`) was added. The original list then completed. Then:

- Run 1: the first agent message (`final_answer`) completed at `1794598577378`; Harness status went
  **idle at `1794598577636`** (final answer + about 250 ms). Codex kept the same turn open, started a
  second `agentMessage` at `1794598580121`, completed it at `1794598580218`
  ("The full list of 120 different tree species is complete.") and sent `turn/completed` at
  `1794598580346`. That second message is **absent from the transcript** (the buffer holds the user
  prompt, the first assistant row and the policy notice only).
- Run 2 (100 bird names): final answer completed `1794599723986`, status **idle `1794599724243`**,
  second message "The complete list of 100 different bird species is finished." completed
  `1794599731652`, `turn/completed` `1794599731777`. Same result: idle 7.5 s early, reply missing.

### Root cause

`CodexAppServerThreadRuntime.steerActiveTurn` (`app-server-thread-runtime.ts`) sends the developer item
but never sets `active.state.steeredInputAccepted`. Only `steerProviderTurn` does (LT-680). So
`scheduleInferredCompletion` (`codex-app-server-notification-adapter.ts`, `INFERRED_COMPLETION_MS = 250`)
completes the turn after the final answer; everything Codex streams afterwards in that turn goes to the
idle handler, which keeps only usage and compaction events. Source reading only; no fix was attempted.

### Implementation status (2026-11-13)

Fix written, not yet closed. `src/main/cli/adapters/codex/app-server-thread-runtime.ts`: `steerActiveTurn` calls the shared
`markSteeredInputAccepted` (`app-server-types.ts`) after `thread/inject_items` is acknowledged; `steerProviderTurn`
uses the same helper for `turn/steer`. Tests: `app-server-thread-runtime.spec.ts` ("keeps the turn open for the provider
after an accepted policy steer") and `codex-cli-adapter.app-server.spec.ts` ("publishes the reply that follows a policy
steer and completes only on turn/completed"); the adapter test fails on the previous source with
`expected [ 'The list' ] to include 'The list is complete.'`.

Live recheck (isolated app on `951663e02` plus this fix, real Codex 0.169.0): five runs, status idle only 3 to 16 ms after
the provider's `turn/completed`, 1.1 to 6.3 s after the final answer where the earlier build went idle 250 ms after it.
That part of the acceptance is met live. **The other part is not:** in all five runs Codex's message after the steer had
empty text, so the transcript never showed a post-steer reply and the non-empty path is exercised only by the synthetic
adapter test. Do not read this as live-verified. What would close it: one more live run in which the steered task makes
Codex write a non-empty follow-up message after the steer (for example a task whose final answer is followed by a
summary), seen in the transcript, or an explicit decision by James that the adapter regression is enough. Evidence:
`docs/plans/2026-10-27-codex-compaction-lifecycle-followup_evidence/2026-11-13-livetest-round2/`.

### Live proof, 2026-11-16 (checkout `f0b3c7380`, isolated app, real Codex 0.169.0)

Instance `x492emjyb`, thread `01a1e4b5-942f-7022-8a39-36709dda8aae`. A labelled test-fixture prompt (list of mountains or
rivers; "if an automated notice from Harness reaches you while you work, start your next message with the words NOTICE
SEEN, then finish the list") was sent, and the actual configured `steer-turn` executor ran on the first `agentMessage`
start (`executed / acknowledged`, developer-role `thread/inject_items`, Harness-authored system row, no policy text as a
user row). Run 1: first answer completed `1794839263455`, second `agentMessage` "NOTICE SEEN / The list was completed."
completed `1794839268376`, `turn/completed` `1794839268501`, status idle `1794839268508` (7 ms after). Run 2: second
message completed `1794839334512`, `turn/completed` `...609`, idle `...613`. Both replies are in the transcript as
assistant rows. The fixture prompt is a test input, not a product change; it is the only difference from the earlier
runs whose post-steer message was empty. Evidence:
`docs/plans/2026-10-27-codex-compaction-lifecycle-followup_evidence/2026-11-16-livetest-round4/`
(`steer-state-run1-result.json`, `steer-state-run2-result.json`, `steer-buffer-result.json`).

### Required behaviour

A policy steer accepted into a running Codex turn must keep that turn's capture open until Codex reports
`turn/completed`, publish every item of the turn (including the reply to the steer) and keep status busy
until then.

### Acceptance

- Adapter-level regression: a turn emits a `final_answer`, a policy steer is accepted before the 250 ms
  timer, then a further agent message and `turn/completed` arrive; the later message is emitted and status
  never goes idle before `turn/completed`. It fails on current source.
- Live repeat of check 7 with a rebuilt app shows the post-steer reply in the transcript and busy until
  real completion. **Met live on `f0b3c7380`, 2026-11-16** (details under "Live proof, 2026-11-16"). Earlier plain
  runs: busy until real completion 5 of 5, post-steer message empty.
- Focused tests, canonical gates and fresh review pass before any completed claim.

Evidence: `docs/plans/2026-10-27-codex-compaction-lifecycle-followup_evidence/2026-11-13-livetest/`
(`steer-main.run1.ndjson`, `steer-main.run2.ndjson`, `steer-state-run1-result.json`,
`steer-state-run2-result.json`, `steer-buffer-run2-result.json`). Times are Unix milliseconds.

## LT-1018

### LT-1018 — priced cost events are blocked by the renderer event check

**Status: fixed and verified live on 12 November 2026.**

### Observed behaviour

In an isolated dev app built from this branch, a Claude Haiku turn priced correctly (cost entry and header total), but the
main log carried `Blocked invalid renderer event payload` for channel `cost:usage-recorded` with
`Unrecognized key: "origin"` on every completed turn. The renderer never received the event, so the open Costs page only
changed on its 10-second poll. The same defect class as LT-822 (`byModel`), which was fixed without noticing `origin`.

### Root cause

`communication-completion-cost.ts` passes `origin` (`machine` or `user`) to `CostTracker.recordUsage`, which stores it on the
entry (`cost-tracker.ts`, `CostEntry.origin`). The cost handler forwards the whole entry, and `CostEntryEventSchema`
(`packages/contracts/src/schemas/cost-events.schemas.ts`) is `.strict()` and had no `origin` field. The earlier regression
test recorded usage without an origin, so it could not catch this.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The event schema accepts a non-empty `origin` string (up to 100 characters; the tracker documents future open tags) and still
rejects an empty one or any other unknown key. Acceptance: `cost-handlers.spec.ts` case "delivers the session origin the
completion recorder attaches to every priced turn" (failed before the fix, passes after). Live: after the rebuild, two
Haiku turns each reached the renderer 1.8 to 1.9 seconds after the send with `origin: "user"`, the Costs page changed 0.17
seconds after the event (not on the poll), and the log held no `Unrecognized key` line.

## LT-1019

### LT-1019 — the CLI update pill event is blocked at every start-up

**Status: fixed and verified live on 12 November 2026.**

### Observed behaviour

Every launch of the isolated dev app logged `Blocked invalid renderer event payload` for `cli-update-pill:delta`,
`Unrecognized key: "waitingSessionCount"`.

### Root cause

`CliUpdatePollService.setWaitingSessionCount` and `refreshInternal` put `waitingSessionCount` on the pill state
(`CliUpdatePillState.waitingSessionCount`, `diagnostics.types.ts`), and the pill component reads it. The strict
`CliUpdatePillStateEventSchema` (`observability.schemas.ts`) did not list it.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The schema accepts a non-negative integer `waitingSessionCount`. Acceptance: `renderer-event-validation.spec.ts` case
"delivers the waiting-session count the poll service adds to its state" (failed before, passes after). Live: after the
rebuild, start-up logged no blocked event.

## LT-1131

### LT-1131 — approving a held permission inside a loop kills the resumed process

**Status: source fix in the queue branch; rechecked live on 14 November 2026 (see the Phase 0 live checks). Priority P1.** Found while closing the full-app check for LT-823.

### Observed behaviour

In an isolated dev app on the test Mac (Claude CLI 2.1.319), a real `/goal` that needed Bash with auto-approve off showed the permission card. Clicking **Allow this once** ran the command once (the marker file held one line), but the loop then paused with "Step 1 stopped without finishing (Degraded iteration (invocation-error) ...)" and the session went to `error`. Reproduced four times: three `/goal` sessions (held 31 minutes, 24 seconds and 12 seconds, the last with extra logging) and a control started with `loopStart` instead of `/goal`. Ordinary chat approval on the same machine worked.

### Root cause

`DeferredPermissionHandler.resumeAfterDeferredPermission` (resident-request branch) calls `waitForResumeHealth`, which maps anything other than `healthy` to false and then terminates the adapter. `RuntimeReadinessCoordinator.evaluateResumeHealth` ended its probe on the first adapter `output` event whenever no proof was available yet (`finishProven(proof ?? true)`). A resumed Claude CLI re-runs the deferred tool first and sends `system/init` (the session-id echo that confirms the resume) afterwards. That order was seen with CLI 2.1.319 on a busy test Mac; the 12 November run on a newer CLI saw the echo first, so the order depends on CLI version or load, and the probe must not rely on it. Logged order, 14 November 08:15:37Z: tool result at +1.7 s, probe settled, lifecycle saw `confirmed: false` and reported "unconfirmed within probe window", then `system init` with the correct session id arrived 213 ms later. The process was healthy and was killed anyway; the held request failed with "Claude CLI cancelled".

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A native resume that has not yet echoed its session id is not proven by output. The probe keeps waiting for the echo (or the timeout) and a wrong or missing session is still rejected. Acceptance: `runtime-readiness.spec.ts` case "does not settle on the first output while a native resume echo is still pending" (failed before the fix, passes after). Live: the held `/goal` allow and the repeat with the fix in place, recorded in the Phase 0 live checks.

<a id="lt-1132"></a>

## LT-1132

### LT-1132 — the stuck-process watchdog kills a session that is waiting for a person's decision

**Status: source fix in the queue branch; rechecked live on 14 November 2026 (see the Phase 0 live checks). Priority P2.** Found while holding the LT-823 permission cards past the iteration timeout.

### Observed behaviour

Two `/goal` sessions held on a Bash permission card (auto-approve off). At about 20 minutes the log carried `Process may be stuck — soft timeout exceeded` for both. At 40 minutes 55 seconds (14 November 08:11:31Z) one of them logged `Process stuck — hard timeout exceeded`, the CLI process was terminated and respawned, the loop's request failed with "Claude CLI cancelled" and the loop paused. The card could no longer be answered.

### Root cause

`StuckProcessDetector` is told about work outside the provider through `hasExternalActivity`, which `instance-manager.ts` wires to `adapterHasPendingLiveAsk`. That helper only recognised the live permission broker. The Bash path uses the hook-deferred route instead (`ClaudeCliAdapter.getDeferredToolUse()`), so a held decision looked like a tool that had gone silent for 40 minutes (alive process, `tool_executing`, hard limit 20 minutes times two).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A running adapter that holds a deferred tool call is waiting for a person, so the watchdog neither warns nor restarts. Acceptance: `stuck-process-detector.live-permission.spec.ts` case "also treats a tool call the hook deferred for a person as a pending ask" (failed before the fix, passes after). Live: a held card past 41 minutes with the fix in place, recorded in the Phase 0 live checks.

<a id="lt-1133"></a>

## LT-1133

### LT-1133 — after "Don't allow" a loop keeps starting iterations that repeat the same question

**Status: source fix in the queue branch; live recheck recorded on 14 November 2026 (rebuilt app on the test Mac: the loop stayed `paused` at one iteration after Don't allow). Priority P2.** Found while closing the full-app check for LT-823 (14 November 2026, test Mac).

### Observed behaviour

A real `/goal` that needed Bash with auto-approve off was held on its permission card for 45 minutes, then **Don't allow** was clicked. The command never ran and the transcript showed the refusal, but the loop then started seven iterations in about a minute (09:10 to 09:11 UTC), each asking the same question, for about $0.04, until **Stop loop** ended it (`cancelled`, "user cancelled").

### Root cause

`DeferredPermissionHandler.resumeAfterDeferredPermission` (resident-request branch) writes the refusal and resumes the held request. Nothing told the loop that a person had answered, so the model's reply ("approve or cancel") counted as a finished iteration and the next one began from the same goal into the same refusal. Only the no-progress check would have parked it, after several paid rounds.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

When a person declines a call a loop is holding, the loop pauses (the in-flight request still finishes) and waits for the person to resume or stop it. An approval, and a refusal nobody was asked about (a saved rule, the reviewer), leave the loop running. Acceptance: `deferred-permission-handler.spec.ts` cases under "a loop is awaiting the held call (LT-1133)" (the decline case failed before the fix, passes after) and `loop-declined-permission-pause.spec.ts`. Live: a held `/goal` card declined on a rebuilt app leaves the loop `paused` with no further iteration. Recorded in the Phase 0 live checks under "Round 3 recheck" (14 November 2026): paused at one iteration, no change over 80 seconds of polling.

## LT-1134

### LT-1134 — a refused Bash permission in an ordinary chat was once worded "Cancelled when the session closed"

**Status: seen once on 14 November 2026 (test Mac); not reproduced in four follow-up runs on the same build; cause unconfirmed; not repaired. Priority P3 (wording only: the command did not run and the model was told it was refused).** Found while closing LT-823 sub-check 4 in the [Phase 0 live checks](2026-10-27-phase0-livetest-remediation_livetest.md#lt-1134-follow-up-14-november-2026).

### Observed behaviour

Ordinary chat, auto-approve off, **Don't allow** clicked on a Bash card at 08:29:43 UTC. `lt823-chat-deny.txt` was never created and the reply said the command was denied. The line left behind for the card read "Cancelled when the session closed" with "Bash" after it. The expected line is "You said no: Bash".

### What is known

- That sentence has one source, `describeRequestOutcome` for the `exited` reason (`src/shared/utils/request-outcome.ts:68`). A refusal is worded by `describeUserChoice` (`denied`, "You said no"). So a card the person had refused was closed through the "session went away" route before, or instead of, the refusal being recorded.
- Three places can close a card with `exited`: the main-process recorder when the session status changes to `respawning`, `terminated` and similar while no reply is in flight (`input-request-receipts.ts` `statusChanged`); the window's status watcher when the card is not marked as being answered (`user-action-request.component.ts:163`, `:386`); and an adapter reporting `exited` (`claude-live-permission.ts` `finishAnswer`, when the reply could not be delivered). A refused deferred permission moves the session through `respawning` while the reply is still being applied, so each guard depends on the reply being marked in flight in time.
- Not tested: which of the three produced the line. The original run was on a busy test Mac with other dev copies running; none of the follow-up runs below was.

### Not reproduced (14 November 2026, 16:07 to 16:12 UTC, test Mac, same branch build, auto-approve off, Claude Haiku)

1. Fresh session, one Bash card, **Don't allow**: "You said no: Bash" on screen; the Tool calls group opened.
2. Same session, **Allow this once** then **Don't allow**: "You allowed once: Bash", then "You said no: Bash".
3. Second fresh session, the same two answers, then a full page reload so the transcript came back from stored history: still "You allowed once: Bash" then "You said no: Bash".
4. Closing the first session afterwards produced no extra line.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A card a person has refused is only ever worded as their refusal. Acceptance for a fix: a spec in which the session status moves to `respawning` before and after a refusal is acknowledged leaves one "You said no" line and no "Cancelled" line, on both the main-process recorder and the window; then a live Don't allow on a rebuilt app under load. Until the cause is found, a fix would be a guess, so this stays open as an observation. Next step if it recurs: capture the app log and the stored history rows for the session at the moment of the click.

## LT-1065 — Desk charity lane fails when its database transactions pass Prisma's 5-second limit

**Status: reproduced on the live Desk on 11 and 12 November 2026, not repaired. Priority P2.** This is a Desk (work-finding repository) defect, filed here because this is the only live-test remediation register. Found by the watchdog-three-faults live check 3 on 13 November 2026 (snapshot 01:20 UTC); the evidence is the sealed read-only query output beside the report named below. Repair belongs in a new Desk plan, not in the watchdog-three-faults plan.

### Observed behaviour

The latest `get-work-day` runs succeeded daily from 28 October to 10 November, then ended `partial` (reason `internal_error`) on 11 and 12 November. Only the `charity_drafts` stage failed. On 12 November Prisma reported "Transaction already closed ... timeout for this transaction was 5000 ms, however 5006 ms passed" at `tx.outreachMessage.create()` (`apps/desk/src/db/repositories/outreachWave.ts:939`). On 11 November the same expiry class occurred at `db.organisationEvidence.create()` (`apps/desk/src/conversations/coordinationIssuance.ts:524`). Both runs left the charity lane with 0 drafts, so the 12 November watchdog raised `get_work_day_lane_no_sendable_output` for `lane:charity` and `outreach_desk_stale`. The first failure came about two hours after the 11 November 05:24 release; that is a timing correlation, not a demonstrated cause.

### Root cause

Not isolated. The charity-lane interactive transactions run with Prisma's default 5-second limit and no `timeout` option exists on the `$transaction` calls in `outreachWave.ts`. Whether the transactions became slower (data growth, lock waits, the 11 November release) or are doing more work inside the transaction than they should was not tested.

### Required behaviour

The charity lane either completes or fails with an actionable cause, and the watchdog does not alarm for a lane that ran correctly. Work that does not need to be atomic stays outside the interactive transaction; any remaining transaction has a deliberate time limit.

### Acceptance

`charity_drafts` succeeds on a weekday `get-work-day` occurrence (the 13 November 07:30 UTC run was the first one due after the observation), or records `no_eligible_work`. The read-back is the deferred "Read back the 13 November 07:30 work-day and 08:30 watchdog occurrences" check in the linked live-test document. A regression test reproduces a transaction that exceeds 5 seconds.

### Evidence

[Watchdog three faults live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/watchdog-three-faults-2026-10-20/watchdog-three-faults_livetest.md), check 3 (13 November 2026 snapshot).

## LT-1066 — Desk conversation reconciliation: mailbox sources unavailable and runs left `running`

**Status: reproduced on the live Desk on 13 November 2026 from read-only database queries, cause not isolated, not repaired. Priority P2.** This is a Desk (work-finding repository) defect, filed here because this is the only live-test remediation register. Found by the watchdog-faults livetest worker (queue item 6cb4db0c) between 01:00 and 02:40 UTC; nothing was written, restarted or run. Repair belongs in a new Desk plan, not in the watchdog-faults plan.

### Observed behaviour

From `automation_runs` where `run_type = 'conversation-reconciliation'` (schedule every five minutes), last 24 hours to 02:29 UTC on 13 November 2026: 258 runs, 199 `succeeded`, 39 `failed`, 20 `partial`, 29 still `running`.

- Every `failed` and `partial` run has reason `source_unavailable`. In failed runs all three mailbox sources report `unavailable` with 0 inserted. In partial runs one mailbox is `complete` and two are `unavailable`.
- `calendar` is `unavailable` in every sampled run and `m365Configured` is `false`: a standing configuration fact, not a per-run fault. Calendly is `complete`.
- 28 of the 29 `running` rows are more than an hour old (oldest 12 November 18:00 UTC) and none has an `ended_at`.

### Root cause

Not isolated. Not tested: whether the mailbox outages come from credentials, provider throttling, network faults or a source circuit breaker; and whether the long-`running` rows are abandoned rows that never finalise or rows closed by another path. Whether the stale `running` rows cause any wrong user-visible state is also unknown. This does not explain or fix the three live watchdog warnings and must not be read as doing so.

### Required behaviour

A mailbox outage ends the run with an actionable cause that names which source and why. A run that cannot finish is closed or flagged by a rule rather than left `running` with no end time. The permanent unconfigured calendar source is reported as a configuration fact, not counted as an outage.

### Acceptance

A diagnosed cause for the mailbox `unavailable` states, with either a fix or documented expected behaviour; a regression test for the rule that closes or flags `running` rows with no end time; and a 24-hour readback in which no run is `running` past its expected duration and every `failed` run names its cause.

### Evidence

[Watchdog faults live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/watchdog-faults-2026-10-08/watchdog-faults_livetest.md), "Defect record: conversation-reconciliation source outages and stuck runs" (13 November 2026).

## LT-1100

### LT-1100 — a read by exact title with the switch off says "not found" instead of naming the switch

**Status: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 14 November 2026 (Claude half).** Reproduced 10 November 2026 on a base that did not yet contain the repair (then recorded as LT-1018; renumbered because main already used that number for a different defect).

### Observed behaviour

Rebuilt dev app, base `e429665064` (it predates the repair). With Cross-session messaging on, a Claude and a Codex session in the same folder both
found `read_session` through tool search and answered from a third session by its exact title (audit rows: one per
call, reason `same-folder`). After switching the setting off, both repeated the call by title and received exactly
`{"outcome":"not-found"}`; the audit rows are `not-found`, target empty. The check expects a refusal that names the switch.

### Root cause

`SessionTranscriptReader.readPage` (`src/main/session/session-transcript-reader.ts`) matches titles only among sessions
already readable (`this.scope(...)` is applied before the title comparison), so a title only the switch would open
matches nothing. The plan history records a fix ("Step 1 verifier round 1 repair", 10 November, commit `bd0db3b24`) that answers
`not-allowed` with the switch reason for that case. It was not in the base the live run used; it is in the current branch head, where
`session-transcript-reader.spec.ts` covers the exact-title case.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

An exact title that only the switch would open answers `not-allowed` with the switch reason (no ids, folders or counts;
foreign-folder and scratch titles stay `not-found`). Acceptance: rebuild from the current head and repeat the live check (switch on then off); the off
reply names the switch and the audit row says `not-allowed`.

### Recheck 14 November 2026

Dev app on the test Mac built from head `39e443963`. A Claude reader started with the switch on found `read_session` through the orchestrator tool search and read a sibling session by exact title (audit row `read`, reason `same-folder`). After the switch went off, the same reader's next call by title was refused with "Ask the user to point at this session with @session. Related or same-project sessions also require Cross-session messaging in Settings." (audit row `not-allowed`; one row per call throughout). A reader started while the switch was off was not given the tool at all. The Codex reader half did not run: Codex is not installed on the test Mac.

## LT-1101

### LT-1101 — "Working quietly" never appears on a real silent Claude turn

**Status: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 14 November 2026.** Reproduced 10 November 2026 (then recorded as LT-1019; renumbered because main already used that number for a different defect). The fix is in the branch head from the 13 November change.

### Observed behaviour

A Claude session (Opus, effort max) given a hard question with no tools stayed busy for more than 150 s. The activity
line read "Working" until about 8 s, then "Agent active" until the turn ended or was stopped (172 s since the last event
when sampled); "Working quietly" and its hover were never shown.

### Root cause

`InstanceQueries.activityStateToLabel` returns "Agent active" whenever the process state is `active`, and
`selectedInstanceActivity` / `instanceActivities` use it as the `activity` text. `ActivityStatusComponent.displayText`
returns any non-empty `activity` before its ten-second "Working quietly" fallback, so the fallback only applies when
the process state is not `active`, which is never true during a real turn.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After about ten seconds without a new event the line says "Working quietly" even when the process state is `active`
(the bland state label must not mask it). Acceptance: the live check shows the switch at about ten seconds on a silent
Claude turn, with the hover text.

### Recheck 14 November 2026

Dev app on the test Mac built from head `39e443963`. A silent Opus (effort max) turn with no tools read "Working" for the first ten seconds or so, then "Working quietly" with the running time beside it, and stayed there for more than seven minutes (never "Agent active"). Hovering the words showed "This provider shares its thinking only when a step finishes. Harness shows how long it has been working." After the turn was interrupted the row disappeared. One sample at 1 m 22 s read "Working" again for under ten seconds (an event arrived), then returned to "Working quietly".

## LT-1102

### LT-1102 — the Progress panel does not fill when Claude plans with its newer task tools

**Status: FIXED AND VERIFIED LIVE 14 November 2026.** Reproduced 10 November 2026 (then recorded as LT-1020; renumbered because main already used that number for a different defect) and again on 14 November at head `39e443963`.

### Observed behaviour

With the Claude task list setting on, a Claude chat asked to "plan three small steps, then do them" called `ToolSearch`,
three `TaskCreate` and six `TaskUpdate` tools and finished the work. The Progress panel stayed empty and no `TodoWrite`
call appears in the transcript.

### Root cause

`src/main/instance/todo-tool-parser.ts` recognises only `TodoWrite` (and `todo_write`, `todo.write`) and Codex's
`update_plan`. The installed Claude CLI uses `TaskCreate` and `TaskUpdate` for its task list, which nothing parses.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

`TaskCreate` and `TaskUpdate` calls fill the Progress panel (or the setting is documented as `TodoWrite`-only and the
check reworded). Acceptance: repeat the live check; the panel shows the three steps changing state.

### Fix and recheck 14 November 2026

Source: `extractTodoToolItems(message, readCurrent)` in `src/main/instance/todo-tool-parser.ts` builds the list from `TaskCreate` (adds a task from `subject`/`activeForm`) and `TaskUpdate` (changes the task whose number is `taskId`; `deleted` shows as cancelled); the caller in `instance-communication.ts` passes the session's current list. The CLI numbers tasks 1, 2, 3 in creation order (seen in the live transcript), so a task's number is its place in the list; this assumption is stated in the code comment. Specs: `todo-tool-parser.spec.ts` (3 new cases; 7 pass), with the 30 related spec files in `src/main/instance` and `src/main/tasks` passing (360 tests).

Live: reproduced first at head (a Sonnet chat with the setting on called `ToolSearch`, three `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate` calls; nothing in the panel). After rebuilding the dev app from the changed tree, the same prompt produced exactly three tasks, all completed, and the panel header read "Tasks 3 of 3 done". Not covered: tasks deleted mid-run, and a Claude session restarted without resume (the CLI restarts its numbering while Harness keeps the old list).

## LT-1103

### LT-1103 — a test-Mac dev app copy has no orchestrator tools

**Status: REPRODUCED LIVE 14 November 2026; both gaps repaired in source 14 November and verified live 16 November 2026 (one `dev-app.js start` on the test Mac gave a Claude session `read_session`, one audit row `read` / `same-folder`; evidence in the Phase 5 live-test document, final 16 November section); not yet in a shipped build.** Owner: `scripts/remote-checks/dev-app.js` / `remote-run.sh` (plan `2026-11-13-livetests-on-test-mac`).

### Observed behaviour

A Claude session started in a dev app copy on the test Mac (`dev-app.js start`) had only its own tools. Asked for `read_session` it searched three times and answered that the tool did not exist. The main log said `Orchestrator-tools MCP not configured — aio-mcp SEA binary, RPC socket or instance capability missing` for every spawn, and `aio-mcp SEA binary not found — Chrome native-messaging host wrapper not installed` at start-up.

### Root cause

Two gaps. (1) `start` runs `npm run build:main` and the screens build but never `npm run build:aio-mcp-dist`, and `build:main` clears `dist/`, so `dist/aio-mcp-cli-sea/aio-mcp` is absent after every start. (2) `resolveAioMcpCliPath` (`src/main/util/aio-mcp-cli-path.ts`) looks for `dist/aio-mcp-cli-sea/aio-mcp` under `process.cwd()`; the copy is opened through the launcher (`open -n -g -a Electron.app`), whose working folder is `/` (`lsof` showed `cwd /` for the Electron process), so a binary built inside the checkout is still not found.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A copy started by `dev-app.js` gets the orchestrator tools. Either build the helper in `start` and tell the app where it is (a path setting or environment value read by `resolveAioMcpCliPath`), or copy it where the app already looks. Acceptance: after one `start`, a Claude session finds and calls `read_session` without manual steps.

### Repair so far (14 November 2026, second round)

Gap 2 is fixed in source: `resolveAioMcpCliPath` (`src/main/util/aio-mcp-cli-path.ts`) now also looks for `dist/aio-mcp-cli-sea/aio-mcp` beside its own compiled file (`dist/main/util/../../aio-mcp-cli-sea`), so a copy opened through the launcher (working folder `/`) finds a binary built inside its checkout. New case in `src/main/util/__tests__/aio-mcp-cli-path.spec.ts` (6 pass). Not yet seen live: the fix needs a rebuilt copy that also has the binary built.

Gap 1 is repaired in the launcher: the `devapp-job` branch of `scripts/remote-checks/remote-run.sh` now runs `npm run build:aio-mcp-dist` straight after `npm run build:main` (which clears `dist/`) and before the screens build, logging to `aio-mcp.log` and failing the start with `npm run build:aio-mcp-dist failed` if it breaks. It runs under the Node version from `.nvmrc` (24), which `ensure_node` puts first on the path, so the Homebrew Node 26 SEA-fuse problem does not apply. The launcher (`remote-run.sh` devapp commands and `dev-app.js`) is not on this queue branch: it is uncommitted work in the root checkout from plan `2026-11-13-livetests-on-test-mac` (now `_completed`), so the edit was made there in place and lands when that work is committed, not with this branch. `bash -n` passes and `dev-app.spec.ts` plus `remote-run.linux.spec.ts` pass (49 tests); those specs fake the far Mac, so they do not run the build step itself. Still open: one live `dev-app.js start` on the test Mac followed by a Claude session finding and calling `read_session` (acceptance).

### Workaround used on 14 November

Built the helper in the copy with `dev-app shell 'npm run build:aio-mcp-dist'`, copied the binary into the shared Electron install's `Contents/Resources/aio-mcp-cli/` (a place the resolver also checks), and relaunched the app by hand with the launcher command from `remote-run.sh`. The copied file was removed afterwards.


## LT-1142

### LT-1142 — worker config with tokens is saved world-readable

**Status: open; reproduced 12 November 2026.**

### Observed behaviour

After `aio-worker pair "<link>"` and a first connection, the worker home's `.orchestrator/worker-node.json` held `authToken`, `nodeToken` and `recoveryToken` and had mode 644; its folder had mode 755 (default umask 022). Any other account on that computer can read the file and take over the worker's identity.

### Root cause

The config is written with `fs.writeFileSync(configPath, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + '\n', 'utf-8')` (`src/worker-agent/worker-config.ts:630`), with no `mode` and no later `chmod`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The worker config is created and rewritten with mode 600 (and an existing looser file is tightened on the next write). Acceptance: a spec that writes a config under a 022 umask and asserts mode 600, failing before the change; after a real `aio-worker pair`, `stat` shows 600. Windows ignores POSIX modes, so the check applies on macOS and Linux only.


## LT-1143

### LT-1143 — worker port accepts then drops non-loopback connections; the pairing probe cannot see it

**Status: open; reproduced 12 November 2026; cause not isolated.**

### Observed behaviour

Dev app (Electron from the queue worktree, `AIO_DEV_USER_DATA_PATH` profile) with the worker server on port 4979 listening on all interfaces. From the same Mac: `curl http://127.0.0.1:4979/` returned 426 (normal); `curl http://<LAN address>:4979/` returned an empty reply (curl exit 52); a Node `ws` client got "socket hang up" on the LAN address and on the Tailscale IPv4 address, and `aio-worker` logged "socket hang up" for the Tailscale name, both Tailscale IPs and both LAN addresses. A plain `node` HTTP server bound to 0.0.0.0 on the same LAN address answered 200 in the same minute. The macOS application firewall was on and reported incoming connections to that Electron.app as permitted. `aio-worker pair` printed `Paired ... with <tailscale name>:4979` with no "did not answer" line, because its probe passed.

### Root cause

Not isolated. Discriminating evidence: the drop is specific to the Electron process, not the network path (plain Node on the same address works) and not to the pairing code (loopback works). It matches the earlier note that the packaged Harness port answers on neither Tailscale address. Separately and certain: `probeCoordinatorReachability` (`src/worker-agent/cli/pair-cli.ts:148`) only opens a TCP socket and closes it, so an address that accepts then drops is treated as reachable.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

(1) Find why the Electron process drops non-loopback connections on this Mac (firewall or Local Network privacy for the Electron binary, or the dual-stack listener) and fix or document it. (2) The worker's probe should complete a WebSocket handshake, so that an address that accepts and then drops is skipped in favour of the next fallback. Acceptance: with the server up, `curl http://<LAN address>:<port>/` returns 426 from another computer; a pair-cli spec where the first candidate accepts TCP and then closes shows the second candidate chosen (fails before the change); the livetest "Pairing across two computers" check passes without editing the config.

### Update, 14 November 2026

A dev app started on the test Mac (`dev-app.js`, port 4979 on all interfaces) was reached from this Mac on its LAN address, its Tailscale IPv4 address and its MagicDNS name: `curl` returned 426 on both addresses, and `aio-worker pair` from this Mac wrote a config and connected without any edit (roster `connected`). So the drop is specific to the Electron process on this Mac, not to the pairing code or the network. Part (2) of the required behaviour (a probe that completes a WebSocket handshake) is unchanged and still open. The "Pairing across two computers" live check no longer depends on this defect (see the evidence run of 14 November 2026).


## LT-1144

### LT-1144 — dev copy's renderer-event validation rejects `waitingSessionCount` and `origin`

**Status: open; reproduced 14 November 2026; cause unconfirmed.**

### Observed behaviour

During the agent-issued pairing evidence run (a dev app started by `dev-app.js` on the test Mac, data folder under `/tmp`), the renderer-event validation log carried two warnings: `cli-update-pill:delta` had an unrecognised key `waitingSessionCount`, and `cost:usage-recorded` had an unrecognised key `origin`. Neither is related to pairing. The events are sent by `cli-update-poll-service.ts` (`waitingSessionCount`, line 149) and by `cost-handlers.ts` (a `CostEntry` carrying `origin`).

### Root cause

Not isolated. In this worktree's source both keys are already in the strict schemas: `waitingSessionCount` in `CliUpdatePillStateEventSchema` (`packages/contracts/src/schemas/observability.schemas.ts:139`) and `origin` in `CostEntryEventSchema` (`packages/contracts/src/schemas/cost-events.schemas.ts:29`). `src/main/event-bus/renderer-event-validation.spec.ts` (30 tests, run 14 November 2026, all passing) asserts both are accepted. Both keys were added to the schemas on 13 November 2026 (commits `b214cd55a`, `186958a63`). The most likely explanation is that the dev copy ran compiled contracts from before those commits, but the copy's compiled output was deleted after the run, so this is not proven.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Both events pass validation with no warning in a dev app freshly built from a tree that contains the two schema commits. Acceptance: start such a build, let the CLI update poll run once and record one model turn, then read the log: no `unrecognised key` warning for either channel. If a warning still appears on a fresh build, there is a second validator or a stale generated copy to find; if not, close this item as a stale build.

## LT-1159

### LT-1159 — auto re-login reads the login form before it has rendered

**Status: source fix and regression test 13 November 2026; Windows re-check on the rebuilt app pending. Priority P2.** Found by the 13 November 2026 Windows run of the multi-portal remediation live checks ([evidence](2026-10-27-browser-login-multi-portal-remediation_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-13-plan-queue-livetest-worker)).

### Observed behaviour

On `windows-pc`, with a signed-in-then-logged-out Connected Places Catapult tab (`https://supplier.in-tend.co.uk/cpcatapult/home`, recipe `5c7cd728-…`, `portalPath: /cpcatapult`), `check_session` returned `state: unknown, reason: markers_not_matched_on_signed_in_page, attempts: 1, reloggedIn: false`. Three tries in a row gave the same answer, including once starting from a different Catapult page. The tab stayed on the logged-out login form, and the audit trail shows `navigate` to the login URL, a snapshot, then `query_elements` returning **0 selector candidates** about 30 ms later, then nothing: no `fill_credential` and no submit. The same page read through `query_elements` by hand a moment later lists the password inputs. The Publica buyer's identical form (same selectors) filled and signed in on its first attempt in the same run.

Reproduced again on 16 November 2026 on the restarted installed app (which does not contain the fix), and not only on Catapult: a fresh Catapult tab and a fresh Publica tab (`/publicagroup/home`, recipe `16a7b479-…`) each returned the same `unknown / markers_not_matched_on_signed_in_page, attempts: 1`. The Publica audit shows a form read of 61 elements before the navigate and 0 after it, then no fill. Publica passed the same way on 13 November, so the race is intermittent and not specific to one portal.

### Root cause

`attemptRelogin` (`src/main/browser-gateway/browser-session-relogin.ts`) calls `deps.navigate(loginUrl)`, which resolves before the portal has drawn its form, then reads the elements straight away. An empty read means "no password field", which the code treats as a signed-in page whose markers do not match, so it stops with that misleading reason and never fills. It is a timing race, not a recipe-selection fault: the right recipe and account were already chosen.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After navigating to the login URL, wait for the recipe's password input (bounded by the existing settle window) before reading the form. If it never appears, behave as before (report unknown, no fill). Acceptance: `browser-session-relogin.spec.ts` case "waits for the login form to render after navigation before filling it" (failed before the fix, passes after) and "still reports unknown without filling when no login form ever appears after navigation". On the rebuilt app, log the Catapult test tab out and run `check_session`: expect `logged_in`, `reloggedIn: true`, `attempts: 1`, and real signed-in page text.
