## LT-1130

### LT-1130 — credential fill audit rows for allowed and dispatch-failed fills had no origin

**Status: fixed in source 14 November 2026, unit-tested; live recheck needs the rebuilt app. Priority P3.** Reproduced live the same day on `windows-pc` during the LT-703 recheck.

### Observed behaviour

`browser.fill_credential` on the LCN login form returned `allowed`/`succeeded` (audit `af686df7-...`) and a wrong-selector request returned `denied`/`failed` with `dispatch:credential_selector_not_found` (audit `1f93f38c-...`). The audit `origin` column was empty on both rows. Only the pre-dispatch denial (audit `a684f1a0-...`) carried `https://login.lcn.com`.

### Root cause

`fillCredentialOperation` resolves the receiving origin (`browser-form-fill-operations.ts`, the `origin = fillOrigin` assignment) and passes it to the denial helper, but the catch-path result and the success result did not pass `origin` to `BrowserGatewayResultRecorder`, which writes only an origin it is given.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Every audit row for a credential fill that got past origin resolution names the origin that receives the secret. Acceptance: `browser-form-fill-operations.spec.ts` asserts `origin` on the success result (frame origin `https://login.lcn.com`) and on the dispatch-failure result (page origin when no frame origin is reported). Both pass, as does the whole `src/main/browser-gateway` suite. The live recheck is to repeat a fill on a rebuilt app and read the audit row.

## LT-1127

### LT-1127 — a spent Claude week on credits does not move a ranked worker list down

**Status: reproduced live 12 November 2026; source fix and unit test 14 November 2026; live recheck with a spent Claude week pending.** Filed on 12 November as LT-1018; that number, and then LT-1099, were taken by other defects on the base branch, so this one is LT-1127.

### Observed behaviour

Dev app on an empty profile (only the pre-pools "Existing Claude account"), build `dba478375`. Saved worker list
Claude then Codex. The Usage pill and `quotaGetAll` showed Claude's `claude.weekly` at 100/100 with
`usageAccess.ordinaryUsageAllowed: false` and extra-usage credits available; Codex was at 31%. A chat session started
a queue run: the triage session and the worker session were both created on Claude (dev log 01:55:38Z and 01:55:49Z,
run `297f4f2c`), the Claude CLI logged "Provider rate limit active" with an overage status and the turn still
completed, and the run card later showed "$0.84 across 1 document". No "worker choice picked by usage left" line was
written because the first choice counted as usable. A third run (`9cdbe431`) behaved the same after a recorded limit
was cleared, which is correct there.

### Root cause

`planQueueRouteUsage` (`src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-route-usage.ts`) previews the pool route for Claude. With only
the pre-pools sign-in the route's source is `legacy`, and the function returns `limitFor(null)`: the provider-limit
ledger alone. A spent plan is read from usage figures only for non-pooled providers (`planSpent`, Cursor and Grok
windows). Claude with credits on never produces a ledger record, so the ledger is empty and the choice is usable. The
pool path would veto an account whose evidence is `creditsOnly` (`account-quota-evidence.ts`), and the file's own
rule is that unattended queue work never counts purchased credits; the pre-pools path does not apply it.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

For a pooled provider on its pre-pools sign-in, a snapshot saying ordinary usage is not allowed (plan spent, credits
only) counts as no usage for queue work, as it does for an account in a pool. Acceptance: a unit case in
`plan-queue-route-usage.spec.ts` with a legacy route, an empty ledger and a Claude snapshot with
`ordinaryUsageAllowed: false` returns `usable: false`; on a rebuilt app with Claude's week spent and no recorded limit,
a Claude-then-Codex list starts triage and worker on Codex and logs "worker choice picked by usage left". Note the
live check recorded a limit by writing a row to the profile's own limit table, which is what a CLI that stops would do.

### Fix (14 November 2026)

`planQueueRouteUsage` (`plan-queue-route-usage.ts`) now applies the pool's usage veto to the pre-pools sign-in too: a pooled provider on its `legacy` route whose usage figures show the plan spent, or running only on purchased credits, has no usage for queue work (`signInSpent`, using the shared `usageVetoFor` in `provider-account-selector.ts`, with windows already past their reset cleared first). Unit case: "has no usage for the pre-pools sign-in whose plan is spent and runs only on credits" in `plan-queue-route-usage.spec.ts`. Live recheck still needs Claude's real week spent with no recorded limit, plus Codex installed; Claude's week was 3% on 14 November.

## LT-1067 — Desk email starters drop keyboard focus when they disable themselves

**Status: reproduced on 13 November 2026 in a real Chrome on the test Mac, not repaired. Priority P3.** This is a Desk (work-finding repository) defect, filed here because this is the only live-test remediation register. Found by the crm-outcomes-release live-test worker (queue item c72fc4b4) on a disposable fixture page with fictional data only. Repair belongs in a new Desk plan, not in the closed outcomes-release plan.

### Observed behaviour

Open the Write an email panel with the keyboard, Tab to a starter button (for example "Thank-you after a meeting") and press Enter. The subject and message fill in correctly, but `document.activeElement` is then `BODY`. A following Tab moves to the first control on the page (`lt-open-confirm` on the fixture) instead of the subject field next to the starters. The same happens with the pointer; it matters for keyboard and screen-reader users, who lose their place.

### Root cause

`useSnippet` in `apps/desk/web/src/app/colleague-outreach/write-email-panel.component.ts` (around line 220) sets the subject and message, and the template binds every starter button to `[disabled]="!canStartSnippet()"` (`write-email-panel.component.html`, around line 134). Once text exists `canStartSnippet()` is false, so Chrome disables the button that had focus and moves focus to the body. Nothing moves focus to the message field. Source-read only; the fix was not tried.

### Required behaviour

After a starter is used, keyboard focus lands on a sensible field (the message field, or the first bracketed placeholder) so the next Tab or typed key continues the writing. The other starter rules stay: existing words are never overwritten and the starters stay disabled while text exists or a save is in flight.

### Acceptance

A component test that activates a starter and asserts the focused element is the message field (and not `BODY`), plus a keyboard re-check in a real browser: Tab to a starter, Enter, type immediately, and the typed text lands in the message field.

### Evidence

[CRM outcomes release live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/crm-outcomes-release-2026-10-30/crm-outcomes-release_livetest.md), "Evidence run, 13 November 2026". Read-back after the starter press: `{"active":"BODY","subject":"Thank you for the meeting","starterDisabled":true}`.

Recheck 13 November 2026 at measured `innerWidth` 390 (same fixture, real Gateway keys on the test Mac): focus again dropped to `BODY` with the starter disabled, so the defect reproduces at both widths. One correction to the observation above: at 390 the next real Tab landed on the subject field (`write-email-subject`), not the top of the page, because Chrome continues from where the removed button sat. So keyboard users keep roughly their place on that path; focus still falls to `BODY`, which screen-reader users still notice, and typing immediately (without a Tab) still goes nowhere. Priority stays P3.

**Status: reproduced on 13 November 2026, not repaired. Priority P3.**

### Observed behaviour

## LT-1070 — Desk deploy jobs fail on real CI runs (16 of the last 48)

**Status: reproduced on real runs, 20 October to 13 November 2026; 14 of 16 causes isolated; not repaired. Priority P2.**
Found while running the [Desk fast deploy verification repair live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/desk-fast-deploy-verification-repair-2026-10-16/desk-fast-deploy-verification-repair_livetest.md) (check 5) as a Plan Queue worker. Repository `Community-Tech-UK/work-finding`, workflow `ci.yml`, job `deploy / deploy`. Failure text taken from `gh run view <id> --log-failed` on 13 November 2026.

### Observed behaviour

Of the last 48 `deploy / deploy` jobs, 16 failed:

| Run | Pushed commit | Failed step | Text in the log |

| 42216144694 (6 Nov) | `9faa7f221` | Release worker source | "Worker release refused: every crontab job must run through …/cron-guard.sh; nothing was paused or changed" |
| 42265266939 (6 Nov) | `0f0a4ccc8` | Deploy and verify | "Public availability probe did not establish a healthy baseline" |
| 42372282108 (7 Nov) | `bf638cc2b` | Release worker source | "Worker release refused: schema or package source changed: package.json" |
| 42427861374 (8 Nov) | `f7cd38e14` | Release worker source | "Worker release refused: schema or package source changed: package.json, prisma/migrations/20261107100000_…, prisma/schema.prisma" |
| 42467364114 (8 Nov) | `36a52a6b3` | Release worker source | same refusal as 42427861374 |
| 42476729267 (8 Nov) | `646f32fa7` | Deploy and verify | "Public availability probe observed a failed read; ending cutover" then "ACTION NEEDED: online cutover failed across a mailbox reader safety or database schema boundary; candidate remains selected. Fix forward" |
| 42702477473 (9 Nov) | `4d78e4943` | Deploy and verify | "Public availability probe observed a failed read; ending cutover" |
| 42728373259 (10 Nov) | `240990359` | Deploy and verify | "Public availability probe observed a failed read; ending cutover; previous healthy API selected again" |

| 42950490478 (11 Nov) | `41d4f6b39` | Deploy and verify | Same shape as 42940786572 (57 s paused, then exit 1 with no reason line) |

### Root cause

Not confirmed beyond reading the logs; recorded per group:

1. Five "Release worker source" failures (39860849093, 41312235845, 42372282108, 42427861374, 42467364114) are the designed refusal when a push changes the schema or `package.json`. The release is then done by hand as a schema release, but CI still ends red for that push. Whether a designed refusal should show as a failed deploy is a product choice, not decided.
2. One "Release worker source" failure (42216144694) is the cron-guard refusal (a crontab job not running through the guard); one (40016265502) is the financial-refresh refusal. Both are documented refusals; nothing was changed on the box.
3. Five "Deploy and verify" failures (39950384443, 42265266939, 42476729267, 42702477473, 42728373259) are the public availability probe (or its baseline) seeing a failed read. Several fall in the 8 to 10 November window of box moves and memory trouble already in the memory notes; the box now answers 200 from the Mac and Krystal. Not separated from a real defect.
4. Two failures (42967603175, 43125181349) end in "The operation was aborted due to timeout" during candidate verification. The 13 November commit `a8bafeeee` gave that check a bigger time budget, and the two later deploys passed. Plausible but not proven as the cause.
5. Two failures (42940786572, 42950490478) show no reason line at all after the box's `prisma generate`; the online-step output for them is not kept on the box (only worker-release logs and probe files are). Cause not isolated. This is the thing to find first.

### Required behaviour

1. Every failed deploy job prints one plain reason line, and the box keeps the online-step log for each release, so a failure like 42940786572 can be read afterwards.
2. A push that only needs a manual schema release does not leave main red in a way that hides a real deploy failure (decide: separate "needs manual release" outcome, or leave as is and document it).
3. No unexplained "Deploy and verify" failure across the next 20 deploys that did not need a schema release.

### Acceptance

1. Re-run the count over the then-latest 48 deploy jobs: every failure has a reason line and a matching box log, and none is unexplained.
2. The next three consecutive typical deploys all succeed.

### Evidence

Desk fast deploy verification repair live checks, "Evidence run, 13 November 2026 (second round, after verifier round 1)". Raw logs were read from `gh run view --log-failed` into a scratch folder that was deleted afterwards; the table above is the record. Box read-only look on `dev-vps2`: worker-release logs and probe files exist for these commits, online-step logs do not.

## LT-1071 — The Desk deploy job is over its five-minute target on the latest full deploy

**Status: reproduced on real runs 12 and 13 November 2026; not repaired. Priority P2.**
Found while running the [Desk fast deploy verification repair live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/desk-fast-deploy-verification-repair-2026-10-16/desk-fast-deploy-verification-repair_livetest.md) (check 5).

### Observed behaviour

The spec ([desk-fast-deploys_spec_completed.md](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/desk-fast-deploys-2026-09-17/desk-fast-deploys_spec_completed.md), section 3 table and the line "Targets are met when three consecutive typical production deploys land inside them") sets the deploy job at under 5 minutes. The three most recent successful full deploys, by GitHub job start to finish: run 43353022084 (`0e72f4604`, 13 Nov) 347 s; run 43344288239 (`a8bafeeee`, 13 Nov) 285 s; run 42551962659 (`164958aee`, 9 Nov) 183 s. The newest is over target, so three consecutive in-target deploys do not exist. Across all 22 full deploys since 20 October, 20 were under 300 s (median 199 s); the other over-target run was 330 s (run 39986421575, 23 Oct).

### Root cause

Not confirmed. The online step's own metrics for 43353022084 show `drainSeconds` 127 and `candidateStartToCutoverSeconds` 57 plus a 25-sample public probe, and the "Deploy and verify" step grew from about 150 s (late October) to 240 to 262 s on 11 to 13 November, which lines up with `a8bafeeee` giving the candidate deploy check a bigger time budget (check passed in 23989 ms in the latest run). Fixed drain and probe time now leaves little room.

### Required behaviour

Three consecutive typical production deploys finish the deploy job inside 5 minutes, or the spec's target is deliberately changed by a recorded decision.

### Acceptance

Read the job durations of the next three successful full deploys with `gh api`: all three under 300 s, or a dated decision in the spec that replaces the target.

## LT-1073 — Desk email panel keeps a refused (403) or missing (404) read after it is closed and reopened

**Status: reproduced on 13 November 2026 in a real Chrome on the test Mac, not repaired. Priority P4.** This is a Desk (work-finding repository) behaviour, filed here because this is the only live-test remediation register. Found by the crm-outcomes-release live-test worker (queue item c72fc4b4) on a disposable fixture page with fictional data only. Repair, or a recorded decision that this is intended, belongs in a new Desk plan, not in the closed outcomes-release plan.

### Observed behaviour

The fixture's context read answered 403 `colleague_sending_needs_microsoft_sign_in`. The panel showed the plain Microsoft sign-in message and no form. After closing the panel and opening it again, the same message showed and the fixture's request log recorded no new context read.

### Root cause

`toggle()` in `apps/desk/web/src/app/colleague-outreach/write-email-panel.component.ts` (around line 191) calls `load()` on opening only when `phase()` is `"closed"` or `"error"`. The `"forbidden"` and `"missing"` phases are therefore sticky until the organisation id changes (`reset()`) or the page reloads. The class comment says the context "is read when the panel is opened, not with the page", which reads as every open; the code does it once per organisation. Keeping a `"ready"` form and its typed words across close and reopen looks deliberate (a half-written email survives closing the panel). No test or spec records a decision about 403 or 404 reopening (`write-email-panel.component.spec.ts` has one 403 test, which never reopens).

### Required behaviour

Either reopening the panel after a 403 or 404 reads the context again (keeping a ready form's typed words as today), or a dated decision in the component comment and a test states that a refused read is kept until the page is reloaded.

### Acceptance

A component test that returns 403, closes and reopens the panel, and asserts either a second context request (and the form once access is granted) or, if the decision is to keep it, that no second request is made and the comment says why. A browser re-check of the same close and reopen.

### Evidence

[CRM outcomes release live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/crm-outcomes-release-2026-10-30/crm-outcomes-release_livetest.md), "Evidence run, 13 November 2026" (observation) and "Fixes after verifier round 2" (filing). Proof of the reopen behaviour: a component probe on the real `WriteEmailPanelComponent` (`evidence/lt-20261113/lt1073-reopen-probe.log`): after a 403 or 404, close and reopen made 0 new context reads; a 500 control made 1. The browser receipts `1512-context403.json` and `390-context403.json` show only the first read.

## LT-1075 — Desk Pipeline stage handler submits again while the stage is running

**Status: reproduced and fixed on 13 November 2026; fix is in the work-finding queue worktree `queue/running-job-help-code-928099`, not yet committed. Priority P3.** Desk (work-finding) defect, filed here because this is the only live-test remediation register. Found by the running-job-help-code live-test worker (queue item 7863590d); the verifier required it to be filed or fixed.

### Observed behaviour

With Score running (button disabled, running hint shown), a click delivered by the Browser Gateway (`isTrusted: false`) reached the Angular handler of the disabled button. Two such clicks produced two more `POST /api/jobs` (accepted jobs 2 and 3). A real pointer or keyboard cannot click a disabled button, so ordinary users were not affected; the handler simply had no guard of its own.

### Root cause

`JobRunnerComponent.run()` in `apps/desk/web/src/app/research/job-runner.component.ts` called `ResearchJobs.enqueue` unconditionally. Only the template's `[disabled]` binding stopped a second submission.

### Fix

`run()` now returns when `jobs.disabled(stage.name)` is true (not enabled by the server, or already running). A focused component test (`does not submit a second job when the handler runs for a stage that is already running`) failed before the fix (four `POST /api/jobs` instead of one) and passes after it.

### Acceptance

Met on 13 November 2026: the focused test above passes (30 of 30 in the four related spec files), and a live repeat on a rebuilt app (ct-test-mac, same fixture) with the Gateway click plus a further script-delivered click on the disabled running Score button left accepted jobs and write attempts at 1.

### Evidence

[running-job-help-code live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/running-job-help-code-2026-10-09/running-job-help-code_livetest.md), section "Remediation of the disabled-button finding, 13 November 2026".

## LT-1076 — Desk Pipeline stage button drops keyboard focus when its own job starts

**Status: reproduced on 13 November 2026 in a real Chrome on the test Mac, not repaired. Priority P3.** Desk (work-finding) defect, same cause as LT-1067. Found by the running-job-help-code live-test worker (queue item 7863590d).

### Observed behaviour

Tab to a stage button (for example Score) and press Enter. The job starts, the button becomes disabled and `document.activeElement` becomes `BODY`. The next Tab continues from the old position, so nothing is trapped, but the user loses their place and a screen reader gets no focus move.

The stage buttons in `job-runner.component.html` use `[disabled]="jobs.disabled(stage.name)"`; Chrome moves focus off a button that becomes disabled. Not caused by the running hint added in the recovered change.

Focus stays somewhere sensible after a stage starts (for example the button uses `aria-disabled` and stays focusable, or focus moves to the progress line).

### Acceptance

A component test that starts a stage from a focused button and asserts focus is not `BODY`, plus a real-keyboard re-check in a browser.

[running-job-help-code live checks](../../../../communitytech/work-finding/documents/plans/running-job-help-code-2026-10-09/running-job-help-code_livetest.md), "Row 2" and the observation after the table, "Evidence run, 13 November 2026".

### Observed behaviour

`automation_runs` for `get-work-day` at 07:30 UTC: `succeeded` daily 9 and 10 November, then `partial` on 11, 12 and 13 November. On 11 and 12 November the failing stage was `charity_drafts` (LT-1065). On 13 November the `followups` stage was `failed` with reason `internal_error` (it had `succeeded` on 9 to 12 November) and `reply_ingest` was `partial` with reason `source_unavailable`; the run's recorded error text is `source_unavailable`. The receipts name the stage but carry no underlying error text, and a timestamp search of the worker out and error logs on the dev server for the 07:30 to 07:31 UTC window found nothing (a weak negative: the log line format may not match the search). On the same run `charity_drafts` `succeeded` (`completed`), which is the first clean charity lane since 10 November and is relevant to the LT-1065 read-back. The same day `conversation-reconciliation` ended 120 runs `failed` and 18 `partial` (all `source_unavailable`) by 14:53 UTC, with the first failure at 12 November 17:45 UTC (LT-1066 recorded the 24 hours to 02:29 UTC; this run extends it to 14:53 UTC on 13 November). Not isolated. Not tested: whether `followups` failed because the mailbox read behind `reply_ingest` was unavailable, because of a database transaction limit like LT-1065, or for an unrelated reason; and whether the 13 November 14:51 UTC release (`27b02fa8`) changed the behaviour.

### Required behaviour

A `get-work-day` stage that fails records its underlying cause (stage, source and error) in the run receipt, so `internal_error` is never the only text. A mailbox outage ends `reply_ingest` and `followups` with an actionable cause rather than a generic one.

### Acceptance

A diagnosed cause for the 13 November `followups` and `reply_ingest` results, with a fix or documented expected behaviour; a regression test that a failed stage records its error text in the run receipt; and a weekday `get-work-day` occurrence on which every stage is `succeeded` or `no_eligible_work` (the next due is Monday 16 November 07:30 UTC), read back from `automation_runs`.

## LT-1091 — The "of which helper agents" figure undercounts the helper's own transcript: the finish-time sum races the CLI's transcript write

**Status: reproduced live 2026-11-14 in the dev app built from this branch; not fixed. Priority P2** (the helper line appears, totals are right and nothing is double-counted, but the figure is short of the helper's own spend; a bigger helper can lose more than one message). Found by the usage-burn followups livetest, check 2 ("Helper spend shows in the cost breakdown").

### Observed behaviour

Check-2 run 2 (instance `cbcep562s`, session `98c1d728-6bbb-4131-858c-1470147a614d`, helper `agent-aca59efb88f83ce3e`, 2026-11-14 03:13–03:14 UTC): the Costs page showed `of which helper agents: ≈$0.0750` on the Subagents purpose row and as the totals footnote. The attribution record (`cost-attribution-2026-11-14.jsonl`, ts 1794626026043) booked `helperTranscriptUsage {input 2, output 199, cacheRead 0, cacheWrite5m 29,208}` and `helperTranscriptCost 0.075014`. The helper's own transcript holds two assistant messages — `msg_011Ch26Dm8…` (2 / 199 / 0 / 29,208 cw5) at 03:13:25 and `msg_011Ch26FHrp…` (2 / 66 / 29,208 cr / 2,051 cw5) at 03:13:46.015, the final summary — and the booked usage is the first message only. The full sum priced at the repo rates (`src/shared/data/model-pricing.ts`: claude-sonnet-5-5 input $2 / output $10 per MTok, cache read 0.05×input, cache write 5m 1.25×input) is $0.0837263, exactly what `node scripts/claude-cost-audit-report.mjs --compare-transcripts --day 2026-11-14 --projects …` reports for the same helper. The figure is $0.0087123 short (10.4%). Check-2 run 1 (helper `agent-acdf51df8c3bbe3a9`) shows the same race harder: its transcript line carries usage (2 / 279 / 0 / 29,335 → $0.0761315) yet the record booked all-zero usage and no `helperTranscriptCost` at all.

### Root cause

`ClaudeSubagentUsageTracker.enrich()` (`src/main/cli/adapters/claude-subagent-usage.ts:133-175`) sums `agent-<id>.jsonl` with `sumClaudeSubagentTranscriptUsage` (`src/main/cli/adapters/claude-subagent-meta.ts:199-265`) when the `task_notification` finish frame arrives. The Claude CLI appends the helper's final assistant message line *after* that notification — in run 2 the record was booked 28 ms after the final message's own timestamp and already lacked it — and `flush()` re-sums only non-final samples (`claude-subagent-usage.ts:115-119`), so the undercount is permanent for the session. Re-running the same sum on the same file later returns the full totals (run 2: 4 / 265 / 29,208 / 31,259 across two models; run 1: 2 / 279 / 0 / 29,335): the sum logic is correct, the read happens too early.

### Required behaviour

`of which helper agents: $X` equals the helper's own transcript usage priced at the repo rates: every assistant message in `agent-<id>.jsonl`, including the final summary message written around the finish notification, is included in the figure shown on the Costs page and stored in the attribution record.

### Acceptance

A live helper run where the Costs page's helper figure and the record's `helperTranscriptCost` equal the helper transcript's full sum priced at the repo rates (cross-check `node scripts/claude-cost-audit-report.mjs --compare-transcripts`), plus automated coverage for the late-appended final message — a sum deferred past the finish frame, or a later re-sum that refreshes final samples and updates the stored record.

### Evidence

[Usage burn followups live checks](2026-11-12-usage-burn-followups_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-13), section 2 ("Helper spend shows in the cost breakdown").

<a id="lt-1125"></a>

## LT-1125 — Work-finding Desk and Radar test runs cannot leave a Plan Queue copy: the snapshot names a folder only the main checkout has

**Status: reproduced on 14 November 2026; fixed in source and verified the same day (the change is in commit `11720ef18`, "October updates"); acceptance 1 still needs a real Plan Queue run on the new code. Priority P2.**
Found while running [the keep-this-Mac-as-a-backup live checks](2026-11-12-mac-still-pinned_livetest.md), LT-A5 and LT-A3b.

### Observed behaviour

With "Use this Mac when the others are busy or away" off, `~/.ai-orchestrator/remote-checks/runs.jsonl` has 117 work-finding `project`
lines between 14 November 01:10 and 17:55 UTC with `ranOn: "none"` and `notRunBecause: "the snapshot failed, and this Mac is switched off"`,
about ten an hour from 04:00 to 14:00. The running Plan Queue job `reviewed-reply-integration` (run `3d587e67`) held 112 times between
03:46 and 18:00 with "Waiting for a test machine: the snapshot failed, and this Mac is switched off." and retried every 5 minutes
(median gap 302 s). A checker in another run (`b07b564a`, `contextual-help_livetest.md`) read the same `Not run` line from
`npm --prefix apps/desk run test:quiet` and reported it as "the configured test machine is off". The test machines were not off.

Reproduced directly with `takeSnapshot` from `scripts/remote-checks/snapshot.js` (it writes only to a temporary folder):

| Folder | `folders: ['apps', '_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08']` (Desk, Radar) | `folders: ['apps']` (Desk web, Runner) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `work-finding` main checkout | snapshot taken | snapshot taken |
| `.worktrees/queue/watchdog-faults-b86c5f` | `fatal: pathspec '_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08' did not match any files` | snapshot taken |

The same job's checks did complete three times (14:22, 16:27, 17:34 UTC), each with all four suites on the PC, so the folder was present
in that copy at those times (a worker or checker must have left it there); at 18:05 the copy's `_scratch` was empty.

### Root cause

`scripts/remote-checks/projects.js` gives the work-finding Desk and Radar suites `sends: ['apps', '_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08']`.
`takeSnapshot` passes `sends` to `git add -A -- <folders>`, which fails when a named folder does not exist. In work-finding,
`.gitignore` ignores `_scratch/*` but un-ignores `_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08/`, and nothing in that folder is committed
(`git ls-files` lists nothing), so it exists only in James's main checkout (6.4 MB) and never in a queue copy made from a commit. The
snapshot error is caught in `run-remote.js` (`reason: 'the snapshot failed'`, marked final), and with this Mac switched off
`harness-remote-check.js` turns it into `Not run` (exit 69). The queue treats exit 69 as "no test machine" and holds. With the switch
on, the same fault made these runs fall back to this Mac, which hid it.

### Required behaviour

A Desk or Radar test run from any work-finding folder, including a queue copy without that scratch folder, reaches a test machine. A
snapshot fault that a retry cannot fix is not reported as "waiting for a test machine": its message names the real cause, and a queue
job does not hold on it indefinitely.

### Acceptance

1. From a work-finding queue copy with no `_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08`, `npm --prefix apps/desk run test:quiet` and
   `npm --prefix apps/radar run test:quiet` with the switch off each print "Ran on the Windows PC" (or the test Mac) and add a
   `project` line with a far `ranOn`.
2. A Desk or Radar test that needs the CFP fixture either gets it from committed files or is skipped on purpose with a stated reason.
3. A snapshot that cannot be taken (for example an unreadable file, or a nested repository) shows its real cause in the run's output
   and in the queue's wording, and the queue does not loop on it every 5 minutes. (A named folder that does not exist is now skipped
   on purpose, so it is no longer an example of a broken snapshot.)

### Fix, 14 November 2026

- `scripts/remote-checks/snapshot.js`: `takeSnapshot` skips a named folder the copy does not have (keeping a tracked folder deleted from
  disk) and never runs `git add` with only exclusions. A new `ignored` option sends the untracked files of named git-ignored folders,
  listed by `git ls-files --others` and added by exact name with `--force` (git's own walk does not enter an ignored folder once
  exclusions are given), still leaving out secret-looking names and everything in `node_modules`, and counted in the size limit.
  `SCOPED_GIT_ENV` also clears the four `GIT_*_PATHSPECS` settings, which could otherwise turn the secret exclusions into plain paths
  (this closed the same gap in the commit hook's staged snapshot).
- `scripts/remote-checks/projects.js`: the cohort moved from `sends` to a new `sendsIgnored` field for Desk and Radar, so work-finding's
  `.gitignore` can keep ignoring `_scratch/` and nothing private needs committing or un-ignoring.
- `scripts/remote-checks/run-remote.js`: a failed snapshot is taken once more after 2 s (`takeTwice`), so a file vanishing mid-add does
  not count; the reason now carries git's own `fatal:`/`error:` line. With this Mac switched off, a fault every machine would meet
  (snapshot failed twice or refused, or the machine refuses the checks) returns `final` instead of "not run"; with it on, the other
  machines are not tried for such a fault.
- `harness-remote-check.js`, `scripts/run-tests-quiet.js` and `checks.js` report that case as a failure (exit 1) with
  `Could not use a test machine: <reason>. Waiting would not fix this, so it counts as a failure.` (`checks.js` gives every check that
  result, so the queue's batch answer stays complete). The commit hook still lets the commit through.

Verification: new specs in `snapshot.spec.ts`, `remote-checks.spec.ts` (`takeTwice`), `harness-remote-check.spec.ts` (cohort sent from a
copy that has it, a worktree without it still sent; unsendable work fails without waiting), `checks.spec.ts` and
`run-tests-quiet-remote.spec.ts`; targeted specs 250 passed, full suite 48,076 passed, `npm run checks` all green, all on the Windows
PC. Real folders: the snapshot with the real recipe succeeded for all four suites in the main checkout (5 cohort files sent to Desk and
Radar) and in queue copies `watchdog-faults-b86c5f` and `crm-up-to-scratch-a55823` (none sent). End to end from the main checkout,
`npm run test:quiet -- test/cfpOfflineRelease.test.ts` in `apps/radar` ran the cohort test on the PC: 1 passed, 0 skipped, 8 s. Three
independent reviews; the last two returned PASS.

Private data cleanup, 14 November 2026 (James approved): queue checkpoints had committed the cohort twice to work-finding's local
`main` (`98e32daf1`, removed in `b01ea41e8`; `769550c37`, removed in `8e5e9f643`). None of it was on GitHub (all 16 remote branches
checked). The 34 unpushed commits were rebuilt with only `_scratch/cfp-expansion-2026-09-08` taken out of the two trees that held it
(messages, authors and dates byte-identical; 8 commits got new IDs; final files identical), and `main` and
`queue/reviewed-reply-integration-a808a4` moved from `d74b4af03` to `f8ede8448`. The old commits remain in the local reflog only. The
work-finding `.gitignore` edit that un-ignored the folder was reverted, so `_scratch/` is ignored again.

Still open: acceptance 1 in a real Plan Queue run (the next work-finding queue job's Desk and Radar `project` lines in `runs.jsonl`
should show `ranOn` on a test machine, with no "the snapshot failed" lines).

## LT-1126 — "Chat tool use summary" is missing for most chats that used tools

**Status: reproduced on 14 November 2026, cause not isolated, not repaired. Priority P3.**
Found while running [the keep-this-Mac-as-a-backup live checks](2026-11-12-mac-still-pinned_livetest.md), LT-C.

### Observed behaviour

`installChatToolUsageLog` (`src/main/app/runtime-diagnostics.ts`) should log "Chat tool use summary" when a chat that made tool calls is
removed. Across `app.log.3` to `app.log` (13 November 19:07 to 14 November 18:04 UTC) there are 2 summary lines (`ir22w1fze`, 3 calls, and
`iwkvho2pd`, 319 calls) against 93 "Archived instance" lines. For each chat archived on 14 November whose history file is in this
profile's `conversation-history/`, counting `tool_use` messages made that day before its removal: 15 chats had tool calls, and only
`iwkvho2pd` (377) logged a summary. Missing, for example: `ifqlojrk0` (Claude Opus, "Harness Plan Queue set aside list"), 46 tool calls
between 16:38 and 16:56 UTC, removed at 17:01:51 (log shows "Archived instance" and "Unregistered instance" for it, no summary);
`cmes0tht3` (308 calls); `crk2eswl6` (306); `c6gymczsk` (57); `c7hl31g5j` (56); `cez3ftlhf` (52); and two Codex chats (`xbh1zw3xg`, 7;
`xyut7gpi1`, 2). Harness's own process has run for over a day, so these calls were made in the process that removed the chats.
Hibernation is not the difference: `iwkvho2pd`, which did log a summary, had been hibernated twice too.

### Root cause

Not isolated. The summary counts only `provider:normalized-event` envelopes with `event.kind === 'tool_use'` and a `toolName`. Output
messages of type `tool_use` become `kind: 'output'` events (`toProviderOutputEvent`, `src/main/providers/provider-output-event.ts`), so a
chat whose tool calls reach the bus only as output messages is never counted, and no summary is logged for it. A Plan Queue worker
(`cfhj3oq02`) also logged "Queue round activity" with `toolCalls: 0`, which fits the same gap. Not confirmed: why `iwkvho2pd`'s calls were
counted needs checking first.

### Required behaviour

Every chat that made at least one tool call logs one "Chat tool use summary" when it is removed, whatever the provider and however its
tool calls arrive.

### Acceptance

A unit test that feeds tool calls the way the Claude and Codex adapters really deliver them and expects a summary on removal; then, in the
rebuilt app, a Claude chat and a Codex chat that each make a few tool calls and are closed each log one summary with the right count.

## LT-791 — process search does not discover the host-process tools

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27: the real stdio forwarder's `orchestrator.tool_search` with `query: "process"` returned
only `set_setting` and `git_batch_pull`, omitting both `list_host_processes` and
`stop_leftover_processes`. A fresh build from the queue worktree reproduced the same omission.
Receipts (root checkout, gitignored): `docs/plans/evidence/2026-10-27-host-process-tools-retry/`
`diagnostic-discovery.json` and `compiled-diagnostic-discovery.json`. The full tool catalogue does
contain the host-process tools; this was a discovery failure, not missing registration.

### Root cause

`src/main/mcp/tool-search-ranker.ts` tokenizes whole words without stemming. The host-process tool
names contain plural `processes`, while their descriptions used `programs` and did not contain
singular `process`. Other tools mention the parent process or concurrency, so they alone matched the
prescribed query. There is no evidence that an outdated binary caused it.

### Required behaviour

The default `process` search discovers both host-process tools on deferred and stable tool surfaces,
without changing ranking semantics, ownership checks, caller authentication or fences.

### Acceptance and implementation status

- Both shared descriptions in `src/main/mcp/orchestrator-host-process-tools.ts` contain singular
  `process` (list tool: "for each process"; stop tool: "re-checks every process"). On main since the
  host-process discovery plan's code commit `4e0bd43c8`.
- Regression tests drive the complete catalogue with query `process` and the default limit for the
  deferred surface (`orchestrator-mcp-deferral.spec.ts`) and the stable surface
  (`orchestrator-mcp-stable-tools.spec.ts`). Re-run 2026-11-11: those two files plus
  `orchestrator-host-process-tools.spec.ts` and `tool-search-ranker.spec.ts` pass (4 files, 37 tests).
- Installed discovery verified live 2026-11-07 (LT-A1): a fenced Claude session found both tools with
  query `process` and no limit. Receipt `docs/plans/evidence/2026-11-07-host-process-tools-resume/lt-a1-native-claude.json`
  (SHA-256 `c3e29d1c7d75c5a0bad6515c9125e99919c0a8ffa6f09e26183ff9c84ba0478c`; contents quoted in the
  follow-up live-test document).
- Installed two-session repetition (LT-A3) passed 2026-11-11; receipts under
  `docs/plans/evidence/2026-11-11-host-process-discovery-worker/`.
- Not closed: the coordinator's independent verifier has not yet accepted the work.

Owning documents: [live check](2026-10-27-host-process-discovery-remediation_livetest.md) and
[plan](2026-10-27-host-process-discovery-remediation_plan.md). This entry was recreated on 2026-11-11
after the original, written on the parked branch `queue/2026-10-16-host-process-tools-6e4f78`
(commit `b7fed11ba`), was never merged into this register.

## LT-1113

### LT-1113 — Codex command mode applies no skills policy

**Status: mostly fixed 14 November 2026 on branch `queue/2026-10-20-oct2-phased-tokens-f56759`; only the reminder-as-developer-input part stays open, pending James's decision.**

**Fixed on this branch.** `codexExecPolicyArgs` (`codex/codex-thread-policy.ts`) replaces `codexExecContextWindowArgs`: for non-chat kinds the exec launch carries the context window cap, `skills.max_context_tokens=1500`, and `skills.include_instructions=false` when the checker catalog resolves to omitted (controller settings, or the `omitSkillCatalog` the controller sent a worker), and records `skillCatalogOmitted`. `prepareMessageForExecution` (`codex-exec-adapter.ts`) appends the `Skills for this turn: $name` line from `requiredSkillMentionLine` on every turn, resumes included, so the named skill and a checker's completion-gate skill load by Codex's own selection. Chat is untouched. Covered by `codex-exec-skills.spec.ts` (real adapter, real process runner, exact argv and process input) and `codex-thread-policy.spec.ts`. The real Codex CLI 0.169.0 honoured both overrides and loaded both skills (see the livetest document's 2026-11-14 section).

**Fixed in verifier round 2: old workers are refused.** Workers advertise `codexExecSkillsPolicy: 1` (`worker-agent/capability-reporter.ts`; read by the heartbeat schema in `remote-node/rpc-schemas.ts`, where a malformed value reads as absent). `assertRemoteCodexExecSkillsPolicySupported` (`remote-codex-helper-policy.ts`), part of `assertRemoteCodexWorkerSupported` and called by `RemoteCliAdapter.spawnRemote` before the spawn RPC, refuses every non-chat Codex session on a worker without it. Chats are exempt. Covered by `remote-codex-helper-policy.spec.ts`, `remote-cli-adapter.codex-helper-policy.spec.ts` (real adapter, no spawn RPC sent) and `capability-reporter.spec.ts`.

**Still open, with the reason.** Reminders: `codex -c developer_instructions=... exec` applies the text as developer input on a fresh thread, but `exec resume` ignores it (measured 14 November 2026, Codex 0.169.0: the reply and the stored thread both lack it). A hook passed with `-c hooks.UserPromptSubmit=[...]` does not run either, because Codex requires a persisted trust entry and the only bypass (`--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`) is forbidden. Command mode has no other developer-role input, so a resumed reminder stays user input inside the Harness envelope (`<harness_internal_message>`, which names Harness as the author). Closing it needs the trusted-hook route (a generated hook helper declared and trusted in a private per-session Codex home; the "Worker F4" design in dangling commits `8339c9f74`, `c5c8ed31c`), which adds a runtime TOML parser dependency and depends on a Codex-internal hash format. Decision for James: (1) accept the envelope for command mode and amend the acceptance, or (2) approve building the hook route as its own item.

### Observed behaviour

On a dev app built from this branch (Codex CLI 0.167.0), a Codex session that carries the plan-queue checker role (`planQueueRole: 'verifier'`) was run in app-server mode and in command mode with the checker catalog setting on `omit` and on `full`, plus an ordinary chat. A second Codex worker built from the same checkout ran a checker in command mode.

- App-server mode: the `session-policy` record shows `catalog: omitted` and both `skills.max_context_tokens` and `skills.include_instructions` in the applied keys.
- Command mode, `omit` and `full` alike: the real launch is `codex -c model_context_window=272000 exec --model … --json --sandbox danger-full-access --skip-git-repo-check`, with no skills key and no `session-policy` record. A chat has no `-c` at all.
- Command mode on the worker: `exec --json --sandbox danger-full-access --skip-git-repo-check`, no `-c` at all.
- Internal reminder on resume (`internalSource: 'plan-queue'`): the process input begins `<harness_internal_message source="plan-queue">` and contains the reminder text, so it reaches Codex as user input. The resume argv carries no skills or developer-instruction setting. No `Skills for this turn` line or skill selector is added, and the required completion-gate skill was not loaded by Harness (the model read only the skill the prompt named).

### Root cause

`codex-exec-adapter.ts` builds its arguments (`buildArgs`, about line 76) from account overrides and `codexExecContextWindowArgs` only. `prepareMessageForExecution` adds replay, system prompt and RTK text but never calls `withRequiredSkillMentions` or `requiredSkillInputs`, and never reads `metadata.internalSource`. `resolveCodexThreadPolicy` (`codex/codex-thread-policy.ts`) and `codex-required-skills.ts` are used only on the app-server path (`codex-thread-requests.ts`, `codex-app-server-turn-adapter.ts`). The remote worker has no settings store, so `noPerThreadConfigPolicy` returns no config at all. The repair the Phase D plan records as "Worker F4" lives in dangling queue checkpoint commits (`04e0e59b4`, `8339c9f74`, `c5c8ed31c`), reachable from no branch and not in `main`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Original requirement: supported command-mode Codex work applies the same machine skills policy as app-server work: the 1,500-token cap for non-chat kinds, catalog omission for checkers when the setting selects it, required skills selected explicitly on start, resume and recovery turns, and internal reminders kept out of user input where the CLI allows it. Chat stays native. A worker or policy that cannot apply this refuses rather than running uncapped. Acceptance: the Phase D command-mode livetest checks 1 to 3 pass with the real launch argument list and a skill-load record showing the omitted catalog, and an actual-dispatch test covers the exec path alongside the native one.

## LT-1061

### LT-1061 — an unfinished step that needs James's approval lands as a "deferred check"

**Status: reproduced live 12 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, scratch repository); not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Found while running [the deferred checks live check](2026-11-04-pq-c1-deferred-checks_plan_livetest.md), check 2. A plan with two
steps (add `notice.txt`; publish it to the public website, which needs James's explicit approval that has not been given) ran
with a Cursor worker and a Codex checker. The worker did the file, did not publish, and listed the publish under
`deferred_checks`. The checker passed it with `deferred_checks: ["Publish notice.txt to the live public website"]`,
`criteria_total: 2` and a `need_james` entry classified `policy-gated`. One of two is not more than half, so the item
landed (run `2349e887`, round 2) and the plan was renamed `_completed` with the publish not done. A second plan whose
blocking item was a fact only James has (the release approver's name) got a `needs-human` finding and parked `needs-james`
after one round, as designed (run `e3805f2a`).

### Root cause

`PLAN_DEFERRAL_RULES` in `src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-verdict-prompts.ts` lets a criterion proved "by a person" be a
deferred check, while `FINDING_KIND_RULES` makes "an approval or a fact only James can give" a `needs-human` finding. Both
describe a step waiting on James, and nothing says which wins when the work itself (not a check of finished work) is waiting.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

State in the prompt that a deferred check is a check of work that is built and only needs a rebuilt app, a person or an
outside service to prove it, and that a step whose work is not done because it needs James is a `needs-human` FAIL. Acceptance:
the same approval-gated plan parks `needs-james` naming the approval and starts no new worker round, in at least two runs;
the six-criteria plan with one rebuilt-app check still lands.

## LT-1062

### LT-1062 — a livetest with one check left for James sometimes parks instead of landing

**Status: reproduced live 12 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (1 of 2 runs); not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Two `livetests` runs on the same shape of document (one runnable check, one that needs a physical iPhone), Cursor worker,
Codex checker. Run `c43b3a8b`: PASS, `document_complete: false`, `need_james` classified `real`; landed, document kept its
active name. Run `0d97177a`: FAIL with one `needs-human` finding naming the iPhone, plus the same `need_james` entry; the
item parked `needs-james` after round 1 and nothing landed.

### Root cause (not proven)

For a livetest the prompt's only example call is a FAIL (`verdictExamples`, `plan-queue-verdict-prompts.ts`), and the finding
kind rules (a FAIL of only `needs-human` findings starts no worker round) apply to livetests as well. The checker is free to
read an open check as either a PASS with `need_james` or a FAIL with a `needs-human` finding, and the two now end differently.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

For a livetest, say that a check left for James is a PASS with `need_james` and `document_complete: false`, never a FAIL
finding, and show that PASS as the example. Acceptance: three runs on the same document all land with the document
unrenamed and the open check classified.

## LT-1063

### LT-1063 — a missing signing identity is replaced by a made-up value and the check passes

**Status: reproduced live 14 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, scratch repository); not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Found while re-running check 1 of [the deferred checks live check](2026-11-04-pq-c1-deferred-checks_plan_livetest.md). A plan
had two criteria: create `notes.txt`, and `npm run sign` must exit 0. `npm run sign` exits 1 unless the environment variable
`LT3CCE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` is set, and the plan said every criterion can be checked on this computer and none may be listed as
a deferred check. The variable was not set anywhere on the computer. The Cursor worker ran `npm run sign` with the variable set
to a 19-character value it made up for that one command, reported exit 0 and said so in its summary ("The signing identity was
not on this computer, so npm run sign was run with a local fixture"). The Codex checker repeated the command with
`LT3CCE_SIGNING_IDENTITY=<local-fixture>`, got exit 0, and passed the plan (`criteria_total` 2, no findings, no deferred
checks). The item landed in round 1 and the plan was renamed `_completed` (run `a1e6b541`). Nothing was parked, so James would
never learn the real signing step was never run.

With the same script in an earlier run (`305bb017`, round 1) the worker did the opposite and listed the signing step as a deferred
check; that run also landed after the checker accepted it (1 of 2 criteria is not more than half).

A third plan with the same script, whose text now forbids stand-in values and deferral (run `e9ceb0ba`), did stop at round 1, but the checker labelled
the missing identity `needs-human` ("An operator must provide LT3CCE_SIGNING_IDENTITY ..."), so the item parked `needs-james`
("Waiting for your answer") rather than `needs-setup` ("Something is missing on this computer"). Two more runs of that plan
(`ea099c2e`, `a7cabe87`) were labelled `environment` and parked `needs-setup`, as the prompt intends: 2 of 3 right.

### Root cause (not proven)

`FINDING_KIND_RULES` in `src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-verdict-prompts.ts` names "a missing credential" as an `environment`
finding but says nothing about a gate that passes only because the checker (or the worker) supplied its own stand-in for the
missing value. The checker treats a local fixture as a way to run the gate rather than as proof the real thing is missing, and an "operator-only" credential reads to it as either `environment` or `needs-human`.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Tell the checker that a gate which needs a value only the operator holds (a signing identity, a token, a key) cannot be passed
with a value made up for the run; if the real value is not available it is an `environment` FAIL naming the missing thing, even
when a stand-in makes the command exit 0, and that a missing credential is `environment` (not `needs-human`, which is for an
approval or a decision). Acceptance: the same plan parks `needs-setup` naming `LT3CCE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` in at least three of three
runs.

## LT-1064

### LT-1064 — Resume after a missing setting is provided does not reach a Codex checker

**Status: reproduced live 14 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, scratch repository); cause likely, not proven; not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Found while running the resume step of check 1 in [the deferred checks live check](2026-11-04-pq-c1-deferred-checks_plan_livetest.md).
A plan whose final step is `npm run sign` (it exits 1 unless `LT3CCE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` is set) parked `needs-setup` at round 1 with
the note "Resume once this is provided" (run `ea099c2e`). The dev app was stopped and started again with the variable in its
environment, then Resume was pressed (`resume-item`). The item went straight back to `working` and then `verifying`; the
Cursor worker reported that the variable was present and `npm run sign` exited 0. The Codex checker's own `npm run sign` still exited 1
and it reported an `environment` finding ("absent from this verifier environment"), so the item parked `needs-setup` again.

### Root cause (likely; no environment dump was taken)

The saved Codex configuration on this Mac has `[shell_environment_policy] inherit = "core"`, which gives a Codex shell only the
core variables plus the ones listed under `[shell_environment_policy.set]`. A variable set for Harness reaches Claude and Cursor
sessions but not the commands a Codex checker runs. The `needs-setup` note tells James to "provide" the thing without saying where.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Either pass the setting the item names to the checker's shell, or make the `needs-setup` note say where the setting has to be put so
that the checker can see it. Acceptance: with the variable set where the note says, Resume on the same plan lets the Codex checker's
`npm run sign` exit 0 and the plan lands.

## LT-1129

### LT-1129 — a missing validator program is passed as a deferred check instead of parking for setup

**Status: reproduced live 12 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, scratch repository); not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Found in the first run of check 3 in [the deferred checks live check](2026-11-04-pq-c1-deferred-checks_plan_livetest.md) (run `96cc4797`, evidence run of 12 November, check 8 row). The plan had two criteria and one of them needed a real validator program that is not installed on this computer. The Codex checker did not report an `environment` finding naming the program. It put the step under `deferred_checks` and passed the plan once the other round-1 problem (a `code` finding) was fixed, so the item landed (1 of 2 criteria deferred is not more than half). Nothing parked `needs-setup`, so James would not learn the validator had never run on any computer.

This is the same family as LT-1063 (a missing signing identity passed with a stand-in), but a different cause: here the checker chose the deferral route for something an agent can only run once setup is done, rather than supplying a stand-in. Only one run of this shape was kept (run `96cc4797`); its exact plan text and the checker's wording were not saved beyond the summary in the live check, so the frequency is not measured.

### Root cause (not proven)

`PLAN_DEFERRAL_RULES` and `FINDING_KIND_RULES` in `src/main/plan-queue/plan-queue-verdict-prompts.ts` define a deferred check as something proved "in a rebuilt or restarted app, by a person or by an outside service". A program missing from the checker's computer reads as "an outside service" or "cannot run now" to the checker, and the `environment` rule ("a gate that cannot run on this computer") does not say that it wins over deferral.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Tell the checker that a gate which cannot run because a program, credential or setting is missing from this computer is an `environment` FAIL naming the missing thing, never a deferred check; a deferred check is only for something that needs a rebuilt app, a person or an outside service even when the computer is set up correctly. Acceptance: the same plan parks `needs-setup` naming the missing program in at least three of three runs.

<a id="lt-1128"></a>

## LT-1128

### LT-1128 — the checker asks for automated tests in a repository that has no test runner

**Status: reproduced live 12 and 14 November 2026 on the rebuilt dev app (isolated profile, scratch repositories); not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

Seen repeatedly while running checks 3, 4 and 8 in [the deferred checks live check](2026-11-04-pq-c1-deferred-checks_plan_livetest.md). In scratch repositories that contain a few text files and no test runner, the Codex checker added a `code` finding along the lines of "no automated test" in round 1 of runs `96cc4797`, `61886f5a`, `2349e887`, `df71bf9f` and `305bb017` (the first three on 12 November, the last two on 14 November; `0e232d3e` had a similar "no file added" finding in round 1). The plans never asked for a test and the repositories had nothing that could run one, so the worker had to spend a fix round on it. In `61886f5a` a mixed `environment` + `code` FAIL went to a fix round instead of parking for setup; that is what the design says for any `code` finding, so the only fault is the unwarranted finding.

### Root cause (not proven)

`FINDING_KIND_RULES` makes `code` the "normal kind" for anything a worker can fix and says nothing about how to treat a missing test. The checker applies its own habit of asking for test coverage even when the plan and repository give no way to run one.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Tell the checker to report a missing automated test only when the plan or the repository's conventions require one and a test runner exists, and otherwise to judge the plan's own acceptance criteria. Acceptance: on a one-file scratch repository with no test runner, three of three plan runs have no finding about missing tests in round 1.

## LT-1158

### LT-1158 — accepting "Leave" on a pop-up that stopped close_tab leaves the tab open

**Status: source fix verified 12 November 2026 (extension 0.2.57); installed-extension check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

Reproduced twice on windows-pc on 12 November 2026 (Browser Gateway to the real Chrome, throwaway page with a
`beforeunload` listener and a real key press). `browser.close_tab` failed with `browser_dialog_open: the page opened
Chrome's "Leave site?" pop-up`; `browser.handle_dialog { accept: true, actionHint: "close the test tab" }` returned
`succeeded` (`dialogType: "beforeunload"`); the tab then stayed open: a snapshot succeeded 8 seconds later (first run)
and 20 seconds later (second run), and `list_targets { refresh: true }` still listed it. A second `close_tab` then
closed it with no new pop-up. The same accept after a pop-up raised by `navigate` does complete the navigation.
Evidence: [Check 2b](2026-10-28-browser-page-popups_livetest.md).

### Root cause

Confirmed only as far as the code and the two runs show. `resources/browser-extension/background.js` answers the
pop-up with `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog` and relies on the `chrome.tabs.remove` it left pending to finish the close.
In real Chrome that pending call did not close the tab. Why Chrome drops it is not established (the extension's
debugger session and the pop-up were both answered cleanly); a second `tabs.remove` after the answer works, which
is what the fix uses. The previous test only covered the Stay path.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

After `handle_dialog { accept: true }` on a pop-up that interrupted `close_tab`, the tab is closed without the caller
repeating the close. Extension 0.2.57 (`finishCloseAfterLeave`) checks for the tab for up to two seconds and, if it is
still open, asks Chrome to close it again (bounded to two seconds so a second pop-up cannot hang the answer). Stay and
a pop-up raised by another command are unchanged. Acceptance: `browser-extension-assets.spec.ts` cases under
"answering the pop-up that stopped close_tab" (the Leave case fails without the fix); and on windows-pc running 0.2.57,
Check 2b of the page pop-ups livetest ends with the tab gone from `list_targets { refresh: true }` after one accept.

## LT-1168

### LT-1168 — Escape on a focused Settings icon also leaves Settings

### Observed behaviour

Dev app on this Mac, 10 November 2026, Settings menu squeezed to icons. Tab to the "General" icon: its hint opens.
Press Escape: the hint closes and the browser URL goes from `/settings` to `/`, so the whole Settings page closes
too. Reproduced with a real key press over the debugging connection (`esc-probe.mjs` in the run's scratch folder):
focused General, tooltip `["General"]`, URL `/settings`; after Escape, tooltip `[]`, URL `/`.

### Root cause

`aio-tooltip.directive.ts` binds `(keydown.escape)': 'hide()'` with no `stopPropagation`. The key then bubbles to
`SettingsComponent.onKeydown` (`settings.component.ts`), whose own comment says Escape closes "the deepest open
overlay first ... never more than one thing at a time", and which calls `goBack()` when no drawer is open. It does not
know a hint is open.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Escape pressed while a hint is open closes only the hint; a second Escape then leaves Settings. Acceptance: with a
Settings icon focused and its hint open, one Escape leaves the URL on `/settings`; a second Escape returns to `/`. Add a
directive spec that the key event is stopped only when a hint was actually open (Escape with no hint must still reach
other handlers).

### Fix (11 November 2026)

Fix: `AioTooltipDirective.onEscape` stops the key only while a hint is open (spec: Escape reaches other handlers only when no hint is open). `plan-handoff-dialog.component.spec.ts` now expects the first Escape to close the open hint and the second to close the picker.


### Live recheck

Verified live 16 November 2026 (rebuilt dev app, real key events): with a collapsed Settings icon focused and its hint open, one Escape closed only the hint and the URL stayed `/settings`; a second Escape returned to `/`. Checked on General, Display & input, Agents and Second opinion.

## LT-1169

### LT-1169 — a waiting session's reason detail is hover-only in the header

### Observed behaviour

Dev app, 10 November 2026, seeded session with `waitReason: {kind:'backoff', attempt:2, retryAt: now+300 s}`. The header
reads "Charlie waiting rename Backing off — retry in 203s" and nothing else. "Attempt 2, retry at …" appears only in the
hint on the label. The migration plan says "the wait reason is now visible text ('Backing off — retry in 5s — Attempt
2, retry at …')" and the live check 1f.2 requires the detail to be visible without hovering.

`instance-header.component.html` renders `<span class="wait-reason-label" tabindex="0"
[appTooltip]="waitReasonDetail()">{{ waitReasonLabel() }}</span>`; no element prints `waitReasonDetail()`. The
as-built claim was not what landed in `6824ebec1`: `instance-header.component.spec.ts` ("explains the waiting state on a
focusable hover…") asserts `textContent` does **not** contain "Attempt 2".

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Print the detail beside the label whenever the session is waiting, keeping the hint only for anything longer. Acceptance:
the header text of a backoff-waiting session contains the attempt and retry time without hovering; update the spec so it
asserts the visible text rather than its absence.

### Fix (11 November 2026)

Fix: the header prints the detail beside the label (`.wait-reason-detail`); the specs assert the visible text. The old hover wording "allowance resets at" was retired in the wording ledger (a quota wait has no header label; its banner carries the time).


### Live recheck

Verified live 16 November 2026 (rebuilt dev app): a session backing off showed "Backing off — retry in 300s — Attempt 2, retry at 01:48:16" in the header with no hover. The live check also showed the first fix printed "300s— Attempt" with no space before the dash (Angular dropped the whitespace-only text between the label and the detail span); fixed the same day with `&ngsp;` and the header spec now pins "Waiting for interrupt… — Attempt 2".

## LT-1160

### LT-1160 — the shared Help panel opens under the title bar, so its Close button cannot be clicked

**Status: reproduced 10 November 2026 on the dev app built from `queue/2026-10-10-oct-phase4-tooltips-6bbc5c`; fixed on that branch and re-checked live 14 November 2026.**

**Fix:** `.app-container.macos/.windows` now define `--title-bar-height` (52 px / 40 px, also used for their `padding-top`); the Help drawer's `aside` uses `inset: var(--title-bar-height, 0px) 0 0 auto`, so it starts below the title bar and its chips; glossary entries have `scroll-margin-top: var(--spacing-md)`. Spec: `help-drawer.component.spec.ts` ("starts below the fixed title bar"). Live result is in the 14 November (second) section of the Phase 4 tooltips live-test document.

### Observed behaviour

With the window at 1400 by 900, a real mouse click at the centre of the Help panel's "×" does nothing and the panel stays
open. `document.elementFromPoint` at the button's centre returns `DIV.title-bar-overlay.macos`, and at the panel's own
title ("Working in a session") returns the quota chip button. The panel (`aside`, `position: fixed; inset: 0 0 0 auto`,
`z-index: calc(var(--z-modal) + 3)` = 403) starts at the very top of the window, but `.title-bar-drag-area` (`z-index:
1000`) and `.title-bar-overlay` (`z-index: 1100`) in `app.component.scss` sit above it. The same panel opened from the
Settings "Help & tips" drawer at 1000 by 700 shows the same cover. Escape and a click on the dark backdrop close
it while focus is inside the panel, and focus returns to the opening control. After the dead click on the "×", focus fell to
`BODY` and Escape no longer closed the panel (the handler is `(keydown.escape)` on the `aside` only); only the backdrop did.

Second symptom, same cause: opening a glossary word (the queued "steer" word, Settings → RTK savings "Output
compression") runs `anchor.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` in `help-drawer.component.ts`. The entry's heading ends
up at y = 0.06 px and its definition at y 22 to 58 px, where the drag strip and the status chips take the pointer and
hide the right half of the text. The panel's own header has scrolled away at that point (header top at -2012 px), so
there is no visible way to close it with the mouse.

### Root cause

The drawer was written as a full-height overlay with no top offset, but the title bar (52 px on macOS, 40 px on
Windows) and its right-hand chip cluster are fixed above every modal layer. Nothing reserves that strip for the
drawer, and the scroll target has no margin below it.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The panel's header and Close button are fully visible and clickable below the title bar (offset the drawer by the title
bar height, or lower the title bar's layer while a modal Help panel is open), and the scrolled-to entry lands fully
below the title bar (for example `scroll-margin-top`). Acceptance: at 1400 by 900 and 800 by 600, in dark and light
themes, `elementFromPoint` at the centre of "Close help" returns that button, a mouse click on it closes the panel, and
after clicking "steer" the whole highlighted entry (heading and definition) is visible. Add a spec for the offset.

## LT-1135

### LT-1135 — transcript minimap tick buttons are too small and too close together

**Status: reproduced live 15 November 2026 in the rebuilt dev app; not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

During sidechat cleanup acceptance, the full-panel axe 4.13.0 audit reported one serious `target-size` violation affecting two transcript minimap buttons (`.tick:nth-child(1)` and `.tick.active`). Both measured 20 × 7 CSS pixels; axe also reported insufficient space to adjacent targets (safe clickable-space diameter 0 px). Evidence: [audit result](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/live-axe-result.json), [final wide panel](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/panel-wide-final.png), and [final narrow panel](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/panel-narrow-final.png).

### Root cause and scope

The shared [transcript jump rail](../../src/renderer/app/features/instance-detail/transcript-jump-rail.component.ts#L160) fixes each `.tick` button at 20 × 7 px. Its [marker layout](../../src/renderer/app/features/instance-detail/transcript-jump-rail.markers.ts#L44) normally separates tick centres by 12 px and can compress that to 4 px. The separately drawn thin line does not enlarge the button's hit area.

This is an existing shared transcript defect, outside the sidechat throwaway cleanup functionality. The jump-rail component has no diff from the task baseline `234b7e405^`; the sidechat's existing `app-output-stream` binding is unchanged. The [shared output stream](../../src/renderer/app/features/instance-detail/output-stream.component.html#L431) renders the same navigator in this panel. No source repair or accessibility waiver is included in the sidechat task.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- Make each tick satisfy the 24 × 24 CSS-pixel target-size rule or its valid spacing exception, without overlapping clickable targets or losing access to densely packed turns.
- Re-run the full-panel accessibility check on rebuilt wide and narrow sidechat layouts and an ordinary session with an overflowing transcript. The minimap must have no `target-size` violation; include a dense turn count and earlier-message loading.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus, prompt previews, Escape dismissal, Enter/Space activation, correct turn jumps and the active-turn indication. Retain the new live evidence with the future repair's acceptance record.

## LT-1136

### LT-1136 — Escape closes the model picker without returning focus to its chip

**Status: reproduced live 15 November 2026 in the rebuilt dev app; not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

A single browser-control session used real keys: Tab focused the sidechat's `.compact-picker__chip`, Enter expanded the picker and focused `.model-picker-search__input`, and Escape closed the menu (`aria-expanded="false"`) but left `document.activeElement` on `BODY`. The retained keyboard assertion intentionally failed on the missing focus return. Evidence: [complete single-session keyboard sequence](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/live-keyboard-final.json) and [chip focus](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/live-keyboard-tab.json).

### Root cause and scope

The shared [compact model picker](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L216) defaults `trapFocus` to false. Its [focus-trap effect](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L309) therefore creates no trap for this host. Escape dismisses the selection panel through `closeMenu()`; [closeFocusTrap](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L497) restores focus only through `focusTrap?.restore()`, so the default path has nothing that returns focus to the trigger before the focused overlay disappears.

The task baseline `234b7e405^` has the same default and restoration mechanism, and the earlier sidechat binding also omitted `trapFocus`. The sidechat cleanup moved this existing picker to the composer and added only `max-width` styling in the shared component; it did not introduce this focus-restoration path. This is separate shared-component repair work, outside the sidechat throwaway cleanup; no source repair or accessibility waiver is included here.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- When Escape dismisses a picker whose menu owns keyboard focus, return focus to the chip that opened it, including the default `trapFocus=false` path. Preserve intentional focus changes caused by navigation or parent teardown.
- Repeat real Tab → Enter → Escape in one browser-control session on a rebuilt sidechat panel. Observe the search field focused while open, the menu closed afterwards, and the original chip focused; the next Tab must continue from that chip rather than the page body.
- Cover default and focus-trapped shared picker callers in regression checks, including an ordinary session picker and a modal host. Preserve nested focus trapping, model selection and normal dismissal. Retain the live keyboard results with the future repair's acceptance record.

## LT-1137

### LT-1137 — model picker chip refers to a missing controlled panel

**Status: reproduced live 15 November 2026 in the rebuilt dev app on the test Mac; not repaired.**

### Observed behaviour

The real-key sequence opened the sidechat model picker and focused its search input. The retained open-state receipt reports `expanded="true"` and `menuOpen=true`, but `controlsTargetPresent=false`: the chip's `aria-controls` value does not identify an element in the document even while the controlled panel is visible. Evidence: [test Mac keyboard and accessibility relationship result](../../_scratch/sidechat-cleanup/live-keyboard-mac-result.json), specifically its `opened` state. This is a separate defect from the Escape focus loss recorded in [LT-1136](#lt-1136).

### Root cause and scope

The shared [compact model picker trigger](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L80) assigns `aria-controls` from its [generated menu identifier](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L202). Its [selection-panel binding](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/compact-model-picker.component.ts#L110) supplies no matching `id`. The [selection panel's dialog](../../src/renderer/app/features/models/model-selection-panel.component.ts#L75) also has no supplied identifier or host-ID setter that connects this value to the rendered panel. The trigger therefore advertises a relationship that the DOM does not provide.

The task baseline `234b7e405^` has the same trigger and selection-panel binding. The current diff for the shared compact picker adds only `max-width` styling, so the sidechat cleanup did not introduce the missing target. This is existing shared-component accessibility repair work outside the sidechat throwaway cleanup; no source repair or accessibility waiver is included here.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- While the picker is open, make the chip's `aria-controls` resolve to the actual controlled panel with a unique, stable identifier. Keep the advertised popup semantics consistent with the rendered panel.
- Repeat real Tab → Enter on the rebuilt test Mac app and inspect the expanded chip and its referenced element in the same browser-control session. Require an existing, visible controlled panel while open; record its accessible role and name and preserve normal search and model selection.
- Check an ordinary session picker and a modal host as shared callers, including multiple pickers on one page. References must resolve to their own panels without duplicate identifiers. When a panel is removed on close, omit any reference that would point to a missing element. Retain the resulting live evidence with the future repair's acceptance record.

## LT-1161

### LT-1161 — jump-rail preview card is dark with dark text in the light theme

**Status: source fix applied 10 November 2026 (`transcript-jump-rail.component.ts`); verified live in a hidden off-screen window; Windows check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

On the dev renderer with the light theme applied through the real settings path (`SettingsStore.applyTheme('light')`), Tab to a transcript tick. The preview card appears with a dark background and the prompt line in near-black (`rgb(12, 10, 9)`), contrast 1.06:1 against the card; the reply line is 4.37:1. In the dark theme the same card measures 18.28:1 and 7.07:1.

### Root cause

`.preview` set `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--surface-color, #1a1d24) 94%, transparent)`. It predates the keyboard work: the card has been dark-only since the July hover preview.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The card background follows the theme (`--bg-elevated`, the variable the other popovers use). Acceptance: with the light theme, the prompt line against the card is at least 4.5:1 and the reply line likewise; the dark theme is unchanged in look.
