## LT-1163

### LT-1163 — Escape with a hint showing also closes the page or dialog around the control

**Status: source fix applied 14 November 2026; on merging with main (18 November 2026) this branch's mark-the-press approach was dropped in favour of the fix already on main: the hint's Escape handler stops the press (`event.stopPropagation()`) only while a hint is open, so Settings never sees it (`aio-tooltip.directive.ts`, covered by the directive spec). Live recheck of the Settings sequence and of the attachment preview (which now also stays open on the first Escape while a hint shows) pending on the rebuilt copy.**

### Observed behaviour

Reproduced on 14 November 2026 in a dev app copy on the test Mac (real keys over the debugging port). Settings > Provider accounts, Tab to "Sign in again": its hint ("Opens a terminal already running the sign-in command") opens. Pressing Escape closed the hint and also navigated away from Settings (path `/settings` became `/`). The hint's own Escape handler and the Settings page's Escape handler (`settings.component.ts`, `onKeydown`: "Escape closes the deepest open overlay first ... never more than one thing at a time") both ran for one key press.

### Root cause

`AioTooltipDirective` handled `(keydown.escape)` with `hide()` and left no sign on the event, so the Settings page's own Escape handler could not tell that the press had already been used for a hint.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

When a hint is showing, Escape closes the hint and the press goes no further (the directive stops it), so the first Escape closes only the hint and the second leaves Settings. With no hint showing nothing changes. Every page or dialog that closes on Escape, including the attachment preview, behaves the same way. Acceptance: the Settings sequence above leaves the page open with the hint closed, a second Escape leaves Settings; the attachment preview stays open on the first Escape while a hint shows and closes on the second; the directive case passes.

## LT-1164

### LT-1164 — six controls with no accessible name (Hooks, Reviews, RLM context browser)

**Status: source fix applied 14 November 2026 (`hooks-page.component.ts`, `review-results.component.ts`, `context-query-panel.component.ts`); first four verified in the accessibility tree; Start and End Offset verified by a component test only (`context-query-panel.component.spec.ts`), not yet in the live accessibility tree; spoken check pending.**

### Observed behaviour

A Tab-order sweep of 44 screens in the test Mac dev app (14 November 2026) listed every focusable control with no visible text, label or aria-label, then read each one's accessible name from Chromium's accessibility tree. Four had an empty name: the `textarea.textarea` in Hooks > Evaluation Preview, the `input.confidence-slider` range in Reviews ("Min Confidence: n%" is a separate span), and the two `input.query-input.small` number fields in the RLM context browser (the "Max Results" and "Top K Results" text is a separate span). Verifier review the same day found two more in the RLM Slice query mode, which the sweep never rendered (it only saw the default Grep mode): the Start Offset and End Offset number fields (`context-query-panel.component.ts`, sibling spans only).

### Root cause

None of the six had an `aria-label`, `<label for>` or `aria-labelledby`; the visible words sit in sibling spans. They predate the tooltip migration (like LT-1162).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

Each control has an accessible name: "Evaluation context (JSON)", "Minimum confidence", "Max results", "Top K results", "Start offset", "End offset". Acceptance: the accessibility tree gives each control that name; behaviour unchanged.


## LT-1185

### LT-1185 — Sort out loses its Plan Queue tools when reopened from History after a restart

**Status: reproduced live 16 November 2026 in the installed app; fix built 17 November 2026; awaiting the live recheck.**

### Observed behaviour

Live check 2 of the [Set aside live checks](2026-11-15-set-aside-agent-merges-itself_plan_livetest.md): after the 23:03 restart on 16 November the Sort out session was reopened twice (16 November 23:08 and 17 November 18:53). The app log records `HistoryRestoreCoordinator "History restore complete" restoreMode native-resume` for both, on the same History thread. Neither restored session's saved state held the `planQueueSetAsideFolder` marker, and its Set aside tool calls were refused with "Only the agent started from the Set aside tab on the Plan Queue page may use this tool". The original Sort out session did hold the marker.

### Root cause

The earlier fix carried the marker only through crash-recovery revival (continuity state). A restart archives open sessions into History, and reopening one goes through `HistoryRestoreCoordinator`, which builds the new session from the History entry. The History entry had no field for the marker, and startup archiving of crash autosaves (`archive-recoverable-sessions.ts`) also dropped it.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- The History entry records the folder when a Sort out session is archived, keeps it when the thread is archived again, and startup archiving of a crash autosave keeps it too.
- Reopening the entry from History, by native resume or by replay, gives the new session the marker, merged with any phone-member policy. A fork of the conversation does not get it.
- Live: rebuild and restart, press Sort out, restart again, reopen the Sort out session and confirm its Set aside tool calls succeed (check 2 of the live-test document).
- Fix record: [2026-11-17-sort-out-keeps-tools-after-history-restore_plan_completed.md](2026-11-17-sort-out-keeps-tools-after-history-restore_plan_completed.md).

## LT-1177

### LT-1177 — cancelling a native compaction leaves its row "Compacting the session…" for good

**Status: patched in source and live rechecked 16 November 2026 (OpenCode 2.3.0); independent review pending.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-16-opencode-2-live-run), dev app built from this queue worktree, OpenCode 2.3.0 installed in a temporary folder, isolated profile.

### Observed behaviour

On a disposable OpenCode 2 session (model `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, three answered turns), `compactInstance` showed the row "Compacting the session…"
(`phase: in_progress`, `streaming: true`). `interruptInstance` about 1.5 s later returned the session to idle, but the row stayed `in_progress`
with `streaming: true` in both the main process and the renderer, for as long as the session was watched (25 s and longer). Two runs, same result.

### Root cause

Instrumented adapter log (since removed), interrupt at 12:55:28.765: `cancelCurrentPrompt` sent `session/cancel` and, as designed, rejected the local prompt
promise at once. That made the native attempt return false, so `CompactionCoordinator` started `restart-with-summary` at 12:55:28.771.
OpenCode's `compaction_update status=cancelled` (same `compactionId`, confirmed with a direct ACP session: it arrives 7 ms after
`session/cancel`) reached the adapter at 12:55:29.000, 235 ms later, as the old adapter was being replaced. The row was keyed correctly
(`compactRet: cancelled`), but the replacement meant it never reached the transcript. Nothing else finishes a pending compaction row.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A cancelled compaction finishes its pending row whatever happens next. Fix: `OpenCodeAcpUpdates.cancelPending()` finishes every pending compaction row as
"Compaction cancelled." when `AcpCliAdapter.cancelCurrentPrompt` runs; later progress for a finished row is ignored and the provider's own marker leaves it
cancelled. Tests: `opencode-acp-updates.spec.ts` (two cases) and `acp-cli-adapter.opencode-v2.spec.ts` ("finishes a pending compaction row when the turn is
interrupted"), the last failing before the change. Live recheck, same fixture: the row read `in_progress` at the interrupt and `cancelled` in every sample from
2.5 s on, and the rendered transcript showed "Compaction cancelled.".

## LT-1178

### LT-1178 — cancelling a native compaction still replaces the provider thread

**Status: reproduced live 16 November 2026 (OpenCode 2.3.0); not repaired.**

Source: [Oct2 later live checks](2026-10-20-oct2-later_livetest.md#evidence-run--2026-11-16-opencode-2-live-run).

### Observed behaviour

Same fixture as LT-1177. After `interruptInstance` during a native compaction the session went `initializing`, then `busy`, then `idle`, and the transcript gained a
"Harness (automated)" message beginning "[Context Compaction Continuity Package] Compaction method: restart-with-summary" with the recent turns. The log shows
"Native compaction failed; recovered via restart-with-summary … the provider thread was replaced, not compacted in place" and an exit (143) of the old OpenCode process.
The person had asked for the compaction to stop; the app did a heavier one.

### Root cause

`CompactionCoordinator.runCompaction` (`compaction-coordinator.ts`) treats any false from the native strategy as a failed attempt and falls back to
`restartCompactStrategy`. A client cancel (`ACP_PROMPT_CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT_MESSAGE`, thrown into `sendAcpCompactionCommand`) is indistinguishable from an error
once `compactContext()` has returned false.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A compaction the person cancelled ends as cancelled: no fallback, the provider thread is kept and the session returns to idle. Needs a cancelled outcome from
`compactContext()` through `nativeCompact` (`compaction-runtime.ts`) into the coordinator, which must not start `restartCompactStrategy` for it. Acceptance: repeat the
LT-1177 fixture; the session keeps its provider session id and no continuity package appears.

## LT-1040 — entering Settings throws while the control shell looks up the active page

**Status:** fixed on main (shared fix with LT-790; see the completed plans listed below). Re-verify after landing. Origin: LT-A1 to LT-B3 live test, 2026-10-27 run (originally recorded there as the branch-local number LT-723, which collides with an unrelated Plan Queue defect; LT-732 and LT-791 were also used and not retained). Pending independent verification.

### Observed behaviour

2026-10-27, isolated dev profile. The first dashboard to Settings navigation logged `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'data')` from `ControlSurfaceShellComponent.findActiveSurfaceId`. A second dashboard to Settings navigation with a cleared capture buffer logged it again. Settings then rendered and its controls worked. Receipt: `settings-route-repro.json` in the root checkout's `docs/plans/evidence/2026-10-27-host-process-tools/` (that folder is gitignored by `docs/plans/*evidence/`, so it exists only in the root checkout).

### Root cause

The shell's constructor subscription read `current.snapshot.data` on live child routes, which have no snapshot until their outlet activates. The recognised snapshot tree (`route.snapshot.firstChild`) already existed.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

The active page id comes from the complete recognised snapshot tree; the deepest page with metadata wins; no exception on direct load or navigation to Settings, Local AI, Automations or a nested route. Acceptance: `control-surface-shell.component.spec.ts` real-router cases (they failed on the old code, per the root plan `2026-10-27-control-surface-route-snapshot-remediation_plan_completed.md`) pass, and a 2026-11-11 dev-app run opened Settings and the page collected no window error events (script `e13.js` in the root checkout's `docs/plans/evidence/2026-11-11-host-process-fence-ui-worker/scripts/`; the run is described in the livetest document).

## LT-1041 — searching for "process" does not find the host process tools

**Status:** fixed on main. Installed-app discovery verified 2026-11-07 (`evidence/2026-11-07-host-process-tools-resume/installed-discovery-2026-11-07.json`) and a native Claude session found both tools with the default limit. Pending independent verification. Origin: LT-A1 live test, 2026-10-27 retry (originally recorded there as the branch-local number LT-791, not retained).

### Observed behaviour

The installed forwarder and a fresh worktree build both answered a `process` search with only `set_setting` and `git_batch_pull`. Looking the tools up by exact name worked.

### Root cause

The tool-search ranker matches whole words and does not stem. The tool names contain the plural `processes` and the descriptions said "programs", so the singular `process` matched neither.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

A `process` search with the default limit returns both tools on the deferred and stable surfaces, with no change to search semantics, schemas, ownership rules or the fence. Acceptance: the full-catalogue regressions in `orchestrator-mcp-deferral.spec.ts` (line 176) and `orchestrator-mcp-stable-tools.spec.ts` (line 119) pass; the installed run above found both tools. Implementation notes: root plan `2026-10-27-host-process-discovery-remediation_plan.md`.

## LT-1197

### LT-1197 — Chrome's HTTP sign-in prompt cannot be answered on a computer with a protected site

**Status: reproduced live 21 November 2026 on `windows-pc`; fixed in 098888229; live checks passed on `windows-pc` the same day.**

### Observed behaviour

21 November 2026, 01:34-02:10, and again at 11:17: `browser.find_or_open` of
`https://dev.myshellartstudio.com/wp-login.php` on `windows-pc` returned
`inspection_unavailable`, `url: https://redacted.invalid/` and no `httpAuthChallenge`.
`browser.request_credential_access` and `browser.fill_http_auth` were refused with
`target_unavailable` (or `invalid_url` without `url`). The Harness log has four
`Saved-login tab check failed` lines, each `snapshot_allowed_failed` /
`browser_secret_inspection_unavailable`. The same login worked on `ct-test-mac`.

### Root cause

`windows-pc` has `login.lcn.com` tabs under secret protection, so the extension checks every tab
for frames of a protected site. While Chrome's prompt waits, Chrome has committed a blank error
page at the challenged URL that no script can run in (measured on Chrome for Testing 158), so the
check fails and every page read on the tab, including the snapshot Harness used to learn the
tab's origin, is refused. Chrome also marks that error page loaded about 20 ms after the
challenge, and the extension deleted its challenge record on every completed load, so the prompt
was never reported on any computer (the open question in the 2026-10-17 HTTP auth live test).

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- A waiting prompt is reported while Chrome shows it, confirmed against the tab's live frames,
  and forgotten once a new top-level navigation starts or the tab closes.
- Saved-login requests and `fill_http_auth` resolve the origin of a waiting prompt from Chrome's
  request record when the page cannot be read; page reads stay refused exactly as before; a tab
  under protection and a prompt for another site are still refused.
- Live: the checks in the linked live-test document pass on `windows-pc`.
- Fix record: [2026-11-21-http-auth-prompt-on-protected-computer_plan_completed.md](2026-11-21-http-auth-prompt-on-protected-computer_plan_completed.md).

## LT-1200

### LT-1200 — Every shell command fails in a hardened, non-YOLO Codex session

**Status: reproduced live 21 November 2026 in the installed app; not fixed.**

### Observed behaviour

21 November 2026, 23:12:58Z: a root session in the installed app started a child with
`spawn_child` `provider:"codex"`, `hardened:true`. `app.log` shows `Spawning CLI under Seatbelt
hardened mode` and `Codex adapter using exec mode (hardened mode requires subprocess isolation)`.
Asked to run `rtk proxy node -e 'setTimeout(() => console.log("Progress check complete"), 5000)'`,
Codex got exit code 71 and `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`, twice, and
reported that it could not run any command.

### Root cause

A non-YOLO Codex session is created with `sandboxMode: 'read-only'`
(`src/main/cli/adapters/adapter-factory.ts`, `createCodexAdapter`), and the exec adapter passes it
as `--sandbox read-only` (`src/main/cli/adapters/codex-exec-adapter.ts`, `buildArgs` and
`resolveExecSandboxMode`). Codex then starts each shell command under its own `sandbox-exec`.
Hardened mode already runs Codex inside Harness's Seatbelt jail, and macOS refuses a sandbox
inside a sandbox (the same refusal recorded for queue workers on 11 and 19 November). YOLO
sessions pass `danger-full-access`, so Codex applies no sandbox of its own and is not affected.

### Required behaviour and acceptance

- A hardened Codex session that is not in YOLO mode can run shell commands, and still cannot
  write to the working directory or reach the network, which is what `read-only` promises today.
  Simply passing `danger-full-access` would let it write anywhere the jail allows, including the
  working directory, so that alone does not meet this.
- Acceptance: both checks in the Codex exec progress live test pass in a hardened Codex session
  started with `spawn_child hardened:true` from a root session in the rebuilt app, and a
  `touch` in the working directory from that session is refused.
